NORWICH, CT – Yesterday, Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee, Mark Rayha, President of General Dynamics-Electric Boat, Peter Baker, President of the Metal Trades Council of New London County, AFL-CIO, and Chris Jewell, President of Collins & Jewell and Chairman of the Eastern Connecticut Workforce Investment Board’s Board of Directors, joined Jill Rusk, Mayor of the City of Groton, and a large crowd of state and local officials, educators, and leaders in Connecticut’s submarine industrial base to discuss the newly announced $76.6 billion construction contract awards to Electric Boat for nine Block VI Virginia-class submarines and five Build II Columbia-class submarines.

Congress authorized the Virginia-class Block VI contract in 2023 in the FY24 NDAA and the Columbia-class Build II contract in 2025 in the FY26 NDAA. The legislative language in both bills originated in the Seapower subcommittee’s marks.

Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee

“This is not a normal or incremental contract award announcement that’s coming out of the Pentagon or the Navy. The record size and ‘buying in bulk’ structure of this contract provides the much needed long-horizon demand signal for the submarine industry. This legally enforceable binding contract raises the level of the federal government’s commitment to the Virginia and Columbia programs, and gives shipyards, supply chain companies, and labor contract negotiators the confidence they need to ensure all the pieces come together to ramp up production,” said Rep. Courtney. “At the end of the day, this is about people. If you go back to when Block V was negotiated in 2019, the size of the workforce at Electric Boat was 17,000. Today, in 2026, it’s over 27,000, and if you look at the submarine tonnage output projections, we can’t stop there. It’s going to take a state, region, and nationwide effort by industry and educators to continue the revitalization of our submarine workforce. Everyone’s presence here today with their excitement, passion, and confidence shows that we’re all going to work together as a state to successfully execute these contract awards.”

Mark Rayha, President of General Dynamics-Electric Boat

“These contracts reflect the trust that Electric Boat has earned from the Trump administration, the Congress and the Navy,” said Mark Rayha. “They create stability, opportunity and further solidify the future for EB while providing economic security for thousands of households across Connecticut and Rhode Island. And they allow us to continue playing the critical role we’ve played for generations and take great pride in—delivering freedom.”

Peter Baker, President of the Metal Trades Council of New London County, AFL-CIO

“These really are exciting times at Electric Boat and shipbuilding. Not only is there record growth in ship construction, hiring and training, there are jobs for the building and construction trades to upgrade the shipyard infrastructure. Millions of dollars will be pumped into the local economy, but this does not negate the need for affordable housing, day care, elder care, and public transportation,” said Peter Baker. “Additionally, the hundreds of manufacturers and thousands of employees nationally who produce parts for these ships will be able to stabilize and grow. Most importantly, we will be able to provide to the Navy and to the navies of our allies, the most sophisticated deterrent and defenses needed to protect our nations. The work will not be easy, but it is achievable if we continue to work in partnership. Much of this would not have been possible without the work of Congressman Courtney and his staff, and we owe him a debt of gratitude.”

Chris Jewell, President of Collins & Jewell and Chairman of the Eastern Connecticut Workforce Investment Board’s Board of Directors

“One of the challenges that a lot of suppliers have in the submarine supply chain is the ebbs and flows of work, so we are really confident that these contract awards will help level out those hills and valleys and give us a really good demand signal,” said Chris Jewell. “A lot of businesses are on the cusp of expansion, Collins & Jewell being one of them. Not only does this give me a lot of confidence to move forward with that expansion, but I’m also sure it will give my bankers a lot of confidence as well. The supply chain in eastern Connecticut is really strong. We all work together with one voice to grow our workforce and get people that will hit the floor running right out of the gate better. That’s what the Eastern Connecticut Workforce Investment Board does through the training programs that they offer. I really do think that these contract awards are going to move the needle for the region, and I encourage everyone to stay focused on the objective moving forward: giving the U.S. Navy the best submarines in the world.”

To read Congressman Courtney’s full statement on the Navy’s official execution of the Block VI Virginia-class and Build II Columbia-class construction contract awards, click here.

###
title: Courtney, Electric Boat, Local Officials, & Submarine Industry Leaders Celebrate Block VI Virginia-class & Build II Columbia-class Construction Contract Awards

Rep. Panetta’s Combating Illicit Xylazine Act Unanimously Passes Out of House Energy and Commerce Committee
Washington, D.C. – The bipartisan, bicameral Combating Illicit Xylazine Act, introduced by U.S. Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), was unanimously voted out of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce. This bill would list xylazine as a Schedule III controlled substance while protecting the drug’s legal use by veterinarians, farmers, and ranchers.
Reps. August Pfluger (TX-11), Chris Pappas (NH-01), Gus Bilirakis (FL-12), Scott Fitzgerald (WI-05), and Deborah Ross (NC-02) co-lead this effort in the House of Representatives. Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV) and Chuck Grassley (R-IA) have reintroduced companion legislation in the Senate. The Combating Illicit Xylazine Act previously passed the House with overwhelming bipartisan support.
Xylazine, also known as “tranq,” is an easily accessible veterinary tranquilizer that is being used as a low-cost cutting agent for fentanyl. The bipartisan legislation would schedule this dangerous drug and give law enforcement the tools they need to go after traffickers while protecting access for veterinarians, farmers, and ranchers who use xylazine to treat large animals. The bill is endorsed by 41 state attorneys general, major law enforcement organizations, and veterinary organizations.
“Illicit xylazine is worsening the deadly fentanyl crisis and tearing through communities across our country,” said Rep. Panetta. “The bipartisan Combating Illicit Xylazine Act will help us fight back and keep our communities safe by giving law enforcement the tools needed to crack down on traffickers while ensuring that veterinarians, farmers, and ranchers can continue to use the drug safely and responsibly. The overwhelming passage of this bill in the House Energy and Commerce Committee demonstrates the bipartisan consensus around stopping the illicit spread of this dangerous drug. I look forward to working with both my Democratic and Republican colleagues to get this bill across the finish line and save lives.”
“The xylazine crisis is only getting worse, and communities across America are paying the price,” said Rep. Pfluger. “That’s why I am proud to see the Combating Illicit Xylazine Act advance through the House Committee on Energy and Commerce today. Xylazine was never meant for human use, yet traffickers are increasingly mixing it into street drugs to make them more potent and more deadly. This bill takes direct aim at traffickers exploiting this drug for illicit purposes, while preserving its legal use by veterinarians and agricultural producers. I will continue working with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle until this critical legislation is signed into law.”
“Our goal is to save lives and ensure law enforcement has the tools they need to hold accountable those who are illegally manufacturing and distributing these deadly substances that are devastating communities across the country,” said Rep. Bilirakis. “I’m proud that this bipartisan legislation has advanced out of the Energy and Commerce Committee, bringing us one step closer to addressing this growing threat. At the same time, we must ensure veterinarians who rely on xylazine for legitimate medical purposes can continue to access and use it appropriately. Our legislation strikes the right balance by protecting public health while preserving critical veterinary care.”
“This legislation would help law enforcement crack down on illegal drug traffickers by tracking the manufacture of xylazine, a legal animal tranquilizer, which is being mixed with fentanyl, heroin, and other deadly drugs. It’s now passed out of committee and should be swiftly brought to the floor for a vote,” said Rep. Pappas. “As we work to combat the ongoing addiction epidemic, we must ensure our law enforcement has the resources they need to stop drug trafficking.”
“Xylazine, a powerful animal sedative, is increasingly being cut into illicit drugs like fentanyl, boosting the profits of criminal cartels and drug traffickers while fueling the overdose crisis in the United States,” said Rep. Fitzgerald. “I’m pleased the House Committee on Energy and Commerce advanced the Combating Illicit Xylazine Act. This bill will enhance law enforcement’s ability to track xylazine distribution and impose criminal penalties on those who misuse it, while ensuring its availability for necessary veterinary use. I thank my colleagues for their support and look forward to its passage by the full House.”
“Fentanyl overdoses continue to take far too many lives and devastate our communities, in no small part due to the widespread availability of deadly substances like xylazine,” said Rep. Ross. “This bill will save lives by restricting access to this dangerous substance and giving law enforcement the tools they need to crack down on traffickers, while protecting legitimate uses of xylazine by veterinarians, farmers, and ranchers. I am grateful for the bipartisan commitment to addressing this issue and look forward to hopefully passing this legislation with the full support of Congress.”
The Combating Illicit Xylazine Act would:
- Schedule xylazine as a Schedule III illicit substance under the Controlled Substances Act;
- Ensure veterinarians, farmers, and ranchers can still use the drug for its intended purpose by creating a clear definition of “ultimate user” — someone lawfully permitted to possess a controlled substance for legitimate use;
- Enable the DEA to track its manufacturing to ensure it is not diverted to the illicit market; and
- Require a report on prevalence, risks, and recommendations regarding xylazine.
In December 2024, Rep. Panetta led a bipartisan coalition of 42 members calling for urgent Congressional action on his bipartisan Combating Illicit Xylazine Act. The letter to Speaker of the House Mike Johnson and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries emphasized the growing threat posed by xylazine-adulterated fentanyl to communities across the country, and the need for proactive action to save lives.
Earlier this year, Panetta authored and led a letter to the Trump Administration strongly opposing its decision by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration to end funding for illicit drug test strips. In his letter to Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., Panetta and his colleagues emphasized that test strips are bipartisan, science-based tools that are critical to avoiding preventable deaths amid the rise of synthetic opioids and emerging adulterants like xylazine.
title: Rep. Panetta’s Combating Illicit Xylazine Act Unanimously Passes Out of House Energy and Commerce Committee

AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a former paratrooper and Army Ranger who serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and House Armed Services Committee, along with 14 other Democratic veteran Members of Congress, are demanding the Trump administration release accurate information regarding all troop deaths and injuries during his reckless war with Iran.

"As veterans of America's wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers," wrote the lawmakers.

"The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the war with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports," they continued. "We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers."

After public reporting uncovered that the Pentagon lowered the number of troop deaths during the war with Iran from 18 to 14, the Department of Defense quietly restored the names. The Administration has provided conflicting explanations as to why the servicemembers names were removed to begin with. The reporting also detailed that DoD has misled the public about the number of troops injured and wounded during the war.

Joining Congressman Crow are Representatives Mike Thompson (D-CA), Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA), Chris Deluzio (D-PA), Gil Cisneros (D-CA), Derek Tran (D-CA), Salud Carbajal (D-CA), Jimmy Panetta (D-CA), Ted Lieu (D-CA), Seth Moulton (D-MA), Jared Golden (D-ME), Pat Ryan (D-NY), Maggie Goodlander (D-NH), Bobby Scott (D-VA), and Eugene Vindman (D-VA).

Crow has repeatedly condemned Trump’s illegal war of choice in Iran, and helped lead a war powers resolution that passed the House last week. As an Army Ranger who grew up in a working-class family and served in Iraq and Afghanistan, Crow saw firsthand the repercussions of forever wars on servicemembers and hard-working Americans. He has demanded answers on how this administration is protecting troops in the region, and on recent civilian deaths, including a U.S. strike on an Iranian girls’ elementary school where at least 175 civilians, many of them children, were killed.

A PDF of the letter can be found here.
title: Crow, Democratic Veterans Demand Transparency on Troop Casualties

Lincoln, RI – TODAY, Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) hosted a panel featuring anti-scam experts to educate older Rhode Islanders on how to avoid scams and keep their hard-earned money from being stolen by bad actors. The experts shared ways to protect yourself and your loved ones from fraudsters, and Congressman Amo shared what he’s doing in Congress to stop the proliferation of scams.

“A key part of making life more affordable is ensuring that as much of your money as possible stays in your pocket,” said Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI). “With costs on the rise because of Trump’s illegal war with Iran and erratic tariffs, scammers are worsening financial strain by taking advantage and targeting well-meaning Rhode Islanders already affected by Republicans’ affordability crisis. By bringing together law enforcement, elder justice advocates, and financial experts, we were able to provide critical resources to older Rhode Islanders about how to avoid scams. As a founding co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Stop Scams Caucus, I will keep fighting to stop the scam scourge and pass commonsense legislation like my STOP Scams Against Seniors Act and my National Strategy to Combat Scams Act to make sure that Rhode Islanders ' hard-earned money stays right where it belongs.”

Background

Congressman Amo is a founding co-chair of the Congressional Stop Scams Caucus, a bipartisan group of Members of Congress dedicated to protecting Americans from scams.

Amo introduced the bipartisan, bicameral Strengthening Task Forces to Oppose Predatory (STOP) Scams Against Seniors Act, which would authorize the creation of Elder Justice Task Forces to help local, state, and Federal agencies work together to investigate and prosecute illegal scammers. The bill is co-led by Congressman Jeffersen Shreve (R-IN) in the House and led by Senator Ashley Moody (R-FL) in the Senate.

Amo also introduced the bipartisan, bicameral National Strategy for Combating Scams Act, which would establish a federal working group led by the Federal Bureau of Investigation to coordinate the efforts of more than a dozen federal agencies in combating scams. The bill is co-led by Congressman Derek Schmidt (R-KS) in the U.S. House. Companion legislation was introduced in the U.S. Senate by Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Rick Scott (R-FL), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), and Ashley Moody (R-FL).

###
title: Amo & Experts Help Seniors Avoid Scams in Kickoff to Fighting for an Affordable America Stops

COVENTRY, R.I. – Today, U.S. Senators Jack Reed (D-RI) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), along with U.S. Representative Seth Magaziner (RI-02), joined seniors and Neighborhood Health CEO Peter Marino at the Coventry Resource and Senior Center to mark the 61st anniversary of Medicare and Medicaid, provide an update on health care policy in Washington, and reaffirm their commitment to lowering health care costs for Rhode Islanders.

The event comes as Rhode Islanders continue to face rising health care costs following deep cuts enacted by President Trump and Congressional Republicans, including a nearly $1 trillion cut to Medicaid and the expiration of enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits that helped make coverage more affordable.

View or download photos from the event here.

“Medicare and Medicaid are cost-effective and critical to the health and well-being of thousands of Rhode Islanders and millions of Americans. These programs have helped lift millions of Americans out of poverty, improved their health, and advanced health care innovations that benefit everyone. The historic success of Medicare is self-evident: Before Medicare was enacted, roughly half of all seniors had health insurance. Today, 99 percent of American seniors -- adults aged 65 and older -- have health insurance,” said Senator Reed. “Working together, we can keep the promise of Medicare and Medicaid and ensure these programs are there for older Americans today, tomorrow, and for another sixty-one years. Supporting Medicare and Medicaid provides quality health care to more Americans, slows rising health care costs, and helps reduce federal budget deficit.”

“For 61 years, Medicare and Medicaid have helped Rhode Islanders access affordable, lifesaving health care,” said Senator Whitehouse. “Republican chaos and corruption are driving up Americans’ costs, and the party’s bizarre obsession with ripping away health care has destabilized our already-fragile health care system. It’s a disgrace, and I remain committed to protecting Medicare and Medicaid from Republican mischief.”

“Medicare and Medicaid have helped provide health care to Rhode Islanders for 61 years,” said Magaziner. “But health care has become increasingly unaffordable and inaccessible because of direct attacks by the President and Congressional Republicans. We must do better. I, along with the entire delegation, will continue fighting for a health care system that is affordable for all Americans.”

“Medicare and Medicaid make a tremendous difference, especially because both programs help people manage chronic conditions like high blood pressure or diabetes, and continue living full lives,” said Peter Marino, President and CEO of Neighborhood Health Plan. “These programs make it more likely that someone will see a doctor when something feels wrong instead of waiting until a health issue becomes an emergency. For people without coverage, the choice too often becomes whether to seek care or pay for other basic needs. No one should have to make that choice. That’s why we need to continue investing in these vital programs – it is how we make sure we are taking care of each other.”

The event commemorated the signing of Medicare and Medicaid into law by President Lyndon B. Johnson 61 years ago while highlighting the challenges Rhode Islanders face today as health care becomes increasingly expensive and inaccessible.

During the event, the Delegation members outlined how recent federal health care cuts are affecting Rhode Islanders and the broader health care system. They also reaffirmed their commitment to protecting Medicare and Medicaid, reversing harmful cuts, and lowering health care costs for working people across the state.

For 61 years, Medicare and Medicaid have helped millions of Americans access quality, affordable health care. Today, more than 309,000 Rhode Islanders rely on Medicaid, including 64 percent of nursing home residents, more than half of adults with disabilities, 37 percent of children, and 43 percent of births in the state. An estimated 34,000 Rhode Islanders are expected to lose health insurance once Medicaid cuts passed by Republicans are in full effect. Another 244,570 Rhode Islanders, nearly one in five residents, depend on Medicare for their health coverage and have seen their health insurance rates skyrocket. Members of the Rhode Island delegation outline how recent Republican cuts to Medicaid and the expiration of enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits threaten to increase health care costs and put additional strain on the state's health care system. They reiterated their commitment to protecting Medicare, restoring affordable health coverage, and ensuring every Rhode Islander can access the care they need.
title: RI Delegation Joins Seniors on Anniversary of Medicare and Medicaid, Discuss their Fight to Lower Health Care Costs

Washington, D.C. — Congressman Dave Min (CA-47), joined by Representatives Michael Lawler (NY-17), Jared Huffman (CA-02), and Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), sent a letter urging the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) to develop comprehensive federal safety standards for electric bicycles and higher-speed “e-motos”.

The bipartisan letter comes in response to the CPSC’s Notice of Proposed Rulemaking to establish safety standards for lithium-ion batteries used for e-bikes and other forms of micromobility transit. While the lawmakers acknowledged the importance of addressing the serious fire risks posed by low-quality batteries, they keyed in on the CPSC’s failure to address the broader risks posed by unregulated e-bikes and e-motos.

“While we strongly support the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission taking action to address fire hazards posed by counterfeit and low-quality lithium-ion batteries associated with these products, battery integrity is only one component of a broader set of challenges facing consumers and communities,” said the Members. “We urge the Commission to build on this effort by developing separate, comprehensive safety standards for e-bikes and electric motorcycles.”

“Fire-safe batteries matter, but they will not stop companies from marketing devices capable of motorcycle-level speeds to children as ordinary e-bikes,” said Rep. Min. “Parents should not have to become product safety experts just to know what they are buying for their kids. The CPSC must close these loopholes, require clear product labeling, and establish modern standards that distinguish e-bikes from high-powered e-motos.”

The reforms outlined in the letter reflect key provisions of Congressman Min’s Safe Standards for Personal E-Bike and E-Moto Device Specifications Act, Safe SPEEDS Act, which would establish a comprehensive federal safety framework for electric micromobility products.

Between 2019 and 2022, as e-bike sales in the United States nearly quadrupled, injuries involving e-bikes and e-motos increased by nearly tenfold, according to estimates from the CPSC’s National Electronic Injury Surveillance System. Children and teenagers face particularly serious risks. Health care providers at Rady Children’s Health treated one pediatric e-bike crash patient in 2021 and more than 220 in 2025.

The letter also highlights fatal crashes involving young riders and community members, including the death of 20-year-old Huntington Beach resident Kolby Aipa after an e-bike collision.

The lawmakers urged the CPSC to:

Establish minimum labeling requirements clearly disclosing each device’s maximum speed, motor power, recommended minimum age and intended on-road or off-road use.

Modernize the federal definition of an e-bike and create consistent classifications that clearly distinguish conventional e-bikes from higher-powered e-motos.

Support local crash-data collection and public education by helping law enforcement agencies, emergency responders and local governments accurately identify devices and document injuries and fatalities.

The full letter is available here.

The letter is the latest step in Rep. Min’s continued efforts to improve e-bike safety and close gaps in federal oversight. Earlier this week, Rep. Min joined Irvine Councilmember Betty Martinez Franco’s office for an I-Ride Safe Academy panel focused on helping young riders and their families better understand e-bike risks and practice safe, responsible riding.

###
title: Reps. Min, Lawler, Huffman and Fitzpatrick Call for Stronger Federal E-Bike and E-Moto Safety Standards

WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Congresswoman Summer Lee (PA-12), Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17), and Congresswoman Madeleine Dean (PA-04) sent a letter to Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Office of Refugee Resettlement Acting Director Angie Salazar demanding answers about ORR's decision to place unaccompanied migrant children at Abraxas Academy in Morgantown, Pennsylvania, despite the facility's documented history of child abuse violations.

The lawmakers raise serious concerns about ORR's decision to award Abraxas Alliance a $9.2 million contract in August 2025 despite Pennsylvania officials documenting repeated deficiencies and revoking one of the facility's licenses. They also urge HHS to immediately review all ORR-contracted facilities, suspend the Abraxas Academy contract pending a full investigation, and provide Congress with a complete accounting of how the placement decision was made.

"It is appalling that ORR nevertheless decided to house unaccompanied minors in a facility with such a record, thereby potentially exposing these children to the possibility of abuse and in violation of federal rules," the Members wrote.

The letter details a decades-long pattern of documented problems at the facility, including repeated state findings of physical mistreatment of minors, allegations of sexual harassment and abuse by staff, and a pattern of institutional failures. Although federal law requires ORR to place children in "the least restrictive setting that is in the best interests of the child," reports indicate children are being housed in locked cells.

The Members also cite concerns stemming from a July 8 congressional oversight visit, during which facility staff were reportedly unable to answer basic questions about allegations of abuse or explain legally required procedures for children who turn 18 while in ORR custody. As the Members wrote, "This utter lack of knowledge of the basic, legally required functions of this facility raises serious concerns about the safety of the children living inside."

The letter requests responses by August 14, 2026, including:

Who approved the decision to place children at Abraxas Academy and what child welfare assessments were conducted.

Why ORR proceeded with the contract despite Pennsylvania's documented findings of abuse and licensing violations.

Whether HHS has reviewed other ORR-contracted facilities for compliance with state and federal child welfare standards.

Why some children with parents or close relatives in the United States were reportedly placed in ORR custody rather than reunited with family.

What safeguards exist to protect children from abuse and how staff are trained.

The financial and operational relationship between Abraxas Alliance and GEO Group.

"The federal government bears a solemn responsibility to ensure the proper treatment and protection of every child in its care," the Members wrote. "Allowing any child to be placed in an environment with a history of abuse is cruel and undermines the moral leadership of the United States."
title: Krishnamoorthi, Colleagues Press HHS on Placement of Migrant Children at Facility with Documented History of Abuse

“Hometown Heroes” Honors Local Veterans, Life-saving First Responders, Community Leaders

Above: Gottheimer honoring Fifth District residents as “Hometown Heroes.”

HACKENSACK, NJ — Today, July 31, 2026, U.S. Congressman Gottheimer (NJ-5) honored local life-saving first responders, veterans, volunteers, community leaders, and residents during his Fifth District Hometown Heroes Ceremony at the Hackensack Performing Arts Center.

Watch Gottheimer’s July, 2026 Hometown Heroes Ceremony here.

Gottheimer honored North Jersey residents as Fifth District Hometown Heroes to acknowledge their dedication to improving the lives of their neighbors, families, and communities.

“Today, we are here to focus on our neighbors, who, even in all the noise, look for ways to put others above themselves,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “Each day, our friends, family, and neighbors quietly go out and change lives through their service to others. They do it all without expecting any special recognition. They do it simply because it’s the right thing to do. They all come from different walks of life, but they all embody our Jersey Values and make our community such a special place to live, work, and raise a family. They help us build that more perfect union of our dreams. We all should work to live up to their example.”

Read about this year’s Hometown Heroes below:

Samuel Kim, Englewood Cliffs — At just seventeen, Samuel has already founded two nonprofits serving local seniors: Aim for Unity, which offers free archery workshops for brain health and has served more than six hundred seniors, and the Senior Shield Project, a fraud-prevention and digital literacy program that has reached more than 150 people. A DECA regional champion and Regeneron science fair winner, he lives with his grandparents, whose care drives his work.

Tom Colwell, Closter — Since 2023, Tom has served as Co-Chair of the Closter Food Pantry, turning a small effort into one of the most efficient operations around. He personally orders, picks up, and delivers food every month, builds the spreadsheets, tracks the finances, and secured grants for its equipment — all while holding a full-time job and volunteering alongside his wife and three kids.

Andrew Dunn, Hillsdale — Andrew has been a Hillsdale resident for fifty-three years, and has devoted his life to Habitat for Humanity. Andy is a U.S. Army veteran and honored English teacher — has served as a Habitat for Humanity construction crew leader for more than three decades, including a dozen trips for post-Katrina rebuilding.

Joan Bohan & Mike Schulman, Northvale — Joan, Northvale’s school nurse for fifteen years, and Mike, its athletic director and a physical education teacher for eighteen and 2025–2026 Bergen County Teacher of the Year, didn’t hesitate when a middle school player collapsed in cardiac arrest this February. Using the district’s AED and CPR training, they brought the student back. Thanks to them, Angelo is alive today.

Jim & Meredith Drobinske, Dumont — Dumont residents for thirty-nine years and married for forty-five, Jim and Meredith are retired Teachers of the Year who now serve as pantry managers for the Food Brigade, logging 1,804 volunteer hours in two years and helping feed 150 families a week. Jim — a fifty-two-year member of the Woodcliff Lake Fire Department — is a two-time Hometown Hero, first honored in 2018 for a CPR save on a golf course.

Officer Frank Stefano, Oradell — Off duty at a Hackensack hockey rink, Oradell Officer Frank Stefano performed CPR and delivered two defibrillator shocks to revive a goalie in full cardiac arrest — who has since fully recovered. It’s far from his first save: Frank has twice been honored by Pascack Valley PBA Local 206, including for using Narcan to revive an unconscious individual.

Paul Coller, Ramsey — A Ramsey resident for forty-one years and U.S. Army Reserve veteran, Paul volunteers twice a week with CHORE, part of Bergen Volunteers, performing home repairs that keep seniors and disabled residents safe at home. He has served there more than a decade, including as Board President. As Bergen Volunteers’ director Shara Nadler puts it, “Paul is a community champion who strengthens Bergen County every day.”

Chief Robert Schlossberg, River Edge — River Edge Fire Chief Robert Schlossberg just completed a career that includes delivering a baby, three CPR saves, and several Unit Citations for courage — and this year was named 2025 New Jersey Fire Chief of the Year. He and his wife Joellen raised a true service family, with three children serving in fire, police, and EMS. His focus as Chief was always training, the best way to keep every member safe.

Michele Weber, Waldwick — A lifelong Waldwick resident and cancer survivor, Michele chairs Access for All, raising awareness of what people with disabilities face and offering guidance on ADA compliance and local resources. She also volunteers every Sunday in her church’s Kids’ Ministry. As Mayor Giordano says, “Michele embodies the spirit of community, service, and dedication that defines a true hometown hero.”

Michael McNamara, Branchville — For nearly four decades, Mike has volunteered with Project Self-Sufficiency — known there as “the guy who always says yes,” he once drove to Maryland for a truckload of donated books. When pulmonary fibrosis slowed him, he kept showing up on oxygen, and after a 2023 lung transplant returned with a spring in his step. He’s also hiked the beginning and end of the Appalachian Trail — just not the middle.

Nick Vanhorn, Sussex — Every day, Nick keeps Sussex kids safe as the town’s crossing guard — but his role goes further: free weather and news updates on Facebook, an Easter Bunny costume for town festivities, and a different costume every day during Halloween week. As Sussex Borough Councilman Ross says, “Nick’s presence and contributions are heavily cherished, and he is a staple to the community of Sussex.”

Keri Marino, Franklin — Keri is the first woman to serve as President of the 200 Club of Sussex County and sits on a remarkable range of civic boards. A domestic violence survivor, she has spent years as a trustee of DASI and teaches free trauma-informed yoga to survivors, and she once testified in Washington on renewing VAWA. She has received a Citation from the New Jersey State Legislature and DASI’s Full Circle Award.

Linda Schaefer, Ringwood — A Ringwood resident for thirty-eight years, Linda served with the Ringwood Ambulance Auxiliary — twenty-five as President — funding equipment and free ambulance service for residents. She also spent twenty-six years as the elementary school secretary and served on numerous town boards. As Ringwood Deputy Mayor Kerr says, she is “a selfless person who has devoted her entire life to working and volunteering in Ringwood.”

Gary Oppenheimer, West Milford — In 2009, Gary founded AmpleHarvest.org, which connects home gardeners’ surplus harvests with nearby food pantries. Seventeen years later it links more than 8,500 pantries across all fifty states to 62 million gardeners — run by a staff of just four. A CNN Hero and two-time TEDx speaker, Gary fights food waste and hunger from right here in the Garden State.

Anthony Pulizzano, Upper Saddle River — An Upper Saddle River police officer and PBA president, Anthony has made Special Olympics New Jersey his cause, founding “Climb with a Cop” and coordinating the Law Enforcement Torch Run. He also founded the Rock Adventure Company for kids and once performed the Heimlich to save a choking woman, earning a lifesaving award from the Bergen County Chiefs Association.

Officers Alex Lospinuso & Jake Rotunda, Franklin — Responding to what seemed a routine call, Franklin Officers Alex Lospinuso and Jake Rotunda found a man with life-threatening injuries and applied a tourniquet and chest seal that saved his life. Alex has also been honored for a crash rescue and a mental health crisis response, while Jake, a lifelong wrestler, earned a MADD award for impaired-driving enforcement and now coaches youth wrestling.

John Herrmann, Englewood Fire Department — An Englewood firefighter and union president, John serves as Clinical Coordinator for the state Professional Firefighters’ Peer Support Team, guiding departments through line-of-duty deaths, suicides, and quiet struggles. Drawing on his own experience with anxiety, he has helped many colleagues through their hardest moments. As Chief Jeff Kaplan says, his peer counseling “sets him apart from everyone” — and he does it without compensation.

Razak Buddha, Teaneck — At ninety-three, Razak is the oldest volunteer at Holy Name Hospital, showing up every day at the Courtesy Desk with warmth and a readiness to help — more than 3,498 hours logged over the years. A retired physical therapist who grew up in India, he still visits elderly patients in their homes several times a week to provide care and companionship.

Laurie Epstein, Haworth — After her daughter’s food allergy diagnosis, Laurie became one of New Jersey’s leading advocates for allergy safety, even bringing her second grader to Washington to testify. She has led Girl Scouts in Haworth since 2005 and now runs the program for more than 130 girls. As Councilwoman Siciliano says, her support “has produced generations of future female leaders who believe in themselves.”

Helen Whalen (Posthumously), Westwood — Honored posthumously, Helen was a Westwood resident for more than seventy years who devoted her life to telling North Jersey’s story through the Pascack Historical Society and Westwood Heritage Society. Her history of Westwood was published this year, after her 2023 passing. Her award is received today by her daughter Kathleen, grandson Marc, and niece Tatiana.

Gottheimer was joined by Bergen County Clerk John Hogan, Commissioner Alan Henderson, Hackensack Mayor Caseen Gaines, Sussex Mayor Robert Holowach, Waldwick Mayor Thomas Giordano, Closter Mayor John Gliddon, Mayor Deirdre Dillon, Hillsdale Mayor Michael Sheinfeld, Westwood Mayor Ray Arroyo, Ringwood Mayor Jamie Landis, Westwood Council President Lauren Leitzia, Westwood Councilwoman Erin Collins, Councilman Paul Rubacky, Englewood Cliffs COuncilman Phillip Liang, Council President Thomas Kelly, Councilman David Bandfield, Closter Councilwoman Alissa Latner, Councilwoman Angela Smith, Fire Chief Jeff Kaplan, Police Chief David Gangemi, Police Chief Gregory Cugliari, Police COmmanding Captain Seamus Geddis, Waldwick Borough Clerk Kelly Halewicz, Englewood Cliffs Mayor Mark Park, Englewood Cliffs Councilwoman Rivka Bieggacz, River Edge Mayor Thomas Papaleo, Franklin Councilwoman Stephen Skellenger, Haworth Councilwoman Dina Siciliano.

Below: Gottheimer presents awards to local heroes and their families.

Chester, PA — Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05) this week conducted an unannounced Congressional oversight visit inside Moshannon Valley Processing Center, the largest ICE detention center in the Northeast. After a roughly 30 minute wait, Rep. Scanlon gained entry to the facility and was provided a tour of the Moshannon facility by ICE and GEO administrators for 3 hours. With one exception, she was not allowed to speak with detainees.

The visit occurred without prior notice to ICE after a March 2 court order blocked ICE actions to restrict access to detention facilities by Members of Congress and reaffirmed their legal right to conduct unannounced oversight visits to those facilities.

Moshannon Valley Processing Center is a former prison owned and operated by private prison contractor, GEO Group, and now used solely for immigration detention. While reports of poor conditions at Moshannon have circulated for years, they have dramatically increased since the start of the Trump Administration’s mass deportation efforts, including a hunger strike, reports of inadequate medical care and neglect, allegations of sexual assault, and two detainee deaths.

“The American people are entitled to know how their tax dollars are being spent. Given the billions of dollars in deficit spending that Congressional Republicans and the Trump White House are devoting to mass deportation, it is more important than ever that Congress conduct oversight of ICE and DHS operations to find out how those taxpayer dollars are being spent, and ensure that people being held in custody by the United States government are treated humanely,” said Rep. Scanlon. “Following numerous reports of unsafe living conditions, subpar medical care, and two deaths at this private prison facility, in which dozens of my community members and constituents have been detained against their will, it would be irresponsible not to inspect conditions at Moshannon firsthand. GEO charges us millions of dollars every month to detain people at Moshannon. Taxpayer dollars should be spent to improve the lives of Americans, not to inflict misery and make private prison contractors rich.”

Rep. Scanlon summarized her key takeaways as follows:

Administrators reported that the population at Moshannon during the visit was 1,634 — consistent with increased detention numbers across the country as ICE arrests have escalated in June and July 2026.

Officials at Moshannon indicated that 1,311 of the 1,634 individuals detained at the time of the visit were considered low-security. ICE’s FY2026 statistics confirm that the vast majority (8 out of 10) of people detained at Moshannon have no criminal record.

Only 46 (less than 3%) of detainees were women. This aligns with reports that ICE is targeting male breadwinners for detention in order to pressure self-deportation by entire family units (including children who are U.S. citizens).

The average stay at Moshannon was reported by administrators to be 34 days; current online statistics from ICE list a higher (46 days) average stay.

While ICE and GEO officials on site said that they did not know or could not disclose how much ICE pays GEO to operate the facility at Moshannon, public reporting indicates that GEO is receiving over $5.3 million per month, consisting of a monthly management fee of at least $3.4 million and an additional fee of $10 per person per day up to 800 detainees, and $40 per person per day for over 800 detainees. This fee structure provides a perverse incentive for private prisons to prolong detention. GEO Group representatives also confirmed that it charges the government additional fees for its expanding private transportation services.

If one prorates GEO’s monthly fees as reported for May 2025, before the most recent surge, it is costing taxpayers $43,741 per year to detain someone at Moshannon, which is about what it costs to send a student to Penn State University nearby for a year.

Moshannon Valley Processing Center is a former prison, and is run using prison practices. Detained individuals are required to wear color-coded prison garb and eat in their living quarters. There are severe constraints upon their liberty and their ability to contact family and anyone outside the facility.

By law, immigration detention is supposed to be a form of civil process, not criminal punishment, meaning the system is supposed to be used to manage flight or safety risks and ensure that people attend their court hearings. What detained individuals experience at Moshannon could not be described as anything other than punitive — at best.

Detainees must perform most of the labor at the facility where they are being involuntarily held, including cleaning showers, toilets, and living quarters, and supplying the majority of labor for food service and laundry. Only two full-time janitors service the entire facility, which has a capacity of more than 1,800 people. While GEO and ICE say that such labor is “voluntary,” an administrator acknowledged that these core functions could not be performed without detainee labor. By using detainee labor, rather than hiring employees or contractors at market rates, the private contractor increases its profits.

Many detainees avoid the institutional meals which administrators said are prepared to meet correctional facility caloric and nutrition standards. Due to poor food quality, detainees have initiated two hunger strike protests this year and rely upon food such as ramen noodles purchased from the facility’s commissary, using funds sent to them by friends or relatives. The Congresswoman saw such prepackaged food in the living quarters. She was provided with a lunch tray in the dining hall, which detainees cannot use, but was unable to compare it to what detainees were served.

While the facility denies using solitary confinement for punishment, its “Special Management Unit” currently has 29 detainees in single cells, separate from the general population. The physical setup of the unit, and admissions by management that some detainees were assigned there for infraction of facility rules, at least partially confirmed reports of abuse of solitary confinement standards. All cells were occupied by only one person. Some were on suicide watch. One had been held there for 220 days. Daily recreation for residents of that unit takes place in a cement block hall containing chain link cages in which “natural light and fresh air” is provided by 1’ x 3’ openings in the wall about 12 feet above floor level.

During her visit to Moshannon Valley Processing Center, Rep. Scanlon was able to speak with one of her constituents who had previously completed an ICE Privacy Waiver that authorizes the release of information to a third party, including a Congressional office. Moshannon administrators barred the Congresswoman from speaking with other detainees, which made it difficult to assess their actual treatment and conditions.

The July 29 visit follows an August 2025 visit to Moshannon, when Rep. Scanlon was denied entry under orders of former Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem, and her January 2026 oversight visit to Philadelphia Federal Detention Center, which serves as a temporary holding facility for individuals detained in the area before they are transferred to Moshannon or elsewhere.

Rep. Scanlon, who is a member of the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration, has previously visited a detention center and migrant shelter in Texas, ports of entry on both the northern and southern borders, and a family detention center in Berks County, PA, which has since been closed.

###
title: Congresswoman Scanlon Conducts Unannounced Oversight Visit to Moshannon Valley Processing Center, Largest ICE Detention Center in Northeast

As El Paso families continue to face rising utility bills and extreme temperatures, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) is renewing her call for Congress to advance a package of legislation that would strengthen utility oversight, expand energy assistance, and lower costs by accelerating access to affordable, reliable clean energy.

Congresswoman Escobar supports three bills aimed at addressing the energy affordability crisis from multiple angles: the Lowering Utility Bills Act, led by Congressman Greg Casar (TX-35); the Heating and Cooling Relief Act, led by Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03); and the Energy Bills Relief Act, led by Congressmen Mike Levin (CA-49) and Sean Casten (IL-06).

“Families should not have to choose between keeping the lights on, cooling their homes during dangerous heat, and paying for other basic necessities,” said Congresswoman Escobar. “At a time when utility bills are rising, Congress should be focused on delivering meaningful relief—not protecting excessive utility profits or making it harder and more expensive to build the affordable energy our communities need. This legislative package would increase accountability, expand assistance for families struggling with energy costs, and invest in the reliable, low-cost renewable energy that can help bring bills down over the long term.”

The Lowering Utility Bills Act would establish stronger federal and state standards governing how electric transmission providers and investor-owned utilities calculate their authorized rates of return. By increasing oversight and accountability in the rate-setting process, the legislation seeks to ensure that consumers are not forced to pay unnecessarily high utility bills to support excessive returns for utility companies.

The Heating and Cooling Relief Act would expand and modernize the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP), helping more low-income households afford heating and cooling costs. The legislation would better account for the growing risks and financial burdens associated with extreme weather—an especially urgent need in communities like El Paso, where prolonged and dangerous heat can make access to affordable cooling a matter of public health and safety.

The Energy Bills Relief Act would prioritize working families by driving down energy costs as President Trump’s war of choice with Iran causes global energy market volatility. Specifically, the legislation would reinstate the 2022 clean energy tax credits for home and system-wide energy improvements that were eliminated by President Trump and congressional Republicans, helping families reduce their energy use and lower their utility bills. It would also incentivize utility companies to improve the efficiency of their energy systems, reward cost-saving investments, provide financial assistance to help prevent families from having their power shut off, and crack down on price gouging by energy companies. The bill would ensure that large energy users—including data centers—pay their fair share of the costs associated with the energy they consume rather than shifting those expenses onto local households. It would also strengthen opportunities for communities to have a voice in energy projects and share in the benefits those projects bring.

These efforts come as the Trump administration and congressional Republicans have worked to dismantle clean energy tax credits and slow the deployment of renewable energy. The Republican-backed One Big Beautiful Bill Act accelerated the phaseout of key clean energy incentives, including credits that helped families invest in energy-efficient home improvements and residential clean energy. The Trump administration has also stalled the permitting process for several renewable energy projects, including offshore wind projects in Texas, creating uncertainty for projects that could help expand affordable electricity generation and reduce costs for consumers.

# # #
title: Amid Soaring Utility Bills, Congresswoman Escobar Renews Call for Legislative Package to Lower Energy Costs

PITTSBURGH, PA – JULY 31, 2026 — Yesterday, Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) joined members of the Congressional Black Caucus, Black mayors, and public safety advocates for a virtual roundtable highlighting the community-driven strategies helping cities across the country reduce violence and make families safer.

Hosted by the Vera Institute of Justice, the conversation featured Congresswoman Lee (PA-12), Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11), Baltimore Mayor Brandon M. Scott, Newark Mayor Ras J. Baraka, and Durham Mayor Leonardo “Leo” Williams. Vera Institute President Insha Rahman moderated the discussion.

Participants discussed how investments in housing, education, healthcare, economic opportunity, violence prevention, trauma recovery, and other community resources are helping drive crime rates down across the country. They also warned against the Trump administration’s efforts to cut effective public safety programs while returning to failed policies that criminalize Black communities and use fear to justify federal overreach.

“Communities in Western Pennsylvania and across the country are seeing declines in crime because leaders are investing in the resources that help people thrive--safe housing, good schools, accessible healthcare, living-wage jobs, and community-led violence prevention,” said Congresswoman Lee. “Instead of doubling down on failed policies that criminalize our communities, we should be scaling the solutions that make families safer and stronger. I'm proud to stand with the Congressional Black Caucus, local leaders, and advocates who are advancing a vision of public safety rooted in dignity, opportunity, and justice.”

“While Trump focuses on “tough on crime” fear-mongering and counter-productive gimmicks like deploying the National Guard, Black Mayors across the country are doing the real work to make cities safer. I’m proud to stand with my colleagues in the Congressional Black Caucus to set the record straight and advocate for real public safety solutions,” said Congresswoman Shontel Brown.

“In Baltimore, we know how to solve the issue of public safety,” said Baltimore Mayor Brandon M. Scott. “It's about investing in public health, it's about getting rid of vacant houses and providing opportunities. It's about being focused on the very small percent who are responsible for the overwhelming amount of violence in our communities—going after guns and getting them off our streets. We are currently seeing a historic reduction in violence and homicides, and we want to push it even further. You don't do that without the support of the community.”

“Our approach in Newark is to treat crime and violence as a public health issue,” said Newark Mayor Ras J. Baraka. “And what we see now in our city — with a homicide rate that hasn’t been this low since Eisenhower was president — is the result of us focusing on the kind of things that have been absent from our neighborhoods: investing in housing, investing in our young people, literacy, education, recreation and opportunity. When you start to add that, and at the same time address some of the symptomatic issues and build a community-based public safety ecosystem centered on violence prevention and trauma recovery, you’ll see that violence and crime gets reduce gradually. It’s all about putting the 'public' back into 'public safety.'"

“Crime rates continue to fall across the country to historic levels thanks to bold, community-first approaches to public safety like the ones discussed today. While the Trump administration continues its assault on immigrants and cities, while simultaneously gutting programs that we know increase safety, local and federal leaders—specifically Black leaders like Rep. Summer Lee, Rep. Shontel Brown, and Mayors Scott, Baraka and Williams are charting a path forward for all to follow. Their serious approach to safety is a model for how we can prevent crime before it happens and continue to help communities thrive,” said Vera President Insha Rahman.

Congresswoman Lee is the founder and co-chair of theCongressional Community Safety Caucus, where she works to advance proven, community-led solutions that prevent violence and address its root causes. She has fought toprotect federal funding for community violence intervention programs and expand access to trauma-informed services. Through legislation including thePeople’s Response Act, Lee is working to build a public safety system that prevents harm, supports survivors, and gives every community the resources it needs to not only survive, but to thrive.

The full conversation and Q&A can be viewed HERE.
title: Rep. Summer Lee Joins CBC Members and Black Mayors to Champion Community-Driven Public Safety Solutions

Washington, D.C. — Congressman Jared Huffman (CA-02), Congressman Dave Min (CA-47), joined by Representatives Michael Lawler (NY-17), and Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), sent a letter urging the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) to develop comprehensive federal safety standards for electric bicycles and higher-speed “e-motos”.

The bipartisan letter comes in response to the CPSC’s Notice of Proposed Rulemaking to establish safety standards for lithium-ion batteries used for e-bikes and other forms of micromobility transit. While the lawmakers acknowledged the importance of addressing the serious fire risks posed by low-quality batteries, they keyed in on the CPSC’s failure to address the broader risks posed by unregulated e-bikes and e-motos.

“While we strongly support the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission taking action to address fire hazards posed by counterfeit and low-quality lithium-ion batteries associated with these products, battery integrity is only one component of a broader set of challenges facing consumers and communities,” said the Members. “We urge the Commission to build on this effort by developing separate, comprehensive safety standards for e-bikes and electric motorcycles.”

“Fire-safe batteries matter, but they will not stop companies from marketing devices capable of motorcycle-level speeds to children as ordinary e-bikes,” said Rep. Min. “Parents should not have to become product safety experts just to know what they are buying for their kids. The CPSC must close these loopholes, require clear product labeling, and establish modern standards that distinguish e-bikes from high-powered e-motos.”

The reforms outlined in the letter reflect key provisions of Congressman Min’s Safe Standards for Personal E-Bike and E-Moto Device Specifications Act, Safe SPEEDS Act, which would establish a comprehensive federal safety framework for electric micromobility products.

Between 2019 and 2022, as e-bike sales in the United States nearly quadrupled, injuries involving e-bikes and e-motos increased by nearly tenfold, according to estimates from the CPSC’s National Electronic Injury Surveillance System. Children and teenagers face particularly serious risks. Health care providers at Rady Children’s Health treated one pediatric e-bike crash patient in 2021 and more than 220 in 2025.

The letter also highlights fatal crashes involving young riders and community members, including the death of 20-year-old Huntington Beach resident Kolby Aipa after an e-bike collision.

The lawmakers urged the CPSC to:

Establish minimum labeling requirements clearly disclosing each device’s maximum speed, motor power, recommended minimum age and intended on-road or off-road use.

Modernize the federal definition of an e-bike and create consistent classifications that clearly distinguish conventional e-bikes from higher-powered e-motos.

Support local crash-data collection and public education by helping law enforcement agencies, emergency responders and local governments accurately identify devices and document injuries and fatalities.

The full letter is available here.

The letter is the latest step in Rep. Min’s continued efforts to improve e-bike safety and close gaps in federal oversight. Earlier this week, Rep. Min joined Irvine Councilmember Betty Martinez Franco’s office for an I-Ride Safe Academy panel focused on helping young riders and their families better understand e-bike risks and practice safe, responsible riding.

title: Reps. Huffman, Lawler, Min and Fitzpatrick Call for Stronger Federal E-Bike and E-Moto Safety Standards

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (D-WA-08) and Congresswoman Erin Houchin (R-IN-09) recently introduced the bipartisan Rural Hospital Cybersecurity Enhancement Act, alongside cosponsors Representatives Jefferson Shreve (R-IN), Glenn "GT" Thompson (R-PA), Jill Tokuda (D-HI), and Jennifer McClellan (D-VA). Companion legislation was introduced in the Senate by Senators Josh Hawley (R-MO), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), and Mark Kelly (D-AZ). The legislation strengthens cybersecurity at rural hospitals by directing the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to develop a comprehensive rural hospital cybersecurity workforce strategy, expand cybersecurity training resources, and improve preparedness against growing cyber threats.

“As a doctor and a patient, I know we must protect hospitals from cyberattacks," said Rep. Schrier. “Rural hospitals in particular often lack the funding and workforce necessary to prevent cyberattacks and some in Washington have already been impacted. This bill will give rural hospitals the tools they need to keep patients safe, protect personal data, and secure medical systems."

"Rural hospitals are often operating with limited staff and resources, yet they're expected to defend against increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks," said Rep. Houchin. "When a rural hospital is forced offline, patient care is put at risk. This bipartisan bill is a practical step toward giving rural providers the workforce, training, and tools they need to strengthen their cybersecurity and continue serving their communities."

"Rural hospitals in Indiana's Sixth District are often the only option for Hoosier families who need care close to home,” said Rep. Shreve. “These hospitals don’t have the resources to hire a cybersecurity team, but they still need to keep their patients’ private information secure. This bill gives them the training and tools they need to do that. I'm glad to join Rep. Houchin on this important legislation."

"In our complex world, it is imperative that we safeguard sensitive personal information and medical records from cybercriminals," said Rep. Thompson. "The Rural Hospital Cybersecurity Enhancement Act aims to protect patient information by helping develop, promote, and expand the rural hospital cybersecurity workforce, particularly through education and training programs tailored to the needs of rural hospitals, such as those in Pennsylvania."

"For rural hospitals, a cyberattack isn't just a disruption to technology, it can become a disruption to care,” said Rep. Tokuda. “This legislation helps ensure rural providers can continue delivering lifesaving care by having the resources, training, and workforce support they need to protect patient data, respond to threats, and continue serving their communities."

“In our rapidly changing digital age, cybersecurity threats continue to grow. Rural hospitals and health clinics often lack the resources and personnel to defend against these threats,” said Rep. McClellan. “The Rural Hospital Cybersecurity Enhancement Act develops a comprehensive workforce training program to protect our rural communities from attacks that could exploit vulnerabilities in our health care system and undermine access to care. I am pleased to work on a bipartisan basis with Congresswoman Houchin to bolster our security measures to help maintain a strong care network.”

“For many years, TRIMEDX has worked with, and provided medical device service for, small town and rural hospitals throughout the country. Already challenged by increasing cost pressures, we have seen first- hand how vulnerable rural hospitals are to cybersecurity attacks and we support any efforts for the development of strategies to address cyber challenges,” said Kristi McDermott, TRIMEDX Chief Operating Officer. “Accordingly, TRIMEDX applauds Rep. Houchin and Rep. Schrier for introducing this strong bipartisan bill which seeks to address growing cybersecurity challenges, to include workforce development strategies, in rural hospitals throughout the country.”

The Rural Hospital Cybersecurity Enhancement Act requires HHS to:

Develop a comprehensive rural hospital cybersecurity workforce development strategy that considers public-private partnerships, cybersecurity curricula, workforce training, and policy recommendations.

Make instructional materials available to help rural hospitals train staff on fundamental cybersecurity practices.

Provide annual updates to Congress on the implementation of the strategy and any related workforce development initiatives.

Cyberattacks against hospitals have become more frequent and more sophisticated, placing patient care, medical records, and critical healthcare infrastructure at risk. Rural hospitals are particularly vulnerable because they often lack the resources to recruit and retain dedicated cybersecurity professionals.

The legislation is endorsed by the American Hospital Association, Blue Cross Blue Shield Association, National Rural Health Association, American Academy of Family Physicians, TRIMEDX, and the Alliance for Quality Medical Device Servicing.

The Senate companion legislation has twice advanced out of the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
title: Reps Schrier, Houchin Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve Rural Hospital Cybersecurity

East Hartford, CT – Today, Rep. John B. Larson (CT-01) applauded a $1.3 billion boost for Pratt & Whitney F135 engines, announced by the U.S. Navy. This new contract from the federal government, following Rep. Larson’s push to secure more funding to build spare engines and parts, will support work in East Hartford, Middletown, Windsor, Wallingford and other locations across the country.

“I have been proud to lead the fight in Congress to ensure Connecticut workers keep the world's top fighter jet flying right here at Pratt & Whitney for years to come,” said Larson. “Following our effort in Congress to increase investments in spare part and engine manufacturing, it is great news that this contract will support good-paying jobs not only in East Hartford and Middletown, but at suppliers in Windsor and across the state. I will never stop fighting for the hard-working machinists and engineers that call our state home, who ensure every day that our Armed Forces and allies have the best equipment possible.”

Rep. Larson, as Co-Chair of the Joint Strike Fighter Caucus, led the entire Connecticut delegation and a bipartisan coalition of Members of Congress from across the country, in a call to increase engine spare orders, a request that passed and was signed into law in February.
title: Larson Applauds $1.3 Billion Contract Boost to Build F135 Engine Spares

AKRON, OHIO — U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) hosted her second Housing Together: A Roundtable with Rep. Sykes at the Akron Urban League Thursday. Building on the first event in March, participants discussed the challenges driving housing costs across Ohio’s 13th Congressional District and identified solutions to make housing more affordable for families.

Panelists identified rising property taxes and increased rent prices as the top issues and pointed to long-term investment in properties and a ban on corporations controlling the single-family home market as potential ways to address the housing affordability crisis.

“Housing affordability is one of the biggest challenges facing families in Northeast Ohio and across the country,” said Rep. Sykes. “Solving the issue requires everyone at the table, lenders, realtors, advocates, and community leaders working together, and I’m proud the roundtable presented real solutions.”

Rep. Sykes was joined by 717 Credit Union President and CEO John Demmler, Akron Cleveland Association of REALTORS Vice President of Advocacy Jamie McMillen, Fair Housing Advocates Association Executive Director Vincent Curry, and Ohio Housing Finance Agency Legislative Liaison Grant Miller. The group focused on housing shortages, expanding affordable housing, increasing homeownership, strengthening consumer protections, and fighting discrimination in the housing market.

“Homeownership remains the American Dream, and every Ohio family deserves the opportunity to achieve it. Conversations like today’s housing roundtable keep the momentum moving toward practical solutions that address housing affordability and supply,” said McMillen. “We appreciate Congresswoman Emilia Sykes’ leadership and support of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which provides communities with important tools to expand housing opportunities. Now the work turns to implementation, and the Akron Cleveland Association of REALTORS® is committed to partnering with policymakers and local communities to help more Ohioans achieve the dream of homeownership.”

“This country is experiencing both a housing and an affordable housing crisis and people and communities are suffering,” said Curry. “The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which recently became law, is the first step to addressing those needs. I appreciate Rep. Sykes, who supported the law, for being proactive in highlighting the problems and bringing together community stakeholders to continue to develop strategies and ideas to help this community and this country to meet its housing needs. My office looks forward to continuing to work with her office.”

“We appreciate the opportunity to participate in Congresswoman Sykes’ housing roundtable, and the opportunity to discuss the various ways we can work together to address housing affordability, which is the foundation for a strong quality of life for Ohioans,” said Ohio Housing Finance Agency Director of Public Affairs Penny Martin.

The roundtable builds on Rep. Sykes’ continued housing leadership. A couple weeks ago, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act became law after she and her congressional colleagues passed the landmark bipartisan bill. The legislation expands housing affordability and supply nationwide by incorporating priorities championed in Rep. Sykes’ Homes Over Massive Investors in Neighborhoods (HOMES) Act, including efforts to address the role of large-scale institutional investors in local housing markets.

Following the passage of the bill, she hosted a telephone town hall with federal and local leaders so constituents could hear directly from experts and receive guidance on their housing concerns.

Rep. Sykes also serves as Chair of the New Democrat Coalition’s Housing Task Force and Co-Convener of the House Democrats’ Housing Working Group.

The New Dems released an Affordability Agenda earlier this year that focuses on:

Cutting red tape and updating permitting and zoning to build four million homes in the next decade.

Leveling the playing field by eliminating unfair tax breaks for private equity and large investors.

Utilizing innovative construction technologies to accelerate home production.

Building more affordable homes by increasing Low-Income Housing Tax Credit allocations and community benefits.

In June, Rep. Sykes was tasked by House Minority Leader U.S. Representative Hakeem Jeffries (NY-08) with co-leading the Housing Working Group to create a policy agenda that lowers the cost of living for working families. So far, the group has held a stakeholder roundtable with more than 20 national groups and several meetings with Members of Congress to hear about their districts’ housing priorities.
title: ICYMI: Rep. Sykes Brings Northeast Ohio Housing Leaders Together to Advance Solutions to Housing Crisis

Washington, D.C.– TODAY, Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) led 33 Members of Congress in calling on the Trump Administration to restore the twice-a-day weather balloon launch schedule, as extreme weather and high heat hit across the country.

Twice-a-day weather balloon launches collect information from high in the atmosphere that allows for more accurate forecasting. Current disruptions to the balloon launch schedule create data gaps that undermine confidence in forecast accuracy.

The Members write:

We are alarmed by the reduction in weather balloon launches and its impact on the accuracy of weather forecasting across the United States. Timely and accurate weather forecasts are critical to protecting the lives, livelihoods, and property of the American people.

This is a manufactured crisis. President Trump and DOGE haphazardly slashed the NWS workforce by roughly 15 percent without considering the impact on public safety. Now, the American people are paying the price. Current efforts to fill staffing gaps at NWS are too little too late. Severe weather will not wait for NWS to hire and train hundreds of new staff. NWS must immediately restore balloon launch capacity before an inaccurate or delayed forecast puts our constituents in harm's way.

Continued failure to follow the twice-a-day balloon launch schedule undermines the accuracy of NWS weather forecasts and increases the likelihood that the American people will be left unprepared for severe weather events. Forcing our constituents to accept increased risks because of your shortsighted and partisan staffing cuts is unacceptable. You must protect Americans’ lives, livelihoods, and property by immediately returning to the twice-a-day balloon launch schedule.

The full letter can be found here.

The letter was signed by Representatives Wesley Bell (D-MO-01), Donald Beyer (D-VA-08), Suzanne Bonamici (D-OR-01), Julia Brownley (D-CA-26), André Carson (D-IN-07), Ed Case (D-HI-01), Kathy Castor (D-FL-14), Emanuel Cleaver (D-MO-05), Jim Costa (D-CA-21), Jasmine Crockett (D-TX-30), Sharice Davids (D-KS-03), Adriano Espaillat (D-NY-13), Lizzie Fletcher (D-TX-07), Maxwell Frost (D-FL-10), Sylvia Garcia (D-TX-29), Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ-07), Pablo Hernández (D-PR), Jared Huffman (D-CA-02), Sara Jacobs (D-CA-51), Henry Johnson (D-GA-04), Stephen Lynch (D-MA-08), Seth Magaziner (D-RI-02), April McClain Delaney (D-MD-06), Christian Menefee (D-TX-18), Seth Moulton (D-MA-06), Joe Neguse (D-CO-02), Brittany Pettersen (D-CO-07), Emily Randall (D-WA-06), Deborah Ross (D-NC-02), Haley Stevens (D-MI-11), Shri Thanedar (D-MI-13), Jill Tokuda (D-HI-02), and Paul Tonko (D-NY-20).

Background

Ranking Member of the House Science, Space, and Technology Environment Subcommittee, Congressman Amo has fought to reverse Trump’s cuts to the National Weather Service and protect American meteorological might.

In Summer 2025, Amo led the charge to reverse Trump’s damaging Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) cuts to the National Weather Service staff. After months of public pressure, the National Weather Service announced plans to hire 450 new staff.

WASHINGTON, D.C. (July 31, 2026) – Today, Rep. Adam Smith introduced a resolution built on a simple idea: a dollar earned should be a dollar taxed, full stop. This resolution calls on Congress to start simplifying the tax code so working-class Americans and the ultra-wealthy play by the same rules.

"For decades, we've asked working families to play by one set of rules while the wealthiest Americans play by another. A teacher, a machinist, a nurse — they see taxes taken out of every paycheck before they ever see the money,” said Rep. Adam Smith. “Meanwhile, the ultra-wealthy grow their fortunes by trillions of dollars a year; paying next to nothing in taxes due to loopholes emplaced quietly over the past 40 years. It's time we started simplifying the tax code around one basic principle: a dollar earned is a dollar taxed, no matter who earns it or how.”

“This resolution tells Congress and the Ways and Means Committee to stop looking away from a system that treats identical gains completely differently depending on whose name is on them. If we're serious about the debt and serious about fairness, this is where we have to start."

The resolution has drawn early support from tax law experts, including Ray D. Madoff, Professor at Boston College Law School and author of “The Second Estate: How the Tax Code Made an American Aristocracy."

"I've spent years studying this issue, and the fix isn't complicated: broaden the income tax so it captures every form of monetary gain, not just wages. This resolution asks the correct, and long overdue questions. I'm glad to see Congress willing to take a serious look at why our tax code treats income so differently depending on where it comes from," said Ray D. Madoff, Professor at Boston College Law School.

Here's the problem:

The country is $39 trillion in debt — and the tax system isn't bringing in enough money to keep up, because too much income never gets taxed in the first place.

Regular paychecks are carrying the load. Income taxes make up about 49% of all federal revenue, and payroll taxes make up another 35% — meaning 84 cents of every federal dollar comes from taxes on wages. Taxes on investments, inheritances, and business ownership make up the rest.

The wealthiest 1% now hold about $55 trillion in net worth, while most Americans don't have enough savings to cover an emergency. Seventy years ago, top earners paid a 94% tax rate on that income. Today the top rate is just 37% — and many still pay far less through additional loopholes.

Billionaires can grow richer by billions a year and barely pay taxes on it, because that money comes from stock and business ownership going up in value, not a paycheck. A dollar earned that way isn't taxed anywhere near like a dollar earned at a job.

Some of the richest people in America pay a lower tax rate than teachers and nurses. A 2021 investigation into leaked IRS records found several of the wealthiest Americans paid a true tax rate in the low single digits, or no income tax at all due to tax loopholes, compared to how much their wealth grew each year — lower than many middle-class workers pay on their salaries.

The resolution calls on the House Ways and Means Committee to hold hearings on this gap, and urges Congress to start simplifying the tax code so every American — whether they earn a paycheck or sell a stock — is taxed the same way on the same amount of money earned.
title: Rep. Adam Smith Introduces Resolution Calling for Equal Tax Treatment of Wage Income and Capital Gains

Cincinnati, OH – Today, Congressman Greg Landsman (D-OH-01) released the following statement after Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haiti has officially ended.

President Trump is about to deport tens of thousands of Haitians. It’s cruel, wrong, and terrible for our country.

Starting this weekend, Haitian families are being told to report to ICE facilities, and we don’t know what will happen next.

What we do know is who these families are. They have dignity. They work really hard. They’ve started businesses, filled manufacturing job shortages, and many of them are home health workers taking care of our families.

The violence in Haiti has been terrifying for years, and it’s only gotten worse. Sending them back would be inhumane. They’d have a difficult time finding housing, healthcare, jobs. Many will starve. Some may not survive.

That’s why the House forced a vote and passed an extension of TPS for Haitian families.

The Senate is still in session for another week and must act before it’s too late.

Everyone deserves to be treated with dignity – Americans, Haitians, everyone. We can’t lose sight of our shared humanity.

###
title: Landsman Statement on Trump Deporting Tens of Thousands of Haitians
