San Diego, CA. — Today, Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) introduced a new bill to rename a Pacific Beach Post Office in his district in honor of Mary Wilding, a dedicated public servant and community leader.

Mary served the people of Pacific Beach for over 50 years. She sat on the Pacific Beach Town Council in a variety of capacities, from booster to board member to executive secretary. As a testament to her work, Mary was named honorary mayor of Pacific Beach in 1991 and was recognized as Woman of the Year by the California State Assembly

Image

“Mary was an iconic figure and fierce champion for the Pacific Beach community. She touched the lives of everyone who crossed her path, far beyond the Town Council” said Rep. Peters. “Naming this post office after Mary will ensure that her contributions to Pacific Beach are remembered and that her legacy of compassion and service lives on.”

“Few individuals have left as profound of a mark on Pacific Beach as Mary Wilding. Mary established traditions of civic service and appreciation that continue to this day,” said Pacific Beach Town Council President Charlie Nieto. “Her legacy lives on not only through the lasting improvements she made to Pacific Beach, but also through her family, who have continued her commitment to serving the community. Renaming this post office in Mary's honor is a fitting tribute to the decades of dedication, leadership, and advocacy she devoted to Pacific Beach.”

“Our mom, Mary Wilding, was an English Literature major and had a profound love for the written word. Multiple trips to this post office allowed her masterful letters and clever ideas to reach far and wide,” said Mary’s daughter, Katy. “Her many talents and hard work helped gain support for the PB Town Council. This contributed greatly to her legacy, as well as to the betterment of her beloved Pacific Beach.”

“Mary certainly had a special way with people. Her sincerity and witty sense of humor, allowed her to bring people together to work toward common goals,” said Mary’s family. “She had great initiative and a wonderful imagination. It was often said that she knew everyone in Pacific Beach! Mom’s pleasing personality was truly a gift.”

Mary dedicated herself to improving the Pacific Beach community through practical beautification projects, including the addition of a pedestrian walkway, seawall, and landscaping on Ocean Boulevard.

She was also a strong advocate for small businesses and local law enforcement. She founded the Police and Emergency Services Appreciation Night (PAESAN), an annual community block party and barbecue honoring local first responders. She also spent several years as a docent at the San Diego Museum of Art.

Mary passed away in 2016 and is survived by her eight children, all of whom have continued their mother's legacy of public service.

###
title: Rep. Peters Announces Bill to Name Post Office After Pacific Beach Icon

WATCH: Rep. Harder’s reaction leaving the Stockton ICE facility

STOCKTON – Today, following ICE’s failure to respond to his letter demanding details on current operations, Rep. Josh Harder (CA-09) conducted an unannounced oversight inspection of the Stockton ICE facility to get in-person answers. Harder first inspected the facility in January, but after a federal judge overturned mandatory scheduling rules, Harder led a surprise inspection of the field office and pressed ICE agents for updates.

“I just conducted a surprise inspection of the Stockton ICE facility to get face-to-face answers to the questions that this agency has been dodging for months, and I’m still outraged at the answers we’re not getting,” said Rep. Harder. “The chaos we’re seeing across the Valley proves that this agency is out of control. That’s why I’m opposing any new funding for ICE, and we’re going to keep up the pressure with more oversight until our families get the answers and the accountability that they deserve.”

Harder’s demands about ICE operations in the Valley:

Oversight Inspection – Complete written responses to questions provided in writing and in-person to personnel at the Stockton ICE facility.

Community Concerns – Past, current, and upcoming enforcement activities, as well as details on access to counsel, food, water, medical care, interpretation services, and accommodations for children during detainments at the local facility.

Policy Compliance – Current policies used by agents operating out of the Stockton ICE facility regarding unmarked vehicles, activities near schools and other locations used by children, and compliance with legally-required court orders and federally-mandated policies.

Read Harder’s full letter to Acting Director David Venturella here.

Harder has been pushing for reforms at ICE and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for months, including leading successful calls for former Secretary Kristi Noem’s firing. Following her departure, Harder demanded the new Secretary Markwayne Mullin prioritize clear standards for enforcement, bans on face coverings, mandatory identification, new use-of-force policies, and bans on racial profiling. Harder has also continued to oppose any new federal funding for ICE until these reforms are enacted.

###
title: ICE: Harder Conducts Unannounced Oversight Inspection of Stockton ICE Facility

BURNSVILLE, MN – Yesterday, U.S. Representative Angie Craig hosted her inaugural Unsung Heroes Recognition Event in Burnsville to honor union workers in Minnesota’s Second District. Rep. Craig was joined by Minnesota labor leaders to highlight their collective support for working class wins.

“Labor is the backbone of Minnesota’s economy, but right now it’s under attack,” said Rep. Craig. “From terminating union contracts to blocking the right to organize, the Trump Administration has made union-busting a primary part of its agenda. That’s why I'm honored to host this event – to double down on my support for Minnesota labor and make sure their hard work doesn’t go unnoticed.”

Rep. Craig was joined by Bernie Burnham, President, Minnesota AFL-CIO; Kim Nelson, Political Director, Northern Midwest Regional Council of Carpenters; Amanda Heiser, Northern Midwest Regional Council of Carpenters; John Burcaw, Director, Finishing Trades Institute; Laura Asklein, Political Organizer, AFSCME; Max Hall, External Relations and Planning Director, AFSCME; Rick Bartz, Business Manager and Financial Secretary, IBEW Local 949 and Denise White, President, AFGE Local 1969.

Together, they recognized local union members for the following:

Demonstrating a commitment to service and community engagement.

Demonstrating tremendous leadership skills.

Devoting 15+ years of service.

Going above and beyond every day and showing tremendous pride in their work.

Being assets to their unions, dedicating themselves to outstanding organizing and continuously going above and beyond in the recruiting process.

Rep. Craig has stood with Minnesota’s labor unions and been a champion of organized labor since day one. She helped introduce the PRO Act, which protects workers’ right to organize and collectively bargain for higher wages, better benefits and safer working conditions.

And she has penned her own legislation, like the Supporting Apprenticeship Colleges Act, which would help increase enrollment in registered apprenticeship programs.

Rep. Craig also helped introduce the Faster Labor Contracts Act, which requires employers to begin negotiations with a newly certified union within 10 days of receiving a request, and the No Tax Breaks for Union Busting Act, which blocks large corporations who union bust from collecting tax breaks.

Finally, she is a cosponsor of the Tax Fairness for Workers Act, which would create an “above-the-line” tax deduction for union dues and expenses.

###
title: Rep. Craig Hosts Unsung Heroes Recognition Event to Honor CD2 Labor Unions

WASHINGTON, DC – Following disturbing reports that the Department of Defense removed the names of four American troops from the official Iran War death toll, Congressman Pat Ryan – a member of the House Armed Services Committee, Iraq war combat veteran, and the first West Point graduate to represent the Academy in Congress – and 14 of his fellow Democratic veterans are urging the Administration to accurately and transparently account for U.S. servicemembers killed and wounded in the Iran war.

“As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers,” wrote the lawmakers.

“The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports,” they continued. “We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.”

Following public outcry, the Department of Defense quietly restored the names of the four U.S. servicemembers removed from the Iran War death toll over the weekend. The Administration has not provided an adequate explanation as to why the servicemembers were removed in the first place.

In addition to Ryan, Representatives Mike Thompson (CA-04), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Derek Tran (CA-45), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Jason Crow (CO-06), Bobby Scott (VA-03), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), and Jared Golden (ME-02) signed the letter.

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear President Trump,

As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers.

The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports. Inaccurate and delayed reports from the Department of War about U.S. casualties is bad for morale and undermines our U.S. servicemembers.

We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.

Sincerely,

###
title: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN AND DEMOCRATIC VETERANS DEMAND TRANSPARENCY ON IRAN WAR CASUALTIES

The co-chairs of the Nuclear Weapons and Arms Control Working Group in the House of Representatives, Representative Don Beyer (VA-08) and Representative John Garamendi (CA-08), and Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on the Middle East and North Africa Brad Sherman (CA-32) issued the following statement in response to the recent announcement of a deal to provide Saudi Arabia with nuclear technologies without safeguards that prevent weaponization.

“As leaders who have long supported non-proliferation, we are deeply concerned about the failure of the proposed U.S. – Saudi civilian nuclear agreement to include key protections to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons. It is unacceptable that this Administration would push forward a deal without comprehensive safeguards to prevent Saudi Arabia from weaponizing the nuclear technology that President Trump has agreed to give them. Without these safeguards, we could give Saudi Arabia the tools it needs to become a nuclear-weapons state – something Crown Prince Mohammad Bin Salman has openly aspired to achieve.”

“If the Trump administration submits this so-called deal for the required Congressional review, we will take all available steps, including legislative action, to reject any deal that fails to include the safeguards necessary to prevent Saudi Arabia from developing nuclear weapons.

“Any nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia should include the strongest safeguards, including both a requirement that the nation signs the ‘Additional Protocol’ with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) guaranteeing robust inspection of nuclear facilities, and agrees to the ‘Gold Standard’ prohibiting uranium enrichment and the reprocessing of spent nuclear fuel—capabilities that are necessary to produce nuclear weapons. The Additional Protocol and Gold Standard are reasonable and are included in our nuclear cooperation agreement with the United Arab Emirates (UAE), which allows them to generate electricity efficiently without posing a nuclear weapons threat.

“President Trump is currently waging a disastrous war against Iran ostensibly to prevent it from acquiring nuclear weapons. It was the United States that provided preliminary nuclear technology to Iran when it was ruled by a friendly, pro-Western monarch – and all of the technology in the hands of the Shah in 1978 fell into the hands of the Ayatollah in 1979. We cannot make the same mistake with Saudi Arabia.

“Preventing Saudi Arabia from developing nuclear weapons has long been an area of bipartisan consensus here in Congress – because America’s national security depends on it. We will fight to make sure Congress rejects any nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia that fails to protect the American people from a nuclear-armed Saudi state.”
title: Beyer, Garamendi, Sherman: Congress Must Reject Dangerous Trump-Saudi Nuclear Deal Without Safeguards

MONTGOMERY, Ala. (WSFA) - Congressman Shomari Figures (D-AL) delivered a warning at the Montgomery Area Chamber of Commerce briefing on Wednesday, highlighting how looming federal issues, specifically the solvency of Social Security, threaten to disproportionately impact Alabamians.

“We know that seniors here in the State of Alabama, for a lot of them, for many of them, they weren’t fortunate enough to have big 401(k)s, big IRAs,” Figures said. “Their retirement plan looks like this: own my own home, have children that can help take care of us, and Social Security.”

Figures pointed to updated projections showing the Social Security Trust Fund is on track to run out of money ahead of schedule, with the exhaustion date now expected in 2032.

“What that means in the State of Alabama is that the average Social Security benefit at that time that our seniors receive will be reduced by about 20% to 30%,” Figures warned. “That is real. That is a real problem.”

Figures said that more than 50% of seniors in Alabama rely on Social Security as their primary source of income.

In June 2026, approximately 75,000 Alabamians were receiving Social Security or Supplemental Security Income (SSI).

The financial strain is compounded by low average incomes across the state. While the individual median income in Alabama sits at approximately $34,000, Figures noted that “for seniors in the State of Alabama, that number is even lower.”

The threat to retirement benefits is not the only federal issue impacting Alabamians. Figures noted that legislation passed in Washington, D.C., including the Big Beautiful Bill Act, could signal significant financial shifts for the elderly.

Figures said that other sectors of Alabama’s economy and community are also feeling the squeeze of federal policy decisions, including agricultural tariffs and changes to food assistance programs that have caused some parents to lose SNAP benefits.
title: Rep. Figures warns Social Security in jeopardy for Alabama seniors.

Ahead of the Scarborough Town Council's special meeting Wednesday evening, Congresswoman Chellie Pingree (D-Maine) sent the Council a letter supporting their proclamation calling for a federal review of the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility at 40 Manson Libby Road. In the letter, Pingree urged the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to seriously reconsider whether the facility should continue operating in Scarborough if its presence is undermining public trust and making residents feel less safe.

“The facility at 40 Manson Libby Road has become a symbol of fear, uncertainty, and intimidation for many immigrant families and their neighbors,” Pingree said. “That should concern every one of us.”

In her letter, Pingree emphasized that the Town of Scarborough has every right to question whether continuing to host the ICE facility serves the interests of the community. She called on DHS and ICE to conduct a serious review of the facility's continued operation and to give meaningful weight to the concerns raised by local residents and elected officials.

“When a federal facility reaches the point where its very presence undermines the public confidence and leaves residents feeling less safe, the federal government has a responsibility to reconsider if that facility belongs there at all,” she said.

Pingree also reiterated that her office has been conducting aggressive oversight of ICE's activities in Maine following the fatal shooting of her constituent, Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, in Biddeford. She has demanded answers from DHS, called for a transparent investigation, pursued legislative and appropriations oversight, and remains committed to holding the agency accountable to the communities it serves.

“Federal agencies must carry out their responsibilities in a manner that respects human dignity, civil rights, due process, and the communities in which they operate. When they fail to do so, local communities have not only the right but the responsibility to speak out,” Pingree said.

The full letter is available here and copied below.

Pingree has conducted official oversight visits of ICE facilities in Scarborough, Burlington, Mass., and Dilley, Texas.

Earlier this month, Pingree sent a letter to DHS Secretary Mullin demanding answers about the fatal shooting of her constituent, Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, by ICE officers in Biddeford, Maine, on July 13.

Pingree also joined the other members of Maine’s Congressional Delegation in sending a letter to Secretary Mullin calling for a comprehensive, transparent, and expedited investigation. In addition, Pingree and Reps. Jayapal (D-Wash.), Garcia (D-Texas), Raskin (D-Md.), and Thompson (D-Miss.) led nearly 200 Members in calling for independent investigations into Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and Johan Sebastian Guerrero’s deaths and demanded that ICE halt removal proceedings against the witnesses.

+++

Dear Council Members,

I write to express my support for your proclamation regarding the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility at 40 Manson Libby Road. I commend the Town Council for giving voice to the significant and growing concerns in Scarborough and across Maine about ICE’s presence in our communities.

The tragic death of Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero has profoundly shaken our state. While investigations into the shooting continue, many Mainers are once again confronting a larger and deeply troubling reality: ICE is operating in our communities with no transparency, accountability, or regard for the people who live here. The facility at 40 Manson Libby Road has become a symbol of fear, uncertainty, and intimidation for many immigrant families and their neighbors. That should concern every one of us.

Residents should not have to wonder whether heavily armed enforcement actions will occur in their neighborhoods, whether federal officers are operating under appropriate oversight, or whether a facility in their town is contributing to tactics that erode trust between neighbors and government. This affects whether people feel safe attending school, seeking medical care, reporting crimes, practicing their faith, or simply going about their lives.

The Town of Scarborough has every right to ask whether continuing to host this facility serves the interests of the community. In my view, that question deserves serious consideration from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). When a federal facility reaches the point where its very presence undermines the public confidence and leaves residents feeling less safe, the federal government has a responsibility to reconsider if that facility belongs there at all. I believe ICE and DHS should undertake a serious review of the continued operation of this facility and proceed in accordance with the community’s wishes.

Please know that I am exploring every available avenue to address enforcement operations and the continued presence of ICE in Scarborough. My office has been conducting aggressive oversight of ICE’s activities in Maine and demanding answers from DHS regarding the preventable circumstances that led to Mr. Guerrero’s death. I have demanded a transparent and collaborative investigation, pressed the agency to justify its actions, sought greater accountability, and continue to pursue legislative, appropriations, and administration options to challenge policies that undermine public trust. I remain committed to using every tool available to me as a Member of Congress to ensure that federal agencies are accountable to the communities they serve.

Your proclamation appropriately recognizes that the immigration process and community trust are not mutually exclusive. Federal agencies must carry out their responsibilities in a manner that respects human dignity, civil rights, due process, and the communities in which they operate. When they fail to do so, local communities have not only the right but the responsibility to speak out.

Thank you for your leadership and your willingness to stand with the people of Scarborough during these difficult times. I am proud to stand with you, and I will continue working alongside you to pursue every available opportunity to reevaluate the federal government’s continued operation of this facility.

Sincerely,

###
title: Pingree Backs Scarborough Town Council's Call for Federal Review of ICE Facility

NORWICH, CT – Today, Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee and a senior Member of the House Education and Workforce Committee, released the following statement after the Navy officially executed contract awards to Electric Boat for construction of nine Virginia-class Block VI fast-attack submarines and five Columbia-class Build II ballistic missile submarines. Electric Boat is awarded $42.1 billion for the Virginia-class program and $29.5 billion for the Columbia-class program. Combined with an additional $5 billion for shipyard enhancements, the contracts total $76.6 billion in value, representing the largest shipbuilding contracts in modern history. Congress authorized both the Virginia-class Block VI contract in 2023 in the FY24 NDAA and this Columbia-class Build II contract in 2025 in the FY26 NDAA. The legislative language in both bills originated in the Seapower subcommittee’s marks.

“These Block VI and Build II construction contracts, which Congress authorized in 2023 and 2025 respectively, provide a surging, unwavering demand signal to the entire submarine industrial base. Together, the Block VI and Build II contracts represent the biggest shipbuilding award in modern American history,” Courtney said. “These multiyear commitments by Congress and the Navy secure work at submarine shipyards and thousands of supply chain companies well into the late 2030s, further boosted by the AUKUS security agreement and the sale of three in-service Virginia-class submarines to Australia in the 2030s.”

“These contract awards will be the driving force to stimulate growth across the submarine industrial base. Crucially, the thousands of small business manufacturers who are essential to the industrial base now have the certainty they have been asking for to make needed investments in hiring, facilities, and equipment,” Courtney continued. “Congress and the Navy must now double-down on industrial base investments that are moving delivery schedules to the left. These are targeted investments, such as the record shipbuilder wage improvement funded by Congress and secured through collective bargaining in 2025 that is fueling record hiring and workforce retention at Electric Boat this year. We must continue expanding the successful workforce training programs that have rejuvenated southern New England’s manufacturing sector so they can skill-up more students and jobseekers for long-term submarine careers.”

Earlier this month, Courtney wrote the op-ed, “Building the 21st Century Arsenal of Democracy,” which highlighted the recent milestone of 10,000 graduates from the Southeastern New England’s Defense Industry Alliance’s network of submarine workforce training pipelines. In the piece, Courtney details the effort, dating back to the launch of the Manufacturing Pipeline Initiative in 2016, to rebuild the region’s manufacturing base.

In March, Courtney wrote a letter to the Department of Defense calling on the Navy to execute delivery of the Virginia-class Block VI construction contract.

In April, in a Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee hearing on shipbuilding, Ranking Member Courtney, referring to the Block VI contract, called multiyear procurement the “Da-Vinci Code” to stimulate growth in the shipbuilding industrial base. To watch and download the hearing clip, click here.

###
title: Courtney Statement on New $76.6 Billion Contract Awards to Electric Boat for Block VI Virginia-Class and Build II Columbia-Class Construction

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representative Greg Stanton (D-Ariz) issued the following statement:

“Harry Mitchell was as Tempe as it gets.

Born and raised here, he graduated from Tempe High, attended Arizona State University, and returned to teach American Government at his alma mater for three decades, shaping generations of young minds along the way.

He gave decades of his life to the city he loved, serving on the Tempe City Council, as Mayor, and representing the area in the Arizona Senate. His fingerprints are on nearly every corner of his hometown.

Running for Congress was the culmination of a lifetime of service. A Blue Dog through and through, Harry frequently reached across the aisle—but he was never afraid to take a hard vote. That was Harry: a public servant who put people before politics, always.
title: Stanton Statement on Passing of Congressman Harry Mitchell

Clinics Have Closed, Hospital Beds and Jobs Have Been Cut, and an Erie County Nursing Home Is Slated to Shut Down - With More Cuts Set to Hit Western New York in 2027

BUFFALO, N.Y. - House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (NY-08) joined Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) at Evergreen Health on Tuesday to mark one year since Republicans in Congress passed the Big, Ugly Bill, enacting the largest healthcare cuts in American history. Leader Jeffries and Congressman Kennedy detailed its mounting toll on Western New York, including coverage losses for 470,000 New Yorkers who relied on the Essential Plan as of July 1, 2026. On top of that, clinics have closed, hospital beds and jobs have been cut, and a local nursing home in southern Erie County is slated to shutter, with additional cuts to Medicaid scheduled to take effect in 2027.

“I stood shoulder-to-shoulder last year with doctors, nurses, union leaders, and healthcare leaders, and we warned what would happen when Republicans in Washington voted to enact the largest healthcare cut in American history in order to pay for permanent tax cuts for the wealthy and well-connected,” said Congressman Kennedy. “Clinics have closed, hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers have lost coverage, and premiums skyrocketed for those who were lucky enough to keep their insurance. A nursing home in our community is closing, with many more on the brink of financial collapse. As a direct result of these cuts, hospitals have been forced to cut hospital beds and jobs, weakening our healthcare safety net. Republicans own every single one of those losses. When Leader Jeffries is elected Speaker of the House in 2027, canceling the cuts and delivering for families struggling to make ends meet will be our top priority.”

“Extreme MAGA Republicans have imposed the largest assault on healthcare in modern American history. Their One Big Ugly Bill included a $1 trillion cut to Medicaid, putting hospitals, nursing homes and community health centers at great risk all across the country,” said House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (NY-08). “Access to high-quality, affordable healthcare must be a right available to every single American. That's what House Democrats are going to work to bring to life here in Western New York and all across the country. Together, thanks to the work of fighters like Rep. Tim Kennedy, we will win back the House of Representatives and do all that is necessary to cancel the cuts, lower the cost and save healthcare.”

"The 'Big Ugly Bill' is exactly what its name suggests: a giveaway to the wealthy paid for on the backs of working families,” said Senator Jeremy Zellner. “One year later, Americans are already seeing the consequences through higher healthcare costs, reduced access to care, and growing uncertainty, with even deeper Medicaid cuts still on the horizon. Healthcare should never be treated as a bargaining chip. I stand with Congressman Kennedy and Leader Jeffries in demanding these harmful cuts be reversed before even more families lose the care they depend on."

Assemblymember Jon D. Rivera said, “A year after the passage of the so-called ‘One Big Beautiful Bill,’ Western New Yorkers are already feeling the consequences of Washington’s reckless healthcare cuts. These policies have put affordable healthcare further out of reach for working families, seniors, children, and individuals with disabilities who rely on Medicaid and other critical programs to access the care they need. At a time when families are already struggling with rising costs, these cuts have created even greater uncertainty and hardship for our communities. I am grateful to our Democratic leadership in Congress for continuing to shine a light on the real-world impact of these decisions and for their commitment to reversing these harmful cuts. I stand with them in the fight to protect access to care, strengthen our healthcare system, and ensure that every New Yorker can receive quality, affordable healthcare regardless of their income or ZIP code.”

“Federal cuts to healthcare funding are devastating our Western New York community, creating job losses, limiting the availability of nursing home beds, eliminating critical care services, and shutting down healthcare facilities. Cuts to healthcare impact every Western New Yorker – whether you need reproductive care, elective surgery, or a place for your elderly loved one. When nursing homes like Jennie B Richmond in Springville, Weinberg Campus in Amherst or Absolut Care of Westfield closed – hundreds of nursing home beds were no longer available in our community. Without these beds, hospital patients must wait longer to be discharged into our long-term care system, creating longer wait times for hospital patients and limiting the list of available facilities where loved ones can be placed within our community. We must work together to cancel federal healthcare cuts and fully fund healthcare because quality healthcare for everyone is at risk,” said Grace Bogdanove, 1199SEIU Vice President for WNY Nursing Homes.

“The United Steelworkers stand with Leader Jeffries and Congressman Kennedy as they fight for all working class women and men with their commitment to reversing the devastating effects of this disastrous bill,” said David Wasuria, United Steelworkers District 4 Director.

"When women lose access to healthcare, our entire economy feels the impact," said Sheri Scavone, CEO of the Western New York Women's Foundation. "The One Big Beautiful Bill's more than $1 trillion in Medicaid reductions threaten the health and financial stability of the women who make up the majority of our healthcare, retail, hospitality, and caregiving workforce. Medicaid covers more than 40% of births in the United States and nearly half of all children, while 93% of women enrolled in Medicaid are already working, attending school, caring for children or family members, or living with an illness or disability that limits their ability to work. Women also comprise 77% of healthcare workers with direct patient contact and 84% of the long-term care workforce, making these cuts especially damaging to both the people who provide care and those who depend on it.

"The healthcare cuts enacted last year have had real consequences for working families, seniors, and the most vulnerable members of our community," said Erie County Legislator Lawrence Dupre. "Access to quality, affordable healthcare should never be treated as a political bargaining chip, and I appreciate Congressman Kennedy and Leader Jeffries for continuing to fight against these harmful cuts and for standing up for the people who depend on these critical services."

Western New York is already living with the consequences of the Big, Ugly Bill. Buffalo Therapy Services clinics in Amherst and North Tonawanda have closed, along with an outpatient surgery center in Amherst and the Family Planning Clinic on Main Street in Buffalo. Meanwhile, beds have been cut for rehabilitation services, and approximately 150 jobs have been cut at Erie County Medical Center, the region’s only Level 1 Trauma Center. In nearby Springville, the Jennie B. Richmond Nursing Home has received state approval to close, putting dozens of caregiving jobs and residents' care at risk.

The damage extends statewide. The Big, Ugly Bill eliminated $7.5 billion in federal funding for New York’s Essential Plan, and as of July 1, an estimated 470,000 New Yorkers have lost coverage[1], faced with the choice of sharply higher premiums or no insurance at all. Beginning in 2027, new Medicaid work requirements will threaten coverage for hundreds of thousands more New Yorkers.

Leader Jeffries and Congressman Kennedy demanded House Republicans cancel these cuts before more clinics, nursing homes, and hospital units are lost, and vowed that a Democratic majority would restore the funding that Republicans transferred to billionaires through permanent tax cuts.

###
title: One Year Later: Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries Joins Congressman Tim Kennedy at Evergreen Health to Condemn the GOP's Healthcare Cuts

LOS ANGELES, CA – Today, Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37) held a press conference to announce the upcoming introduction of her Stop ICE’s Medical Neglect Act of 2026, legislation that creates a standardized system to report medical neglect in ICE detention facilities, requires each complaint to be investigated, and ensures adequate follow-up care. The congresswoman was joined by Reps. Judy Chu (CA-28), Lou Correa (CA-46), and Gil Cisneros (CA-31). A livestream is available here.

This legislation is in direct response to ICE repeatedly denying proper medical care to Carlitos Ricardo Parias, a constituent of Rep. Kamlager-Dove, following a gunshot wound he suffered during an immigration enforcement traffic stop in October. He has been detained at Adelanto since December.

“Our humanity does not end at the doors of an ICE detention center. No one should suffer in government custody because their medical needs were ignored,” said Rep. Kamlager-Dove. “Yet for nearly a year, my constituent Ricardo has repeatedly sought medical care at Adelanto, only to watch his pleas go unanswered and his condition worsen. Tragically, Ricardo’s story is not unique. That’s why I’m introducing the Stop ICE’s Medical Neglect Act to track these instances of abuse and ensure every detainee receives the timely and appropriate care they deserve.”

"We will not stand by while our immigrant neighbors are abused, denied basic human dignity, and treated as though their lives do not matter," said Rep. Judy Chu. "Rep. Kamlager-Dove’s legislation is so important because it will provide permanent protections for detainees by allowing them and their advocates to report medical neglect, and ensure those complaints are reviewed by board-certified medical professionals. Those responsible for the suffering and deaths in U.S. custody must be held accountable.”

"Nobody should be denied basic care because they're in federal custody,” said Rep. Correa. "There are too many stories of untreated injuries, ignored medical requests, and unsafe drinking water in these facilities. That's not right, and it's not who we are as a country. This bill gives people in detention a real way to speak up about abuse or neglect without fear of retaliation.”

"Adelanto is a private prison. Owned and operated by the GEO Group with one goal in mind, padding their balance sheet. They do this by cutting back on service like medical treatment. This is happening across the country, and our neighbors are suffering because of it. This rampant mistreatment at ICE detention centers must end now. The bill introduced today will implement measures to hold ICE accountable for their disturbing pattern of mistreatment at detention centers across the country, requires them to provide adequate care, and takes significant steps to protect detainees’ access to the constitutional rights they continue to be denied. It’s long past time for the lawless actions of ICE to be reined in," said Rep. Cisneros.

The Stop ICE’s Medical Neglect Act would:

Require the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to create an accessible database for detainees or legal counsel, advocates, and family members on their behalf, to file complaints of medical neglect or abuse while detained.

Assign contracted, board-certified medical practitioners to review each complaint and provide appropriate treatment or medication to detainees, either in-person or through telehealth video conference call, until appropriate relief is provided.

The medical practitioners will have substantial experience administering care in correctional or detention facilities.

Maintain a confidential filing process to protect detainees against retaliation or adverse treatment.

No information will be shared without the detainee’s expressed consent.

Inform detainees of language-appropriate interpretation services and provide translators during medical visits.

You can read the full bill text here.

Background:

Carlitos Ricardo Parias has been detained at the Adelanto ICE Processing Center since December and has received inadequate medical care for the gunshot wound he sustained during an immigration enforcement traffic stop in October.

In April, the Parias family reached out to the office of Rep. Kamlager-Dove seeking help securing access to medical care, and caseworkers began submitting inquiries to DHS regarding his treatment plan. In May, Rep. Kamlager-Dove conducted an oversight visit at Adelanto to check on Parias and press staff to provide appropriate care. Parias has described suffering from pain, limited mobility, swelling/discoloration, fevers, and persistent headaches. There are also concerns that he may have developed a bone infection.

Earlier this month, following advocacy from Rep. Kamlager-Dove and others, a federal judge ordered sweeping changes to improve conditions for detainees at Adelanto. Last week, Rep. Kamlager-Dove took to the House Floor to once again demand that ICE provide Mr. Parias the medical care he needs.
title: Kamlager-Dove Announces Bill to Ensure Medical Care for ICE Detainees

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) today marked her first 100 days in Congress, a period defined by robust legislative action, sustained oversight of the Trump administration, and direct engagement with constituents across New Jersey's 11th District.

In her first week in office, Representative Mejia introduced her first bill, the Living Wage for All Act. The legislation raises the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour and has since been introduced in the Senate. Since then, she has co-sponsored 85 pieces of legislation, including Medicare for All, the College for All Act, and the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, along with measures to reform the Supreme Court, guarantee universal child care and paid leave, overturn Citizens United, protect LGBTQ+ rights, enact tax fairness, lower housing and energy costs, and support parents and caregivers.

In the district, Rep. Mejia recently secured more than $5 million in federal grants from the Department of Health and Human Services for health care and child care programs. She has held two town halls to hear directly from constituents and, as a member of the House Small Business Committee, has visited local business owners across the district while voting to invest greater resources in Main Street.

"My first 100 days have been about carrying our district with me into every room I walk into down in Washington, D.C., from Randolph to Belleville and everywhere in between," said Congresswoman Analilia Mejia. "When I introduced a bill to raise the minimum wage to $25 an hour, I was thinking about families working multiple jobs just to keep up. When I launched the 14th Amendment Task Force, I was thinking about our neighbors whose rights and safety are under threat. Every hearing, every town hall, every visit to a small business on Main Street comes back to this community. I'm committed to showing up for New Jersey every single day, and for the next 100 days and far beyond, I'm fighting for an economy and a democracy that works for everyone."

As a member of the House Homeland Security Committee, Rep. Mejia regularly conducts oversight of the Delaney Hall and Elizabeth detention centers and tracks the conditions facing medically vulnerable people held inside them. In one of her first hearings, she sharply questioned Secretary Mullin, who was unable to answer basic questions about medical care for chronically ill detainees.

As the administration and the Supreme Court continue to threaten fundamental rights, Rep. Mejia formed the Defend the 14th Amendment Task Force with the support of House Democratic leadership to protect the constitutional guarantees of due process, equal protection under the law, and birthright citizenship through public education and coordinated congressional action.

WATCH: Davids hosts press conference with Kansans benefiting from tax policies she supports

text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28), the only psychologist currently serving in Congress, led 62 House Democrats in a letter requesting answers from U.S. Secretary of Veterans Affairs Doug Collins about significant reductions in the Veterans Health Administration’s (VHA) behavioral and mental health workforce and the impact these staffing losses are having on Veterans’ access to lifesaving mental health care.

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) serves nearly 9 million Veterans nationwide. Nearly one-third of Veterans enrolled in VHA have a confirmed mental health diagnosis, and more than 6,398 Veterans died by suicide in 2023 alone. Yet since the beginning of the Trump Administration, the VA has lost more than 300 psychologists and 700 social workers, including over 200 psychiatrists in 2025 alone. That same year, 57% of VA facilities reported severe psychology staffing shortages, making psychology the most frequently understaffed clinical occupation across the VHA.

VHA mental health professionals are uniquely trained to address the complex needs of Veterans, helping them manage serious conditions such as combat-related trauma, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), anxiety, depression, panic disorders, and substance abuse disorders.

The Members wrote:

“The consequences for Veterans are evident. Staffing shortages have caused longer wait times, cancelled appointments, interrupted treatment, and the loss of trusted clinicians. Some Veterans report waiting multiple months for an available appointment and constantly having to rebuild their relationships with therapists from scratch as they are forced to switch between multiple therapists in succession. Therapists and Veterans also report being forced to replace one-on-one sessions with large group sessions, even when not clinically appropriate This cycle of disruption has led some Veterans to give up treatment all together. One Veteran warned that losing access to their trusted therapist was a matter of ‘life or death.’

…Mental health clinicians have reported unmanageable caseloads, growing uncertainty about the future of their positions, and concerns that political directives around diversity, equity, and inclusion have made it more difficult to provide the highest quality care for their patients. This loss of hundreds of experienced clinicians—and the therapeutic relationships they built with veterans over years of care—cannot be quickly or easily replaced, even as the need for Veterans’ mental health services continues to grow.

[…]

Given the persistent shortages of mental health professionals across the Department, it is critical that Congress understands the scope of these workforce challenges and the Department's efforts to address them.”

The letter was signed by Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), André Carson (IN-07), Troy Carter (LA-02), Ed Case (HI-01), Sean Casten (IL-06), Kathy Castor (FL-14), Gilbert Cisneros (CA-31), Lou Correa (CA-46), Jim Costa (CA-21), Sharice Davids (KS-03), Danny Davis (IL-07), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Diana DeGette (CO-01), Christopher Deluzio (PA-17), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Debbie Dingell (MI-06), Lloyd Doggett (TX-37), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Shomari Figures (AL-02), Bill Foster (IL-11), John Garamendi (CA-08), Jesús García (IL-04), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Glenn Ivey (MD-04), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Rick Larsen (WA-02), Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Sam Liccardo (CA-16), Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), LaMonica McIver (NJ-10), Jared Moskowitz (FL-23), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Nancy Pelosi (CA-11), Brittany Pettersen (CO-07), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Kim Schrier (WA-08), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Adam Smith (WA-09), Greg Stanton (AZ-04), Haley Stevens (MI-11), Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), Thomas Suozzi (NY-03), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Mike Thompson (CA-04), Dina Titus (NV-01), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Paul Tonko (NY-20), Derek Tran (CA-45), Marc Veasey (TX-33), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), and Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).

The letter is endorsed by the National Alliance for Mental Illness (NAMI), Union Veterans Council, Common Defense, and AMVETS.

If you or a loved one need mental health support, dial 988 to be connected to the National Suicide & Crisis Lifeline 24/7. Counselors can also be reached by text message or online chat. You may also dial 911 or go to your nearest emergency room to seek help.

Read the full letter HERE and below.

--------------------------------------------

The Honorable Doug Collins

Secretary

U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs

810 Vermont Avenue NW

Washington, DC 20420

Dear Secretary Collins:

We write with concern regarding recent reports about reductions in the Veterans Health Administration’s (VHA) behavioral and mental health workforce and the potential impact on Veterans’ access to care.

Caring for our nation's Veterans is a fundamental responsibility, and that includes ensuring access to high-quality mental health care. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) serves nearly 9 million Veterans nationwide and is charged with providing timely, high-quality care to support their health, well-being, and successful transition to civilian life.1 VHA clinicians help Veterans manage serious conditions such as post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), anxiety, depression, panic disorders, and substance abuse disorder. These needs are both significant and widespread: 31% of veterans enrolled in VHA have a confirmed mental health diagnosis2, compared to 23.1%3 of U.S. adults. The stakes are also life-threatening—6,398 Veterans died by suicide in 2023 alone.4 Additionally, a substantial share of Veterans who have died by suicide had no prior mental health diagnosis.5 It is important that the VA invest in short term interventions and long term strategies to improve mental health outcomes and reduce suicide risk.

VHA mental health professionals are uniquely trained to address the complex needs of Veterans, with expertise in military culture, lethal means safety, combat-related trauma, and the impact of physical conditions such as traumatic brain injuries or amputations on an individual’s mental health. While community providers play an important role in the continuum of care, many do not possess the same level of Veteran-specific training and experience. In fact, the Government Accountability Office found that only 2 percent of community behavioral health providers receiving VA referrals had completed any of the VA’s core training courses in areas such as suicide prevention, opioid safety, and other Veteran-centric topics.6

Recent reporting and publicly available workforce data raise questions about the stability of VA's mental health workforce and the Department's ability to meet growing demand for behavioral health services.7 According to VA data8, since the beginning of the Trump Administration, the Department has lost over 300 psychologists and 700 social workers, some of whom also provide mental health counseling, even as mental health needs among veterans remain substantial.9 In fact, the Department reportedly lost about 200 psychiatrists in 2025 alone.10 In that same year, 57% percent of facilities reported severe psychology staffing shortages, making it the most frequently understaffed clinical occupation.11

The consequences for Veterans are evident. Staffing shortages have caused longer wait times, cancelled appointments, interrupted treatment, and the loss of trusted clinicians. Some Veterans report waiting multiple months for an available appointment and constantly having to rebuild their relationships with therapists from scratch as they are forced to switch between multiple therapists in succession. Therapists and Veterans also report being forced to replace one-on-one sessions with large group sessions, even when not clinically appropriate.12 This cycle of disruption has led some Veterans to give up treatment all together. One Veteran warned that losing access to their trusted therapist was a matter of “life or death.”13

These reported workforce shortages raise serious questions about the impact of recent staffing and workforce management decisions on Veterans' access to mental health care. Mental health clinicians have reported unmanageable caseloads, growing uncertainty about the future of their positions, and concerns that political directives around diversity, equity, and inclusion have made it more difficult to provide the highest quality care for their patients. This loss of hundreds of experienced clinicians—and the therapeutic relationships they built with veterans over years of care—cannot be quickly or easily replaced, even as the need for Veterans’ mental health services continues to grow.

Given these concerns regarding the adequacy and stability of VHA's mental health workforce, we request responses to the following questions by August 14, 2026:

Please provide, as of the date of this letter, the number of authorized positions, onboarded employees, vacancies, and vacancy rates nationwide for psychiatrists, psychologists, licensed clinical social workers, licensed professional mental health counselors, psychiatric mental health nurse practitioners, peer support specialists, and other direct-care behavioral health personnel.

Please provide equivalent data as of January 1st, 2025.

Please provide the information requested in Question 1 by Veterans Integrated Services Network (VISN) and facility. For each occupation, please also identify the number of positions that have been added, eliminated, or remained vacant during the past 24 months.

In total, how many mental health providers have separated from VA employment since January 20, 2025, including through resignation, retirement, deferred resignation, termination, or other separation? Please provide this information separated by occupation.

For 2026, what is the average time it takes to fill and onboard vacant mental health positions, by occupation?

Please provide the average and median wait times, by VISN and facility, for:

Initial mental health evaluations;

Initial individual appointments; and

Follow-up mental health appointments.

Please also include the type of provider, providing such care.

How many Veterans are currently awaiting outpatient mental health services, including individual psychotherapy, and what is the average length of time they have been waiting? What percentage of Veterans seeking mental health care are seen within VA’s established access standards?

Please provide the number and percentage of Veterans who waited more than 20, 30, 60, and 90 days for an initial individual mental health appointment during FY2025 and FY2026 to date.

Please provide the average and median wait times for Veterans referred to Community Care for outpatient mental health services during FY2026 and FY2025 to date for:

Initial community care mental health evaluations;

Initial individual appointments; and

Follow-up mental health appointments.

Please also include the type of provider, providing such care.

Among Veterans receiving ongoing outpatient mental health treatment, what percentage of Veterans changed mental health providers during the past 12 months? How many Veterans experienced interruption or termination of mental health treatment due to provider departure or vacancy?

How does the Department monitor continuity of care for veterans receiving ongoing mental health treatment? What policies or procedures are in place to ensure continuity of care for Veterans when providers leave the Department or positions remain unfilled?

What action is the Department taking to recruit and retain mental health providers in facilities experiencing persistent staffing shortages? Please describe any financial or non-financial incentives currently being used to improve recruitment and retention. What steps is the Department taking to address clinician workload, caseload size, burnout, and other workforce factors that may contribute to provider attrition?

What metrics does the Department use to assess whether workforce shortages are affecting veterans' access to care, continuity of care, clinical outcomes, suicide prevention efforts, and successful long-term clinical outcomes?

Has the Department conducted any recent internal evaluations, analyses, or assessments regarding the impact of mental health workforce shortages on veterans' access to care or mental health service delivery? If so, please provide copies of any reports, analyses, recommendations, or other relevant documents.

Given the persistent shortages of mental health professionals across the Department, it is critical that Congress understands the scope of these workforce challenges and the Department's efforts to address them.

Thank you for your cooperation with this request. We look forward to reviewing the information provided.

---
title: Rep. Chu Leads Colleagues in Requesting Information on Trump Administration Cuts to VA Behavioral and Mental Health Workforce

More housing grants, expanded loan financing for affordable housing

VIDEO from the construction site tour is available here

TRACY – Today, Rep. Josh Harder (CA-09) traveled to one of the fastest-growing communities in California with the Housing Authority County of San Joaquin to highlight how his bills that just became law will make it easier for families to own a home in the Valley. Harder toured the construction of an affordable housing project managed by the Housing Authority, met with local workers and developers, and discussed how his new laws will get more homes built and lower housing costs.

For decades, Washington looked the other way while the housing crisis grew worse:

California is short millions of homes, and more than half the state is cost-burdened, meaning they spend more than 30% of their income on rent.

Higher housing prices have pushed the median homebuying age to nearly 60 and the first-time homebuying age to 40, boxing out an entire generation from homeownership.

In San Joaquin County alone, families need to earn over $130,000 annually to afford a home, which is 40% higher than the county's average household income.

“One third of young adults are still living at home because we don’t have enough housing and prices are skyrocketing as a result,” said Rep. Harder. “That’s why I stood up to the gridlock in Washington and helped negotiate and pass the strongest housing package in half a century, which included my bills to get more homes built in the Valley. Finally being able to own a home is about to get easier for our families and the next generation.”

How Harder’s bills will unlock homeownership in the Valley:

New Federal Housing Grants – Harder’s Increasing Housing in Opportunity Zones Act authorizes the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to give priority to Opportunity Zone communities when awarding competitive housing grants.

Expanded Loan Financing for Affordable Housing – Harder’s Property Improvement and Manufactured Housing Loan Modernization Act increases limits on loans for manufactured homes and opens up new financing for ADUs, which offer families an early path to homeownership.

More Housing Projects Finished Faster and Cheaper – The broader package also includes provisions to cut paperwork, speed up environmental reviews, and reduce costly bureaucracy that drives up housing costs.

“For too long, we've approached the housing crisis by treating the symptoms instead of addressing the underlying barriers that make housing so difficult and expensive to build,” said Peter Ragsdale, Executive Director of the Housing Authority County of San Joaquin. “The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act is critical because it recognizes the need to produce more housing, reduce regulations that limit production, and invest in the communities that have been left behind. Congressman Harder’s legislation also expands financing for manufactured housing and other smaller housing options. There isn't a single solution to California's housing shortage. We need apartments, manufactured housing, and accessory dwelling units. Every housing type that provides quality, affordable, and desirable homes should be part of the solution.”

San Diego, CA – Today, Rep. Scott Peters convened business, labor, and community leaders to urge the Trump Administration to process Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) renewal applications in a timely manner. Delays at U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), which seem intentional and politically motivated, have slowed renewal processing time to almost double what it used to be.

“Nearly 9,000 DACA recipients call San Diego home. They work hard, pay taxes, and contribute tens of millions of dollars to our local economy every year. For many of them, the U.S. is the only home they’ve ever known,” Rep. Peters said. “I spoke out when Donald Trump attacked DACA the first time, but our work is not over. We need answers from this Administration about the never-ending delays at USCIS. How do they plan to address the backlog they created? Are DACA recipients being detained because of this lag?”

President Trump’s immigration policies have impacted the cost of healthcare, groceries, rent, and electricity. This is in part due to the delays in renewals which threaten the livelihoods of legal immigrants and put undue stress on businesses who are faced with uncertainty as their valued employees await decisions about their status. In San Diego alone, Dreamers, including DACA recipients, contribute $968 million annually to the local economy.

"Every day a DACA renewal sits in a backlog is a day a San Diego business risks losing one of its own employees," said Chris Cate, President & CEO, San Diego Regional Chamber of Commerce. "After more than a decade of temporary protections, it's time for Congress to deliver a permanent, bipartisan solution that gives Dreamers the stability they deserve and gives San Diego employers the certainty they need.”

“Delays in processing DACA renewals are inexcusable and negligent,” said Dr. Arcela Nunez-Alvarez, Co-Founder and Co-Director, Universidad Popular. “These delays expose applicants to unnecessary suffering, including loss of work authorization, income, health coverage, and educational opportunities, and most importantly, loss of immigration protection. The delays create an adverse domino effect, increasing vulnerability for applicants and their families.”

“For a small business barely making payroll, DACA renewal delays mean shorter hours, slower service, lost revenue, and thousands of dollars in turnover costs – money that should be going to wages, growth, and this community,” said Trevor Moore, Vice President, Cush Enterprises. “DACA recipients have done everything by the book their entire lives. They register with the federal government and ask permission to keep working and paying taxes. Our economy is nothing without the effort and loyalty of these people.”

"For 18 months, this Administration’s chaotic, capricious, and arbitrary approach to immigration enforcement has been fundamentally about sowing fear and disrupting our communities,” said Carol Kim, Executive Secretary-Treasurer, San Diego and Imperial Counties Labor Council. “It also disrupts the ability of anyone to do business and reliably work, not just the workers who are targeted, but every working person whose specific tasks or projects are derailed by disappearing coworkers, disappearing funding, and disappearing basic government functions. Every American who expects that work to come through pays the price, too.”

DACA must be renewed every two years, and work authorizations cannot be renewed until DACA status is renewed. Rep. Scott Peters’ office is seeing the highest volume of immigration casework requests during his time in Congress, driven by these mounting delays which affect our community and economy.

A livestreamed recording of the press conference can be viewed here. Additional photos from the event, courtesy of the office of Rep. Scott Peters, can be viewed here.

title: Rep. Peters, Businesses, and Labor Leaders Call on Trump Admin to Stop Stalling DACA Renewals

Washington, D.C. — Today, Representatives Valerie Foushee (NC-04), Deborah Ross (NC-02), and Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) introduced the Advancing International and Foreign Language Education Act to support foreign language and international education programs at colleges and universities by reauthorizing Title VI of the Higher Education Act. For decades, the Title VI/Fulbright-Hays programs have provided a strong foundation for international, research, and world language studies, especially in less commonly taught foreign languages that hold strategic importance for the United States.

Despite their proven importance, this administration has taken steps to undermine and dismantle these critical programs. The President’s Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Budget proposed zeroing out funding for international education programs at the Department of Education. The department has separately proposed eliminating the regulations governing Title VI and Fulbright-Hays, potentially allowing the administration to eliminate these programs entirely. The Higher Education Act has not been reauthorized since 2008.

The United States lags far behind European nations and other countries in foreign language proficiency, with approximately 10% of Americans speaking another language proficiently compared to 65% of Europeans. As demand grows for professionals with language skills and cross-cultural expertise in fields such as health, cybersecurity, and engineering, America’s competitiveness depends on our ability to communicate across languages and cultures.

“Keeping Americans prepared to enter the workforce must include access to foreign language education. Continuing to struggle to keep pace with other nations in language education will threaten our global leadership and our ability to equip the next generation with the proper tools to become civil leaders,” said Congresswoman Foushee. “I’m proud to work with Congresswoman Ross and Congressman Panetta on this legislation that will make critical investments in language education to ensure our nation’s continued leadership for years to come.”

“In Congress, I’m proud to represent world-renowned universities, colleges, and HBCUs, home to students driving cutting-edge research and innovation,” said Congresswoman Ross. “At a moment of unprecedented global competition, the United States cannot afford to fall behind in foreign language proficiency or international education. Yet the Trump administration has sought to eliminate funding for critical programs and attempted to dismantle key federal education funding entirely. It’s clear we must invest in the language and international education programs that strengthen our national security, expand opportunity, and keep America competitive.”

“Language education can broaden horizons and expand opportunities for Americans within our borders and beyond,” said Congressman Panetta. “As the co-chair of the America’s Languages Caucus, I’m proud to support the Advancing International and Foreign Language Education Act, which would extend language programs that are critical to building a workforce ready to compete around the world. By investing in language and international education programs today, we ensure our nation can continue leading the world and the global economy.”

Specifically, the Advancing International and Foreign Language Education Act would:

Reauthorize and extend programs for international and foreign language studies, including National Resource Centers, Language Resource Centers, Undergraduate International Studies, and American Overseas Research Centers.

Reauthorize Foreign Language and Area Studies Fellowships, allowing graduate students to receive stipends for studying foreign languages.

Extend and update the International Research and Innovation program, including establishing a national database on international and foreign language education.

Reauthorize and update programs for international business skills and education, including renaming and expanding activities in professional and technical training curricula.
title: Representatives Foushee, Ross, Panetta Introduce Legislation to Support Foreign Language and International Education Programs

Lafayette, CO — Yesterday, Colorado Congressman Joe Neguse and Senators Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper penned a letter opposing the proposed lease of U.S. Forest Service (USFS) lands in Routt and Moffat Counties to the Bureau of Land Management (BLM). In doing so they joined a number of local leaders who have similarly raised concerns about the Forest Service’s plans to lease nearly 14,000 acres of USFS lands to the BLM, a decision that would open the door to future oil and gas development in the area and could jeopardize critical wildlife habitats, sensitive watersheds, and outdoor recreational opportunities.

The Colorado lawmakers have been steadfast in their efforts to protect Colorado's public lands, teaming up to stop President Trump and Congressional Republicans’ plan to mandate the sale of millions of acres of public land across the American West through the budget reconciliation process, while also introducing landmark legislation like the CORE Act to establish new wilderness areas and safeguard outdoor recreation in these treasured landscapes.

Neguse, who has represented Routt County since 2023 and currently serves as the Ranking Member of the Federal Lands Subcommittee, also recently introduced a bill to protect the right of local communities to provide input into proposed oil and gas lease sales on national public lands. The Local Input Act restores the Department of the Interior’s discretion to incorporate public comments and defer nominated parcels that conflict with the public interest.

Changes enacted under the Trump administration last year effectively stripped local communities, landowners, and state and local officials of a meaningful voice in leasing decisions on public lands by eliminating BLM’s authority to defer lease parcels even if legitimate conflicts are identified.

The proposed federal oil and gas lease sale underwent a 30-day public comment period that began June 18 and ran through July 17. As the Colorado lawmakers have made clear, it’s imperative the administration considers local feedback.

Read their full letter HERE and below:

July 27, 2026

Forest Supervisor Dawn Laybolt

Medicine Bow-Routt National Forests and

Thunder Basin National Grassland

3838 Cherrywood East Loop

Laramie, WY 82070

Dear Forest Supervisor Laybolt,

We write to express our concern with the U.S. Forest Service (USFS)’s Routt National Forest Draft Environmental Assessment (EA), proposing to lease 10 parcels in northwest Routt and Moffat Counties in Colorado, to the Bureau of Land Management (BLM). The USFS has received Expressions of Interest to lease these 13,850 acres to the BLM for potential future oil and gas lease, exploration, and development, and initiated a public comment period last month.

Local leaders, including Routt County, members of the Steamboat Springs City Council, and the Western Resilience Center, have expressed concerns with this proposed lease. Six of the 10 parcels currently under consideration within the EA contain sensitive watersheds, and two contain cutthroat trout habitat. These proposed parcels also overlap significantly with habitat and migration corridors for elk, mule deer, Columbian sharp-tailed grouse, golden eagles, and more.

The proposed lease of these areas for future oil and gas development threatens to disrupt critical wildlife habitats and wildlife migrating and living throughout the region, in addition to degrading important watersheds. These parcels overlap with the California Park Special Interest Area, an area of critical ecological significance for Northwest Colorado and where there is active watershed restoration work underway in collaboration with the USFS.

These areas are also important for recreation, and the outdoor recreation economy is a significant economic driver for Routt County and the surrounding communities. Several existing multi-use trails overlap with the proposed parcels, in addition to areas that are valuable for hunting and fishing. Prior oil and gas development efforts within Routt County have historically not been economically viable or demonstrated commercial viability in the areas proposed for lease. We are concerned that this proposed action would significantly jeopardize the existing economic drivers for the region, including outdoor recreation.

We are also concerned that Routt County was not notified of this proposed action prior to the agency’s announcement. Any proposed leasing actions should be accompanied by significant and meaningful public and community engagement, including with the local jurisdictions that would be impacted.

As you consider the proposed lease of these lands to the BLM, we request you take full and fair consideration of the concerns raised by the impacted community and the highest and best use of these public lands.

Sincerely,

###
title: Neguse, Bennet, Hickenlooper Raise Concerns Over Forest Service Proposal to Lease Nearly 14,000 Acres for Potential Oil and Gas Development

Today, Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07) joined Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) and members of the House Democratic Women's Caucus (DWC) at a press conference with FWD.US and Families Belong Together, following their visit to the Dilley Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Detention Center. The oversight visit follows reports of inhumane treatment of children and families at the facility.

Congresswoman Fletcher’s press conference remarks as delivered:

Thanks so much, Congresswoman Ansari, and I join you in thanks for Congressman Castro and his entire team that have welcomed all of us to San Antonio and taken us to Dilley today. I am from just down the road, I'm Lizzie Fletcher from Houston, and am really grateful for the opportunity to be here today to witness myself what is happening in the great state of Texas and in the United States of America. And every American really needs to know what we saw at Dilley today and what we are seeing happening unfold in streets across this country, and so I'm grateful to everyone who's here, who's sharing this information. I’m grateful to FWD.US for the incredible work that they're doing to make sure that people don't look away from what we are seeing happening, and both of my colleagues have used the word, that if I had to have one takeaway from today, and one word, it is trauma.

The United States government is traumatizing individuals that it has in detention. I spent a lot of time today talking with some of the adults who were there, because there are families as well as a group of women who are detained at Dilley, and I spoke with women who've been there for eight months, who were picked up off the street while they were coming home from exercising. They had no idea why they were being picked up. They had no idea where they were going, and they have very little, if any, contact with anyone outside. They don't know what's happening with their asylum case. They don't know how long they'll be there. They don't know what's going to happen to them when they get out, and they're not getting any answers. They're not getting any information, and they're not getting any help, except from the people who are working so hard to share their stories and make sure that Americans know that this cannot go on. It cannot go on in our names. And what we see is these individual cases of trauma for the children and the families. But this immigration enforcement regime, ICE, and the Trump Administration are creating trauma not only for individuals, but they are terrorizing our communities, and they are creating trauma across our communities. And that's certainly true at my home in Houston, where, as all of you know, we recently saw ICE pursue someone who was not the target of an investigation, in unmarked vehicles, with plainclothes officers, trying to stop Lorenzo Araujo and detain the three men who were with him in his van after they shot and killed him in the street.

People in Houston are outraged, but they're also traumatized. This is a national trauma, and that's why people need to know what's happening, and people need to speak up and speak out wherever they are because this is being done in our names. This is being done by the United States government, and I think for most Americans, it is unimaginable, but it is also something, as Congressman Castro said, that has been hidden. It's been hidden because we are not getting information. This Congress is not conducting the oversight that it should be. That's why I'm so grateful to Congressman Castro and to the DWC for making sure that we are doing the oversight work that the majority in Congress is refusing to do, and we need to make sure that people across the country know, as Congresswoman Ansari said, by definition, no one at Dilley has a criminal record.

Americans are being lied to about what this administration is doing, who it's detaining, what's happening when it takes them into detention. They're not being honest with the people about how, and why, and what they are doing, and it has to stop. It absolutely has to stop. The detention that we see in Dilley and the trauma that we see in our communities, it doesn't serve the interests of the American people. It doesn't meet our values and our aspirations for who we are. I know that this is not who we are, and we all need to stand up in this moment to stop it. So again, I'm grateful to be with all these incredible fighters who are here, including my friend, and classmate, and colleague, an incredible fighter here from Boston, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley.

Texas holds the largest detained population of any state, averaging approximately 13,400 people per day in ICE custody as of mid-September 2025 across a rapidly expanding network of facilities. The ICE Detention Center in Dilley reopened in March 2025 after closing under the Biden Administration. Reports have revealed alarming conditions at Dilley, including poor food and water quality and serious health issues, including a measles outbreak and inadequate care for pregnant women.

Earlier this month, Congresswoman Fletcher joined 110 of her Democratic colleagues in an effort calling for the closure of the ICE Detention Center in Dilley. Since 2025, the Democratic Women’s Caucus has sent six oversight letters to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) calling out their mistreatment of pregnant detainees, insufficient healthcare accessibility, and violence against women.

To watch the press conference, click here.
title: ICYMI: Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher, Members of Congress Hold Press Conference Following Oversight Visit To Dilley ICE Detention Center
