Monterey, CA – Following disturbing reports that the Department of Defense removed the names of four American troops from the official Iran War death toll, United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) joined Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04) and 13 other fellow Democratic veterans in urging the Administration to accurately and transparently account for U.S. servicemembers killed and wounded in the Iran War.

“As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers,” wrote the lawmakers.

“The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran,” continued the lawmakers. “It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports. Inaccurate and delayed reports from the Department of War about U.S. casualties is bad for morale and undermines our U.S. servicemembers.”

Following public outcry, the Department of Defense quietly restored the names of the four U.S. servicemembers removed from the Iran War death toll over the weekend. The Administration has not provided an adequate explanation as to why the servicemembers were removed in the first place.

In addition to Panetta and Thompson, Reps. Pat Ryan (NY-18), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Derek Tran (CA-45), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Jason Crow (CO-06), Bobby Scott (VA-03), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), and Jared Golden (ME-02) signed the letter.

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear President Trump,

As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers.

The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports. Inaccurate and delayed reports from the Department of War about U.S. casualties is bad for morale and undermines our U.S. servicemembers.

We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.

Sincerely,

###
title: Rep. Panetta Joins Congressional Veterans in Demanding Transparency on Iran War Casualties

DOE Selects Five States for Future Nuclear Waste Depository Sites; Initiative Is Supported by $248 Million Secured by Rep. Levin

Washington, D.C.—Today, Rep. Mike Levin (CA-49) applauded the Department of Energy’s (DOE) announcement of five states to serve as potential sites for Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses. The Innovation Campuses are intended to house solutions for the nation’s nuclear waste challenges by supporting activities across the full nuclear fuel cycle, including fuel fabrication, enrichment, reprocessing used nuclear fuel, and disposal of used nuclear fuel.

Five states—Utah, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Louisiana, and Idaho—signed Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) with DOE to begin exploring how to officially become host sites for Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses. Once these Innovation Campuses are in full operation as envisioned, they will accept spent nuclear fuel from decommissioned nuclear plants like the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS).

Watch Rep. Levin’s video on the announcement here.

Rep. Levin’s statement on the announcement below:

“Today’s announcement of potential sites for Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses has been years in the making. It required tremendous bipartisan efforts where policymakers put aside politics and focused on a fix to our difficult nuclear waste challenges. Since my first day in Congress, I’ve prioritized finding solutions to safely remove and dispose of spent nuclear fuel, and today’s selection of states is a monumental step in the right direction. For years I have said that our actions must be based in collaboration with states and local communities, and for the first time in decades, states are raising their hands.

“But there is more work to be done. The hard part is still ahead of us. The federal government has a bad track record on nuclear waste and has not kept its promises to communities for many decades. As we know well, DOE was required by law to start picking up the waste from nuclear power plants like SONGS in 1998, but has fallen woefully behind. DOE must now be consistent, transparent, and honest with states as it completes the selection process for the Innovation Campuses and sets them up for success year after year, and administration after administration.

“I cannot underscore strongly enough that the Innovation Campuses must have solutions for the disposal of spent nuclear fuel if we are to be successful in this endeavor. Any development of new nuclear energy hinges on our country having a workable answer to the spent nuclear fuel challenge.

“Congress must now work in a bipartisan, bicameral fashion to authorize the Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses and write them into law with clear oversight, clear benchmarks, and clear connections to permanent disposal. This will ensure true accountability and real solutions. I will continue to work with the Administration and my congressional colleagues on both sides of the aisle to get this done.”

Since entering Congress in 2019, Rep. Levin has secured over $248 million for the safe removal and management of the nation’s spent nuclear fuel. In January 2026, he wrote to DOE Secretary Chris Wright urging the Department to establish a safe, effective, and long-term management program for spent nuclear fuel. Rep. Levin has also introduced the bipartisan Nuclear Waste Administration Act of 2024, which would modernize our country’s nuclear waste management program by establishing an independent Nuclear Waste Administration to manage the country’s nuclear waste. The safe management and removal of spent nuclear fuel out of SONGS and other decommission nuclear plants across the country remains a top priority for Rep. Levin.

Background on DOE’s Announcement of Potential Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses

The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced the selection of Utah, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Louisiana, and Idaho as potential host states for Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses, a new effort to strengthen and modernize the nation’s full nuclear fuel cycle. The campuses will attract significant investment, expand domestic manufacturing, and create thousands of new high-paying jobs in their respective regions.

The proposed campuses are designed to support activities across the full nuclear fuel lifecycle, including fuel fabrication, enrichment, reprocessing used nuclear fuel, and final disposition of used nuclear fuel. Depending on state priorities and regional capabilities, the campuses may also host advanced reactor deployment, power generation, advanced manufacturing, and co located data centers.

The proposed innovation campuses have the potential to attract up to $50 billion in capital investment, generate as much as $10 billion in state and local tax revenue, and create nearly 25,000 jobs with an establishment of a campus.

Earlier this year, DOE invited states to submit clear statements of interest and constructive feedback on the structure of the Innovation Campuses. In their submissions, states outlined how a campus would advance goals such as workforce development, infrastructure investment, economic diversification, or technology leadership and described the scope of activities they envision hosting. States submitted responses by April 1, 2026.

States that choose to pursue hosting an innovation campus will sign hosting agreements with the Department at a later date.

###
title: Rep. Mike Levin Applauds Selection of Potential Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses

HOUSTON, TX — Today, a federal judge ruled that the City of Houston's Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprise (MWBE) program is unconstitutional. In response, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) released the following statement, warning that the decision is the latest step in a broader effort to dismantle programs that level the playing field for minority- and women-owned businesses.

“This ruling is yet another step by far-right activists, like the lawyers who filed this case, fighting to erase every tool minority and women business owners use to compete on a level playing field,” said Rep. Menefee. “They’ve fought to end diversity programs in our colleges, at corporations, and in government contracts. It’s a shame, and The Supreme Court of the United States has cleared the way for it to happen in ending affirmative action and gutting the Voting Rights Act."

“We’ve seen the data showing that local governments across our region overwhelmingly contract with companies owned by white men,” continued Rep. Menefee. “The gaps in contracting are massive, and they are proof that minority and women business owners still face real barriers when they try to win public contracts. MWBE programs help close those gaps. They are not a favor or a handout.”

Studies conducted over the years, along with evidence presented in the case, show clear racial disparities in who receives contracts from local governments across the Houston area. During the trial, the City's expert witness testified that minority-owned businesses continue to lose out on city contracts, confirming ongoing racial disparities in the City's contracting process. Similarly, a 2020 study of Harris County government contracting found that the county awarded more than 90% of its contracting dollars over a three-year period to businesses owned by white men. These disparities are well documented and are the reason MWBE programs were created in the first place.
title: Congressman Menefee: Killing Minority Business Programs Hurts Every Houstonian

Newport, Kentucky — Yesterday, Congressmembers Gwen Moore (WI-04), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), and Morgan McGarvey (KY-03) visited Campbell County Detention Center in Kentucky to provide oversight of the facility and conduct a welfare check on three constituents suffering from a lack of medical care. The members heard from Anabell, Ricardo, and Octavio who have experienced inhumane conditions, lack of proper food to manage their well-being, delays in medication, and inadequate medical care.

Anabell is a constituent of Congresswoman Moore who suffered a miscarriage in ICE custody and was denied the necessary and adequate medical care.

Ricardo and Octavio are both residents of Illinois’ Third Congressional District who suffer from diabetes. Anabell is a constituent of WI-04 who suffered a miscarriage in ICE custody and was denied the necessary and adequate medical care.

“I visited Campbell County Detention Center in Kentucky with my colleagues, Representatives Ramirez and McGarvey, out of concern for my constituent, Anabell, and others who are suffering from medical neglect. I will continue honoring my oversight responsibilities and fighting for my constituents, wherever that might take me,” said Rep. Moore.

“As a member of Congress, I conducted oversight of the Campbell County Detention Center to check on my constituents, who are being denied needed medical care, including access to insulin. What I saw inside was devastating, and the lack of medical care was appalling: detainees pleading for help, medicine for purchase at the commissary, sickeningly inhumane conditions, and jail leadership attempting to gaslight us,” said Rep. Ramirez. “DHS continues to demonstrate gross disregard of our health, dignity, personhood, and safety. It is clear: We must end detention, dismantle DHS, and MELT ICE!”

“What we saw yesterday is exactly why Congressional oversight matters. We talked to diabetics who told us they can’t get their medicine and detainees who said they can’t get so much as an aspirin, all while the Trump administration has given ICE billions in taxpayer money. I’m grateful to Reps. Ramirez and Moore for coming to Kentucky, and we will continue holding this administration accountable,” said Rep. McGarvey.

“As a Sister of Mercy of the Americas, I stand with Rep. Ramirez and Rep. Moore as they conduct an oversight visit at the Campbell County Detention Center. My Mercy sisters and I have devoted our lives to helping immigrants, women and children, and we are devastated by the cruel, inhumane treatment of our immigrant brothers and sisters by ICE. We call on all people of faith and goodwill to join us in standing ups for our immigrant neighbors, friends and family members,” said Sister Carren Herring, RSM of Cincinnati, Ohio.

The oversight visit comes as new ICE data shows that immigrant detention remains at a record high, with 65,765 detained immigrants, and over 20 deaths documented in detention during the first half of 2026. According to data, primary causes include delayed and denied medical care.

According to DHS’s data, despite the increase in the detained population, medical claims decreased by nearly $300 million from 2024 to 2025, reflecting both unpaid bills and detainees who may never have received care. On October 3, 2025, the VA suddenly terminated its agreement with ICE to process medical claims, leaving ICE with no capabilities to continue paying for off-site medical care for detainees, including prescription medications for individuals in ICE custody. From October to May, at least 29 people died in detention.
title: Moore, Ramirez, McGarvey Visit Constituents with Health Concerns at Campbell County Detention Center

“The world is watching as the Trump administration separates immigrant families, destroys the lives of children and parents, and locks them away without due process or access to adequate water, food, education, and medical care,” said Congresswoman Pressley in a statement. “What we witnessed in this facility was harrowing and horrific. I leave today clear as ever that Congress must close Dilley, end the practice of family detention, and abolish ICE now. We must put an end to Trump and ICE’s campaign of terror, and keep fighting for dignity, humanity, and freedom for every single one of our neighbors.”

“Today, I met again with the children and families being detained in Dilley. For months I have been visiting Dilley, where there still remains no access to proper medical care, food, or education. Despite repeated and continued calls from myself, my colleagues, and our communities demanding, this cruel and inhumane treatment continues. The children and families being held at Dilley must be freed and the center closed immediately.” – said Rep. Joaquin Castro (TX-20)

“What we saw today at Dilley was nothing short of horrific. No child, woman, or family should be locked up like this. We must close Dilley now and release these families. Children are being jailed and traumatized while private contractors profit from it, all at the expense of American taxpayers.” – said Rep. Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03)

“Every American needs to know what we saw at the ICE Detention Center in Dilley today because it is the opposite of what we say we stand for as Americans. What we saw when we went to the facility to conduct oversight was desperation and indefinite detention for some—many women waiting for months and months with no information about their cases. By definition, no one at Dilley has a criminal record, but there we spoke with women who had little contact with the world outside, little information, and little hope. They are experiencing trauma while the rest of the country goes on without insight into their conditions or their cases because the U.S. government is not being honest with the American people about what, how, and why it is doing what it is doing. It must stop. This mass detention of women, children, and families does not serve the interests of the American people and does not represent who we are or aspire to be as a people.” – said Rep. Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07)

“ICE is being increasingly secretive about their actions at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center. We were only allowed to speak to one child out of 112 children – and even that interaction was cut short.ICE is traumatizing over 500 individuals – including pregnant women, children, and infants as young as 2 months old – and subjecting them to inhumane conditions for extended periods of time. These individuals should be living their lives, welcoming their newborn children, playing with their friends, and raising their families outside of ICE detention. The Trump Administration must be held accountable for the trauma it is inflicting on immigrant families. Children should not be detained, and I am continuing to call for the Dilley Detention Facility to be shut down, immediately.” – Rep. Luz Rivas

“The inhumane conditions at Dilley are well-documented and we must end family detention. This includes shutting down Dilley and releasing these children and families immediately. Dilley lacks basic necessities for anyone, especially children: no access to clean water, medical care, or proper education. Dilley reflects a broader pattern that should not be expanded with additional, unprecedented taxpayer funding. Yet, Congress has committed more than $260 billion to expand enforcement, on top of the regular appropriations to ICE and CBP of roughly $30 billion for FY25. This will only cause irreparable harm to children and communities. Thank you to the Members who continue to call for the release of families and we join them in their calls for Dilley’s closure.” – said Todd Schulte, President of FWD.us, at the press conference.

Transcript: Rep. Pressley’s Remarks Following Oversight Inspection of Dilley ICE Detention Center

San Antonio, TX

July 28, 2026

My name is Ayanna Pressley. I’m a Congresswoman representing the Massachusetts Seventh congressional district, which includes the city of Boston, also home to the third largest Haitian diaspora in the country. And so I’ve been on the front lines of this, these grave injustices in many ways.

I do want to also just commend Congressman Castro and his entire team, and Fwd.us, for your vigilance.

It’s so important that we not normalize this. It’s so important that we not acquiesce to this.

This, this fascist administration, this dictator in the Oval Office—history has shown us time again appeasement does not work. The only way to beat a dictator is with defiance. The only way to beat fascism is to refuse to accept this segregated, divided, dark, dystopian view that they have for our country. To reject it as an inevitability.

So we have to resist, reject, condemn at every turn, and shine a light.

And so I’m so grateful for the leadership of Congressman Castro. This is his eighth oversight visit to the Dilley detention facility.

I want to do some quick level setting here. So, and please correct me if my notes were inaccurate. So there are currently 539 individuals, 84 families. 50 out of those 84 families are male, head of household. 16 are female, head of household, and then there are 18 that are dual. There are also four pregnant women.

And I want to correct the record because earlier I said when we first came out of Dilley after our, after our oversight visit that they characterized all the detainees as low-level non-violent criminals. That’s inaccurate. They characterize them as low-level non-criminals.

That’s how they were all—that’s, that’s how, when we were getting our orientation and asking our questions of the officers, that’s how they characterize the detainees: low-level non-criminals.

So it seems their only crime is that they exist?

These are law-abiding people that are our neighbors, people we love, we live next to, we work and worship with, who were just going about their lives and met with such an aggressive disruption that they will be recovering from for the rest of their lives.

And I also just want to say that this these are two sides of a very evil for-profit coin. I have worked my entire life to dismantle mass incarceration, and I need people to understand that if you are outraged by the number of Black and low-income people that are incarcerated, the same for-profit system is driving the unlawful detainment and deportation of our immigrant neighbors.

CoreCivic is worth over a billion dollars, so this for-profit infrastructure, this for-profit evil, is for child abuse. They are for child neglect. They are for childhood trauma. They are for family separation.

One of the young women that I met with—and I have to say, every time I leave a detention facility, I am conflicted. Because I want to uplift these stories, but I don’t want to further endanger anyone. And I know very often when we leave these facilities, they are met with great hostility, and I don’t want to put them in any more harm’s way.

But one young woman that I met with, 30 years old, she is the mother of two children, a five-year-old girl and a three-year-old girl.

She fell into my arms within a matter of seconds, sharing with me that she was unable to wish her five-year-old daughter a happy birthday.

She also talked to me about how she arrived, how she ended up there. She was delivering packages. She’s a delivery driver, and there was a problem with her hazards. So she pulled over her car and had the lights blinking while she went in to deliver the package.

When she came out, law enforcement was there. They asked for an ID. She said, you know, “Why?” But she provided it. It was a Mexico ID. So this young lady, this 30-year-old young woman, she was here on a tourist visa from Mexico. Her mother, who brought her here at the age of four years old, developed cancer and died. So she’s been living here since the age of four, working, law-abiding.

She fell into an abusive relationship, and there were many, many times that the police were called on her husband, who was a violent abuser, and she is so upset because that abuser currently has the custody of her children.

So here she is, someone who is a survivor of domestic violence, law-abiding, making positive contributions, an incredible mom, and she asked me, “My husband was released on a bond of $150 after he beat me for hours and even tried to run me over with his car, and I was told that if I wanted to bond out, I would need to pay $9,000, and I’ve committed no crime.”

I asked her if her faith is some of what keeps her strong in this moment, and she said, “My faith in God is being tested every day. My faith in this country.”

And then just as I close this, I want to say, so many of the detainees that I have met, whether I was in Louisiana or Texas or in Massachusetts, they are some of the greatest patriots you will ever meet.

They love this country, and they are making positive, they have been making positive contributions to it every day, and it is a great betrayal.

And you see that. You see that betrayal in their eyes. You see the vacancy in their eyes. You see the trauma in their eyes.

So Dilley must be shut down. We have to abolish ICE, and then I’m going to take it one step further and say, any of those agents that have contributed to and caused the injury, the harm, and even fatalities, they must also be held accountable. And we should abolish qualified immunity for these federal law enforcement officers. There must be some recourse and some restitution.

And with that, we’ll now turn it over to another incredible member and colleague in the Democratic Women’s Caucus. Again, this is a joint oversight visit with Congressman Castro and the women of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, Rep Rivas.
title: WATCH: Pressley Tours Dilley ICE Detention Center, Renews Her Demands for Its Immediate Closure & the Release of Families

Washington, D.C. – In response to hazardous cases of autonomous vehicles (AV) blocking emergency responders from helping people in danger, driving through construction zones, failing during power outages, and contributing to large-scale traffic jams, U.S. Rep. Kevin Mullin (CA-15) is introducing the AV Emergency Response Coordination Act.

Rep. Mullin announced the bill at a joint press conference in San Francisco alongside Mayor Daniel Lurie, Fire Department Chief Dean M. Crispen, Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety President Cathy Chase, Police Chief Derrick Lew, San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency Director Julie Kirschbaum, San Francisco County Transportation Authority Executive Director Tilly Chang and Department of Emergency Management Deputy Director Adrienne Bechelli.

The bill would direct the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) to establish minimum safety standards and protocols requiring AV operators to improve how they work with local public safety personnel.

“Seconds count during a crisis, and we’ve seen too many terrifying incidents of AVs interfering with police, fire fighters, and paramedics. Public officials have been asked to be guinea pigs in figuring out how to interact with this emerging technology. AV companies have to do better. While it is exciting that the Bay Area is leading the nation in autonomous vehicle innovation, recent disruptions like widespread power outages or the holiday traffic fiasco on Fourth of July in San Francisco, have shown how malfunctions can hamper emergency response,” said Rep. Mullin. “Autonomous vehicles have tremendous potential to improve safety on our roads, but federal regulators need to make sure they’re not inadvertently getting in the way of emergency responders and that public officials are able to quickly work with AVs in an emergency.”

The list of incidents involving emergency responders is mounting in cities across the United States where driverless vehicles are operating, including in Austin, Pheonix, Las Vegas, Dallas, San Francisco and others. Across these locations, there have been reports of AVs obstructing ambulances and paramedics, driving into active crime scenes, blocking fire trucks, and failing to recognize basic safety conditions like flashing lights, flares, smoke, and traffic cones. AV companies are also not providing sufficient information and training to emergency responders to ensure the safety of vehicle occupants, pedestrians, and other road users when there are collisions, malfunctions, and other incidents involving AVs.

Rep. Mullin’s AV Emergency Response Coordination Act is the first legislation of its kind to directly address this issue, which has bipartisan interest. The Trump Administration’s NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison recently sent a letter to AV companies demanding that they address the issue of AVs interfering with first responders and law enforcement.

Specifically, the AV Emergency Response Coordination Act would:

Require AV companies to provide clear, standardized emergency response protocols for first responders;

Establish a 24/7 hotline for public officials to communicate directly with AV companies during autonomous vehicle incidents;

Direct NHTSA to develop minimum national emergency response standards across AV operators; and

Create a process for public officials to issue “geofence notices” so that AVs avoid certain areas during an emergency or while there is an ongoing safety hazard.

“Emergency responders must be able to reach people in danger or distress without being delayed or obstructed by autonomous vehicles (AV). The AV Emergency Response Coordination Act would establish much-needed, commonsense federal standards for coordination between AV companies and emergency personnel. Advancing innovation cannot threaten public safety. We commend Rep. Kevin Mullin for introducing this important legislation and urge Congress to enact it,” said Cathy Chase, president of Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety.

“San Francisco is the global center of innovation, and we’ve been on the cutting edge of autonomous vehicles and street safety. Because we were one of the first cities to welcome autonomous vehicles at scale, we have learned more than almost any other city about how they operate in a dense, complex urban environment,” said San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie. “This legislation will help keep San Franciscans safe while taking the lessons we’ve learned to the rest of the country. My number one priority is public safety, and I want to thank Congressman Mullin for his leadership in supporting our first responders so they can do that critical work.”

“A top priority of the San Francisco Fire Department is ensuring that our personnel can respond quickly and safely to emergencies. During several recent large-scale events we have experienced challenges involving autonomous vehicles. We have been working closely with AV companies and welcome this technology, provided it is deployed in a manner that supports public safety and emergency response operations. We appreciate Representative Mullin introducing thoughtful legislation that will move our mission of public safety forward,” said San Francisco Fire Department Chief Dean M. Crispen.

“I want to thank Congressman Kevin Mullin for his leadership and his steadfast commitment to ensuring public safety as autonomous vehicle technology continues to evolve,” said San Francisco County Transportation Authority Chair and District 7 Supervisor Myrna Melgar. “This timely legislation recognizes that advancing innovation must be matched by strong standards for emergency management and preparedness. The San Francisco County Transportation Authority looks forward to working alongside Congressman Mullin, our public safety partners, and the autonomous vehicle industry to ensure first responders have the tools, information, and coordination they need to protect our communities.”

Rep. Mullin has prioritized strengthening oversight and transparency around the development of driverless cars, including previously introducing the AV Safety Data Act, which would require companies to collect and report key safety data to NHTSA. He has also authored several letters urging the agency to require more comprehensive reporting on AV operations, safety incidents, and performance data.

A copy of the full AV Emergency Response Coordination Act text can be found here.

###
title: Rep. Mullin Introduces Bill to Standardize Autonomous Vehicles Protocol During Emergencies

Three bipartisan bills backed by Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) were voted out of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce last week, and now head to the House floor for a vote before the full House of Representatives.

Pappas introduced the bipartisan, bicameral Combating Illicit Xylazine Act with Rep. Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), which would list xylazine as a Schedule III controlled substance and give law enforcement the tools they need to go after traffickers while protecting the drug’s legal use by veterinarians, farmers, and ranchers. Xylazine, also known as “tranq,” is an easily accessible veterinary tranquilizer that is being used as a low-cost cutting agent for fentanyl.

Pappas cosponsors Tyler’s Law, bipartisan legislation designed to prevent fentanyl overdoses in the United States. This bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to complete a study on how frequently hospitals test for fentanyl when a patient is experiencing an overdose. Based on these results, the bill instructs HHS to issue guidance to hospitals on implementing fentanyl testing in emergency rooms.

“As we work to combat the ongoing addiction epidemic, we have to make progress across the board on this issue. We must ensure our law enforcement has the resources they need to stop drug trafficking and that our health care centers have the resources for care and recovery,” said Congressman Pappas. “These bills would do that and should be swiftly brought to the floor for a vote.”

Pappas cosponsors the Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act of 2025, legislation to streamline the outdated prior authorization process in Medicare Advantage (MA). With nearly 33 million Americans enrolled in Medicare Advantage, the bill updates a system that has become a top administrative burden for providers and a barrier to timely care. Audits by the HHS Inspector General have found that Medicare Advantage plans subjected enrollees to unnecessary delays, incorrectly denied medically necessary care, and ultimately approved 75% of requests that were initially denied.

“This legislation is about cutting red tape and fixing systems that aren’t working so that seniors can access the care they need when they need it and physicians can focus on their patients, not paperwork,” said Congressman Pappas. “It’s commonsense and it’ll make a real difference for folks in New Hampshire and across the country.”

Background:

The Combating Illicit Xylazine Act would:

Schedule xylazine as Schedule III illicit substance under the Controlled Substances Act;

Ensure veterinarians, farmers, and ranchers can still use the drug for its intended purpose by creating a clear definition of “ultimate user” — someone lawfully permitted to possess a controlled substance for legitimate use;

Enable the DEA to track its manufacturing to ensure it is not diverted to the illicit market; and

Require a report on prevalence, risks, and recommendations regarding xylazine.

The bill is endorsed by 41 state attorneys general, major law enforcement organizations, and veterinary organizations. The Combating Illicit Xylazine Act previously passed the House with overwhelming bipartisan support.

Tyler’s Law is named in memory of Tyler Shamash, a 19-year-old boy who died following a fentanyl ingestion in 2018. He was not tested for fentanyl after being brought to the hospital with a suspected overdose. His mother, Juli, is an advocate for this legislation and is sharing Tyler’s story to prevent others from experiencing the same tragedy. Still to this day, many emergency rooms do not include fentanyl in their drug screenings. According to HHS, fentanyl-related deaths have skyrocketed 103-fold in the United States from 1999–2023. Adding fentanyl testing to emergency room drug screenings could save countless lives. A full list of endorsing organizations is here.

The Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act of 2025 would:

Require MA plans to adopt an electronic prior authorization (e-PA) system with standardized transaction;

Improve transparency around MA Prior Authorization use and requirements;

Clarify HHS’ authority to set timelines for determinations, including real-time decisions for routine items; and

Mandate HHS and other agencies report on oversight and further improvements to the e-PA process

In the 117th and 118th Congresses, this legislation was endorsed by more than 500 organizations representing patients, providers, medical technology innovators, biopharmaceutical companies, and health plans.
title: Three Pappas-Backed Bipartisan Bills to Fight the Addiction Crisis and Improve Care for Seniors Advance Out of Committee

WASHINGTON — Following reports that the Department of Defense removed the names of four American troops from the official Iran War death toll, Congressman Jared Golden (ME-02) and 14 fellow Democratic veterans are urging the Trump Administration to accurately and transparently account for U.S. servicemembers killed and wounded in the Iran war.

“As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers,” the lawmakers wrote in a letter to President Trump.

“The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports,” they continued. “We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.”

The letter was led by Congressman Mike Thompson (CA-14). Golden was joined on the letter by Reps. Pat Ryan (NY-18), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Derek Tran (CA-45), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Jason Crow (CO-06), Bobby Scott (VA-03), Salud Carbajal (CA-24) and Gil Cisneros (CA-31).

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear President Trump,

As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers.

The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports. Inaccurate and delayed reports from the Department of War about U.S. casualties is bad for morale and undermines our U.S. servicemembers.

We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.

Sincerely,

###
title: Golden, Democratic veterans demand transparency on Iran war casualties

Washington, DC – Today, Representatives Ro Khanna (CA-17) and Anna Paulina Luna (FL-13) introduced the No Campaign Funded Cover-Ups Act to prohibit candidates for federal office and federal officeholders from using campaign contributions or legal expense funds to cover costs related to sexual assault, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment claims. By requiring more detailed reporting of campaign-related legal expenses, the bill will also give the public greater transparency into how political funds are being used.

"Survivors must be heard and respected,” said Congressman Ro Khanna. “Our bipartisan legislation addresses a basic principle: money donated to support a political campaign should not become a personal legal-defense fund for alleged sexual misconduct. Our bill will increase public transparency and help prevent attempts to silence those who come forward about abuse.”

“Those who seek or hold federal office must be held to the highest standard of accountability,” said Congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna. “If a candidate is accused of sexual assault, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, campaign donations and legal expense funds should never become a personal bailout. If you commit sexual misconduct, you should foot the bill, not the donors who put their trust in you.”

"Across the country, too many powerful men are relying on the silence of women to win elections or cling to power. This bill sends a strong message: no more campaign funded cover ups," said Cheyenne Hunt, Executive Director, Reckoning Action. "Standing with survivors is not a partisan issue. We were proud to work with Rep. Khanna and Rep. Luna to ensure survivor experiences were centered throughout this process."

Specifically, the legislation will:

Prohibit campaign and legal defense funds from paying legal fees to defend against such claims.

Ban those funds from paying settlements or court-ordered judgments arising from such claims.

Prohibit payments for private investigators or opposition research intended to investigate or uncover damaging information about a person who brought a claim.

Apply these restrictions to payments made during the two years before the law’s enactment. Require campaigns to disclose more information about all legal expenses, including the recipient, amount, date, purpose, type of legal payment, and whose expenses were covered.

###
title: Reps. Khanna and Luna Introduce the No Campaign Funded Cover-Ups Act

Washington, DC - Last week, Congressman Shri Thanedar urged greater transparency from the heads of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) regarding the recent surge in cyclosporiasis cases. In a letter to Dr. Kyle Diamantas and Dr. Jay Bhattacharya, Acting Commissioner of the FDA and Acting Director of the CDC respectively, Thanedar laid out the public health threat posed by cyclosporiasis and called on the officials to improve efforts to keep the public informed.

“The American public deserves accurate information about potential public health risks and the confidence that every possible step is being taken to identify the cause of these illnesses, prevent future infections, and ensure access to appropriate treatment,” wrote Congressman Thanedar. “We are urging the FDA and CDC to continue working closely with state health departments and local public health agencies to strengthen food safety measures, improve outbreak detection, and identify all other sources as immediately feasible. The FDA should continue to collaborate with the CDC to invest in the Cyclospora Prevention, Response, and Research Action Plan to support research on prevention, detection, treatment, and improved surveillance of cyclosporiasis.”

Cyclospora outbreaks have increased across America over the past year, but Michigan, especially Southeast Michigan, has been the hardest hit for cyclosporiasis cases in the country. As of July 23, 2026, Michigan has experienced 8,176 reported cases since late June 2026, with 160 hospitalizations.

Congressman Shri Thanedar was joined on this letter by Congressman Eric Sorensen, Congressman Joaquin Castro, Congressman Tom Suozzi, Congresswoman Nanette Díaz Barragán, Congressman Chuy García, Congressman Gil Cisneros, and Congresswoman Sarah McBride. The full text of the letter can be viewed here.

Congressman Shri Thanedar proudly represents Michigan's 13th Congressional District, which includes Detroit, Downriver, and the Grosse Pointes. As a champion for working families, Shri is committed to advancing economic opportunities, education, healthcare access, and entrepreneurship for underserved communities. Drawing from his journey from poverty to success, he works tirelessly to uplift Metro Detroit, ensuring every resident has the resources and support they need to thrive.

Washington, D.C. — Today, Representatives Deborah Ross (NC-02), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), and Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) introduced the Advancing International and Foreign Language Education Act to support foreign language and international education programs at colleges and universities by reauthorizing Title VI of the Higher Education Act. For decades, the Title VI/Fulbright-Hays programs have provided a strong foundation for international, research, and world language studies, especially in less commonly taught foreign languages that hold strategic importance for the United States.

Despite their proven importance, this administration has taken steps to undermine and dismantle these critical programs. The President’s Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Budget proposed zeroing out funding for international education programs at the Department of Education. The department has separately proposed eliminating the regulations governing Title VI and Fulbright-Hays, potentially allowing the administration to eliminate these programs entirely. The Higher Education Act has not been reauthorized since 2008.

The United States lags far behind European nations and other countries in foreign language proficiency, with approximately 10% of Americans speaking another language proficiently compared to 65% of Europeans. As demand grows for professionals with language skills and cross-cultural expertise in fields such as health, cybersecurity, and engineering, America’s competitiveness depends on our ability to communicate across languages and cultures.

“In Congress, I’m proud to represent world-renowned universities, colleges, and HBCUs, home to students driving cutting-edge research and innovation,” said Congresswoman Ross. “At a moment of unprecedented global competition, the United States cannot afford to fall behind in foreign language proficiency or international education. Yet the Trump administration has sought to eliminate funding for critical programs and attempted to dismantle key federal education funding entirely. It’s clear we must invest in the language and international education programs that strengthen our national security, expand opportunity, and keep America competitive.”

“Keeping Americans prepared to enter the workforce must include access to foreign language education. Continuing to struggle to keep pace with other nations in language education will threaten our global leadership and our ability to equip the next generation with the proper tools to become civil leaders,” said Congresswoman Foushee. “I’m proud to work with Congresswoman Ross and Congressman Panetta on this legislation that will make critical investments in language education to ensure our nation’s continued leadership for years to come.”

“Language education can broaden horizons and expand opportunities for Americans within our borders and beyond,” said Congressman Panetta. “As the co-chair of the America’s Languages Caucus, I’m proud to support the Advancing International and Foreign Language Education Act, which would extend language programs that are critical to building a workforce ready to compete around the world. By investing in language and international education programs today, we ensure our nation can continue leading the world and the global economy.”

Specifically, the Advancing International and Foreign Language Education Act would:

Reauthorize and extend programs for international and foreign language studies, including National Resource Centers, Language Resource Centers, Undergraduate International Studies, and American Overseas Research Centers.

Reauthorize Foreign Language and Area Studies Fellowships, allowing graduate students to receive stipends for studying foreign languages.

Extend and update the International Research and Innovation program, including establishing a national database on international and foreign language education.

Reauthorize and update programs for international business skills and education, including renaming and expanding activities in professional and technical training curricula.
title: Ross, Foushee, Panetta Introduce Legislation to Support Foreign Language and International Education Programs

Leads Congressional Oversight Visit with Democratic Women’s Caucus

Hollywood Stars Mark Ruffalo, Ms. Rachel, Ilana Glazer, Busy Philipps, Cynthia Nixon, Jessica Alba, Ximena Sariñana Join Push

DILLEY, TX — Today, Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) and members of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, including Reps. Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), and Luz Rivas (CA-29) conducted a congressional oversight visit to the Dilley Trailer Prison in South Texas. Actors Mark Ruffalo, Ilana Glazer, Busy Philipps, Cynthia Nixon, Jessica Alba, Ximena Sariñana and prominent educator Ms. Rachel joined the push to shut down Dilley. In addition, countless lawmakers joined the push on social media, highlighting a letter signed by 111 House Democrats from earlier this month calling for the closure of the facility.

Watch press conference here.

The group was joined by Dr. Anita K. Patel, MD, critical care specialist and associate professor of pediatrics in Washington, D.C., for a press conference in San Antonio, where Congressman Castro delivered the following remarks:

Thank you for your incredible work in bringing the nation's attention to the horrors at the Dilley Detention Center, what I call the Dilley Trailer Prison. It's an honor to be here today and to have inspected Dilley today with members of the Democratic Women's Caucus who have joined us in San Antonio and in Dilley for this inspection, and also with Dr. Patel, a pediatrician who has been very outspoken about the lasting trauma, both physical and mental, to the children, especially who were imprisoned at Dilley.

Recently, as many of you know, there were 110 of us in Congress who came together to demand that the Dilley Detention Center be shut down. We know that it's possible because it's been done before, during the Biden Administration.

The trauma, physical and mental, on those children will be harsh and long-lasting. Every single day that a child spends in Dilley, they are traumatized. And over the past several months—this was the seventh time that I've been to Dilley—I've seen it in their faces, as some of them are stone-faced, others are sobbing and clinging to their parents or begging to get out. The parents themselves are often despondent. There are just very sad and horrible stories about medical care that's either denied or delayed, legal processes that people are not only unfamiliar with but also, they're in legal limbo.

Remember, this is a system where you have young kids who will sometimes have to represent themselves in front of judges in court. Something that in the United States even a convicted killer doesn't have to do, because they get legal representation. And so today it was no different.

Unfortunately, the numbers at Dilley have gone up. There are now more than 500 people there. The last time we were there, the numbers were probably about 100 less. There are now more children there than there were before. They were 96 in May. They're now at 112. I believe that is the result of the ICE surge that we've seen over the last month or so. We've seen these raids on the street, we've seen families that have been torn apart on the street and brutality on the street. The result of that is that more families and more children are now imprisoned at Dilley.

Remember, every time a child is put into the Dilley detention center, somebody in America makes more money. We have commodified child imprisonment in our nation. CoreCivic is a private prison company whose investors include some of the largest asset managers in this country. That includes asset managers that manage firefighter pension funds and public teacher pension funds and so forth. They are making money. The more kids that are put in Dilley.

And then finally, a few quick stories because I told you there was incredible human trauma. I talked to a woman who had recently had a heart procedure done. She had had heart trouble before she went to Dilley, and then when she was there, it worsened. She had a heart procedure done, a kind of operation, and she was not given the follow-up appointment that she was supposed to have—she was not given the proper medication that she was supposed to have because of that heart situation.

We talked to another young woman, who a 16-year-old girl actually who was there with her father. She spoke about spending two days at the San Antonio Processing Center, Crosspoint. She mentioned that in that room where people are detained, that there are cameras that can see the entire room, and not only is there a camera in the main room, there's a camera that's pointed at the place where people use the restroom. That's how dehumanizing the situation is for folks.
title: Castro Continues Push to Shut Down the Dilley Trailer Prison

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Maryland Congressional Delegation members – Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05), U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (both D-MD)< and U.S. Representatives Kweisi Mfume (MD-07), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Glenn Ivey (MD-04), Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), April McClain Delaney (MD-06), and Johnny Olszewski (MD-02) – are calling on the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to take action to ensure Marylanders are not forced to bear skyrocketing electricity costs due to increasing energy demand from data centers located outside of the state. The lawmakers urged FERC to require PJM Interconnection (PJM) to implement strong protections that would ensure fair energy costs for Marylanders after PJM, the grid operator responsible for coordinating electricity transmission in the region, assigned roughly $2 billion in costs to Maryland ratepayers for infrastructure that is needed primarily to serve out-of-state data centers. The lawmakers’ letter supports a complaint at FERC filed by the Maryland Office of People’s Counsel challenging PJM’s existing transmission cost allocation rules.

“As members of the Maryland Congressional Delegation, we write regarding a pressing matter that has the potential to significantly raise energy costs for our constituents. PJM Interconnection LLC’s (PJM) existing transmission cost allocation rules result in the unjust assignment of billions of dollars in costs to Marylanders, contributing to unaffordable electricity bills,” the lawmakers begin.

On the rising costs of electricity due to data centers outside of Maryland, the lawmakers write, “Data centers being built outside of Maryland are driving one of the largest transmission expansions in PJM’s history. Across its three most recent regional transmission planning rounds, PJM has advanced $22 billion in projects needed principally to serve data centers. Under PJM’s current cost allocation rules, roughly $2 billion of those costs have been assigned to Maryland ratepayers rather than the data centers that are driving the demand.”

“Marylanders are already shouldering the immense burden of skyrocketing electricity costs, and it is unjust and unreasonable to force our constituents to subsidize the energy infrastructure needs of the wealthiest companies in the world. Unless the Commission acts, our constituents will pay an estimated $1.6 billion on their electric bills over the next ten years for these projects alone, and $823 million of that total cost will fall on residential customers, which equates to roughly $345 for the average customer,” the lawmakers continue.

On PJM’s current cost allocation rules, the Maryland lawmakers note, “PJM’s cost allocation rules have not kept pace with the build out of hyperscale data centers, just one of which can equal the electricity demand of a small city. PJM’s current rules spread costs broadly across the region regardless of where, and for whom, the underlying projects are actually needed. Maryland regulators have no ability to assign such costs to data centers located in other states, and with tens of thousands of megawatts of additional data center demand growth projected across PJM over the next two decades, our constituents face billions of dollars in further charges absent Commission action to address this unjust and unreasonable cost allocation. Furthermore, because much of the forecasted growth in data center energy demand is speculative, our constituents bear the unacceptable risk of paying for projects built to serve potential data centers that are never built due to any number of external reasons.”

“We urge the Commission to act expeditiously to provide relief from these costs for Maryland ratepayers, including as requested in OPC’s complaint. Thank you for your consideration of this important issue that is essential to ensuring just and reasonable energy costs for our constituents,” the lawmakers conclude.

The full text of the letter is available here and below.

Dear Chairman Swett,

As members of the Maryland Congressional Delegation, we write regarding a pressing matter that has the potential to significantly raise energy costs for our constituents. PJM Interconnection LLC’s (PJM) existing transmission cost allocation rules result in the unjust assignment of billions of dollars in costs to Marylanders, contributing to unaffordable electricity bills. This matter has been brought before the Commission by the Maryland Office of People's Counsel (OPC) (Docket: EL26-63), and the basic principle underpinning this issue is simple: our constituents should not be forced to pay for transmission projects that they did not cause and from which they will not meaningfully benefit.

Data centers being built outside of Maryland are driving one of the largest transmission expansions in PJM’s history. Across its three most recent regional transmission planning rounds, PJM has advanced $22 billion in projects needed principally to serve data centers. Under PJM’s current cost allocation rules, roughly $2 billion of those costs have been assigned to Maryland ratepayers rather than the data centers that are driving the demand.

Marylanders are already shouldering the immense burden of skyrocketing electricity costs, and it is unjust and unreasonable to force our constituents to subsidize the energy infrastructure needs of the wealthiest companies in the world. Unless the Commission acts, our constituents will pay an estimated $1.6 billion on their electric bills over the next ten years for these projects alone, and $823 million of that total cost will fall on residential customers, which equates to roughly $345 for the average customer.

PJM’s cost allocation rules have not kept pace with the build out of hyperscale data centers, just one of which can equal the electricity demand of a small city. PJM’s current rules spread costs broadly across the region regardless of where, and for whom, the underlying projects are actually needed. Maryland regulators have no ability to assign such costs to data centers located in other states, and with tens of thousands of megawatts of additional data center demand growth projected across PJM over the next two decades, our constituents face billions of dollars in further charges absent Commission action to address this unjust and unreasonable cost allocation. Furthermore, because much of the forecasted growth in data center energy demand is speculative, our constituents bear the unacceptable risk of paying for projects built to serve potential data centers that are never built due to any number of external reasons.

We were encouraged by the Commission’s June 18, 2026 orders directing PJM and five other grid operators to justify or reform how they assign the costs of serving large loads, which advance the essential goal of protecting ordinary consumers. Those orders, however, are forward-looking. We also seek to obtain relief for our constituents from the billions in costs PJM has already assigned, and because most of those costs have not yet appeared on customer bills, timely Commission action can prevent much of this harm before it occurs.

We urge the Commission to act expeditiously to provide relief from these costs for Maryland ratepayers, including as requested in OPC’s complaint. Thank you for your consideration of this important issue that is essential to ensuring just and reasonable energy costs for our constituents.
title: Maryland Democrats Urge FERC to Protect Marylanders from Rising Electricity Costs Due to Out-of-State Data Centers

text:
Riley took growers’ case directly to Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins and pushed USDA to deliver relief

WASHINGTON, DC — Congressman Josh Riley (NY-19) today announced that he secured a U.S. Department of Agriculture disaster declaration for Upstate New York growers devastated by this spring’s extreme weather.

The declaration allows eligible growers to apply for low-interest emergency loans and other disaster assistance through the USDA Farm Service Agency. New York growers reported more than $30 million in losses, with some farms losing nearly their entire crop.

“After April’s freeze, growers across Upstate New York told me they were facing catastrophic losses. I took Saunderskill Farms’ story straight to Secretary Rollins because when a farm loses nearly half its crop, it still has workers to pay, equipment loans to cover, and another growing season to finance—with half the income to do it,” said Congressman Riley. “These growers deserve support to recover, rebuild, and stay afloat until the next growing season. I worked with Secretary Rollins to get this disaster declaration approved, and we got it done.”

Following April’s freeze, Riley’s office heard directly from farms across Upstate New York about severe damage to apples, grapes, strawberries, stone fruits, and other specialty crops.

One of those farms was Saunderskill Farms in Accord, where the family was facing the loss of nearly half its apple crop.

During a June 4 hearing of the House Agriculture Committee, Riley brought Saunderskill’s story directly to U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins and called on her to work with him to approve New York’s disaster declaration as quickly as possible.

After the hearing, Riley visited Saunderskill Farms to meet with the family, inspect the damage firsthand, and discuss what federal relief would mean for the farm’s recovery.

Less than eight weeks after Riley took the issue directly to Rollins, USDA approved the disaster declaration.

The designation gives eligible producers eight months to apply for emergency loans through their local Farm Service Agency office. The loans can help growers restore or replace essential property, cover production costs, pay essential family living expenses, reorganize farming operations, and refinance certain debts.

Riley is also fighting to make sure Upstate growers are better protected before the next disaster. He secured provisions in the House-passed Farm Bill to improve crop insurance and strengthen disaster assistance for apple growers and other specialty-crop producers.

###
title: RILEY DELIVERS MAJOR WIN FOR UPSTATE APPLE GROWERS FACING $30 MILLION IN LOSSES

The Regional Food Bank’s 2026 State of Hunger report shows that more than 12% of their service area – which includes Dutchess, Orange, and Ulster Counties – is food insecure, including 1 in 6 children

The report comes amid the fallout from several harmful Trump Administration actions, including the largest cut to SNAP in history, cost-raising tariffs, and cuts to TEFAP which forced the foodbank to serve 2 million fewer meals in 2025 than 2024

Ryan joined food bank representatives, local electeds, and partner organizations to discuss his work in Washington to bring down food costs, support local farmers, and hold the Trump Administration accountable

NEWBURGH, NY – Today, Congressman Pat Ryan joined local advocates, partners, and electeds at the Regional Food Bank to discuss the State of Hunger in the Hudson Valley. The 2026 report, informed by new research by Feeding America’s annual Map the Meal Gap study on food insecurity, paints a grim picture of growing food insecurity in the Hudson Valley amid harmful Trump Administration policy.

Among the report’s most alarming figures is that 53,390 (1 in 6) children in the Hudson Valley lack access to adequate nutrition. That is 5,000 more children than in 2025. It follows more than a year of cost-raising policies and actions from the Administration, including the largest cut to SNAP in history – which is ripping food assistance from more than 40 million Americans, including up to 70,000 in the Hudson Valley, as well as placing financial strain on farmers – and as prices continue to rise across the board due to Trump’s war in Iran.

Standing with the gathered community Ryan advocated for his bipartisan Lower Grocery Prices Act, and discussed his recently introduced Family Grocery and Farmer Relief Act, which breaks up greedy monopolies that jack up prices on hardworking Americans and push out small businesses. When a harmful Trump Administration policy cut two million meals at the Regional Food Bank – and slashed a critical income source for Hudson Valley farmers – Ryan immediately rallied with the community and hosted a Community Speak Out demanding the cuts be reversed.

“Hudson Valley families have to spend way too much of their income just to put food on the table. There are real people behind the data in this new report – children who aren’t getting the nutrients their growing bodies need, seniors pinching pennies to feed themselves, and families on fixed incomes worrying they won’t be able to afford new groceries this week. Especially after thousands lost their SNAP benefits because of Trump’s USDA cuts and as grocery prices continue to rise, I’m so grateful to our exceptional food bank’s tireless work, helping meet this unprecedented demand in our community,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “One of my top priorities is making life more affordable, and I’ll keep fighting to pass my Lower Grocery Prices Act and to protect SNAP benefits until no one has to go hungry in the Hudson Valley.”

“The challenges we are facing as well as our partners in the charitable food industry have faced in recent months, are truly unprecedented,” said Tom Nardacci, CEO of Regional Food Bank. “With federal cuts to the USDA, the SNAP crises and increasing inflation, our more than 1,000 partner agencies are witnessing longer lines and greater demand. The generosity of industry partners, businesses, groups and organizations, volunteers and our neighbors allowed us to hold the line of food insecurity rates among adults at 12%, but we need more help from our community to meet the demand for our children.”

Last year, Congressman Ryan stood with the food bank and community members in fighting back against the Trump Administration’s cut to The Emergency Food Assistance Program (TEFAP) – which partners local farms with food banks to serve food insecure populations. Trump cut the program by 50%, eliminating crucial business for local farmers and forcing the Hudson Valley branch of the Regional Food Bank to provide 2 million fewer meals in 2025 than 2024.

Hudson Valley families have also been dealing with skyrocketing grocery costs due to the President’s tariffs back in April 2025. In January, following polling that showed 87% of Americans were dealing with increased grocery prices under Trump, Ryan conducted a community inquiry. More than 99% of respondents said they were feeling the burden of higher grocery costs, with 75% of them citing Trump’s tariffs as the main driver.

Congressman Ryan’s bipartisan Lower Grocery Prices Act would require the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) to analyze the price of groceries over the last 20 years, provide effective solutions on how to lower costs, and develop a national plan to combat the high prices and ease the affordability crisis. Ryan originally introduced the legislation after the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) released a report in March 2024 which detailed how large grocery companies exploited the high-price environment caused by the pandemic to jack up their prices and pad their profit margins, unfairly raising prices for consumers as well as snubbing smaller competitors’ profits.

Most recently, Ryan introduced the Family Grocery and Farmer Relief Act, landmark legislation breaking up greedy monopolies and ending unfair pricing practices that raise costs for American families and box out local farmers and ranchers.

ST. PETERSBURG, FL — This week, U.S. Rep. Kathy Castor (FL-14) announced $2,290,288 in community project funding for two stormwater projects designed to cut costs and protect St. Petersburg residents, roadways and property from frequent flooding. St. Petersburg Mayor Kenneth T. Welch, City Council Members Deborah Figgs-Sanders and Brandi Gabbard and community leaders cheered the local investments.

Castor secured the investments through federal Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Community Project Funding (CPF) on behalf of the City of St. Petersburg. The projects will upgrade aging drainage infrastructure in two flood-prone areas, improve emergency access and public safety during storms and strengthen the city’s long-term resilience as heavy rainfall and tidal flooding become more frequent.

View photos from the press conference here.

“Tampa Bay families should not have to worry that a heavy rainstorm will flood their street, damage their property or cut them off from their neighborhood,” said Castor. “I am proud to have worked with local leaders to secure these federal investments because protecting our neighbors from flooding requires reliable, modern infrastructure. These projects will help keep important roadways open, move stormwater more effectively and make our community safer and more resilient for years to come.”

Castor community projects include:

MLK Street South Flooding Alleviation — $1,145,144: The project will elevate and improve Martin Luther King Jr. Street South between 30th Avenue South and 36th Avenue South, where flooding can make the roadway impassable during heavy rainfall. The funding will also expand stormwater culverts to improve drainage capacity and reduce roadway flooding under current and future conditions.

88th Avenue North and 4th Street North Storm Drainage Improvements — $1,145,144: The project will address recurring street flooding near a tidally influenced stormwater outfall. Planned improvements include replacing and enlarging stormwater conveyance systems, installing new inlets and underground piping, and adding stormwater storage. Green infrastructure will be incorporated where feasible to reduce runoff and improve water quality.

Together, the projects will reduce the risk of roadway and structural flooding, protect nearby homes and businesses, improve access for residents and emergency responders during severe weather, and increase the reliability of St. Petersburg’s stormwater system.

Castor secured $19,607,288 for 15 community priority projects across Tampa Bay through the FY 2026 federal appropriations. These investments will lower costs, expand affordable housing, strengthen flood mitigation, improve transportation, create workforce training opportunities in trades and expand services for students, young people, veterans and military families.

LOS ANGELES, CA – Today, Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37) convened a fireside chat with Adrianne Todman, former Acting Secretary of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, and a panel discussion with local housing leaders to examine what the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act means for families and communities across Los Angeles.

The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act took effect on July 11, 2026. This bipartisan housing package aims to address challenges related to housing production, affordability, preservation, and coordination between federal and local partners. Read the full bill text here.

The panel featured leaders from the Los Angeles County Development Authority, the Los Angeles Housing Department, the Housing Authority of the City of Los Angeles, Habitat for Humanity of Greater Los Angeles, Abundant Housing Los Angeles, Enterprise Community Partners, and Strategic Actions for a Just Economy.

“Whether it’s seniors on fixed incomes or working families, too many Angelenos are struggling to keep a roof over their heads,” said Rep. Kamlager-Dove. “Addressing the housing crisis takes more than just a whole-of-government approach—it demands close collaboration with community partners to pinpoint areas of need and deliver real solutions. I was proud to convene federal and local leaders to help ensure Los Angeles can turn the opportunities created by the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act into shovels in the ground and more affordable homes.”

“We applaud Congress for working diligently to pass this monumental housing reform legislation that is poised to significantly address the affordable housing crisis felt not only within Los Angeles County but by communities across the nation,” stated Emilio Salas, LACDA Executive Director. “This comprehensive approach to enhance housing at multiple levels requires that we collaborate with our local and State partners to ensure successful implementation, which we are prepared to do, but we must also advocate to our Congressional leadership to ensure that the proposed reforms are fully funded and supported by the Federal government, to see actual change.”

“The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act represents one of the most significant federal housing achievements in a generation providing critical tools to preserve affordable housing, revitalize public housing, and strengthen pathways to stability for families across Los Angeles," said HACLA President & CEO Lourdes Castro Ramirez. "We applaud Congresswoman Waters for her unwavering leadership on affordable housing and appreciate Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove for bringing housing leaders together to implement this transformative legislation. Turning these historic policies into real, lasting change requires building solid partnerships across every level and I'm excited to see such collaboration taking shape."

"I am so pleased to work with my colleagues on the local, State and Federal levels on finding ways to expedite the development of much needed affordable housing," said Tiena Johnson Hall, General Manager of LAHD. "Finding creative ways to work collaboratively is so vital as we work to house Angelenos."

“The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act creates important new opportunities to increase housing production, preserve existing housing, and expand pathways to homeownership,” said Erin Rank, President of Habitat for Humanity of Greater Los Angeles. “We appreciate Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove for bringing together local leaders to focus on implementation and impact. At Habitat for Humanity of Greater Los Angeles, we believe success will ultimately be measured by the number of homes built, homes preserved, and families who can achieve long-term stability and build wealth through affordable homeownership in Los Angeles County.”

“With overwhelming bipartisan support, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act included 47 provisions that broaden public-private investments, strengthen existing federal programs, and create new tools to boost housing supply and affordability,” said Jimar Wilson, Vice President of Enterprise Community Partners. “One proven provision is the expansion of HUD's Rental Assistance Demonstration program by 100,000 units, unlocking private capital to preserve aging public housing. This is the tool effectively used in the $664 million transformation of Jordan Downs over the course of a decade, which has delivered to date 787 new affordable homes in Watts."

“Tenant protections are a key to solving our affordable housing crisis,” said Cynthia Strathmann, Executive Director of Strategic Actions for a Just Economy. “Protecting renters from evictions, harassment, and unreasonable rent raises not only keeps people housed, but it also helps keep rents stable. Without strong tenant protections in place, California will continue to see rising homelessness, overcrowding, and economic strain on working- and middle-class households.”

Dilley, Texas — Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29), representative for California’s 29th Congressional District, conducted a Congressional oversight visit of the Dilley Immigration Processing Center in Texas with her colleagues, Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), and Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07). The Members visited the Dilley Immigration Processing Center to meet with women, children, and families who have been detained for extended periods of time and conduct oversight on the conditions of the facility, which has been consistently reported as inhumane and dire.

“My colleagues and I met with 20 people, including a 16-year-old, who have been detained at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center for months,” said Congresswoman Rivas. “I spoke with a woman from Maryland who was attending her court hearing in March when she was detained and sent to the Dilley Immigration Processing Center. Her 12-year-old son with special needs has a court hearing tomorrow and is worried that he, too, will be sent to the Dilley Immigration Processing Center or even deported. This is one story among hundreds – of mothers detained, children pulled away from school, families separated, and lives being disrupted in ways that often go unseen. We owe it to these families to listen and respond.”

Unfortunately, ICE officials on-site severely limited access to Members. More specifically, the Members were only able to talk to one child, even though over 100 children are detained. Members were not shown the medical unit nor classrooms, which were of particular importance especially to determine the conditions of the facility. Members observed that ICE is becoming more secretive and more restrictive, including not even providing the number of federal workers on site. This is concerning and only underscores the continued calls to shut down the Dilley Detention Facility. During their visit, Members were shown a courtroom where cases are heard, an intake facility where pregnant women, children, and infants are processed, and a small plastic playground that offers no shade to children from the Texas sun.

Congresswoman Rivas continued: “ICE is being increasingly secretive about their actions at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center. We were only allowed to speak to one child out of 112 children – and even that interaction was cut short. ICE is traumatizing over 500 individuals – including pregnant women, children, and infants as young as 2 months old – and subjecting them to inhumane conditions for extended periods of time. These individuals should be living their lives, welcoming their newborn children, playing with their friends, and raising their families outside of ICE detention. The Trump Administration must be held accountable for the trauma it is inflicting on immigrant families. Children should not be detained, and I am continuing to call for the Dilley Detention Facility to be shut down, immediately.”

Background:

Congresswoman Luz Rivas has conducted seven oversight visits at immigration detention facilities in California and Texas, including at the Edward R. Roybal Federal Building, the Adelanto Detention Facility, the California City Detention Facility, and the Dilley Immigration Processing Center. ICE blocked Congresswoman Rivas from conducting oversight of detention facilities three times.

Congresswoman Rivas joined Congressman Joaquin Castro and over 100 of their House Democratic Caucus colleagues in calling for the Dilley Immigration Processing Center to be shut down.

Congresswoman Rivas has also sent five letters to ICE leadership calling for accountability into the conditions at detention centers and joined her colleagues for field hearings into ICE abuses in Los Angeles and Minneapolis-St. Paul.

Dilley Immigration Processing Center, also known as the South Texas Family Residential Center, was built in 2014 to detain women and children. 539 individuals are currently being held at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center.

A report on the Dilley Immigration Processing Center from Refugee and Immigrant Center for Education and Legal Services (RAICES) found that families are routinely being held longer than the 20-day legal limit, with many being held for months. The report noted unsafe and degrading conditions, including inadequate access to food, water, personal hygiene, and basic care that are particularly harmful to children. Pregnant women face inadequate prenatal care and unsafe medical practices, putting them and their unborn babies at risk. Many are deported without a meaningful opportunity to seek protection, raising concerns under U.S. and international law.

The report also mentions that facilities at the Dilley Immigration Detention Center lack educational resources for children, noting that classes are taught by a prison guard.
title: Congresswoman Luz Rivas Conducts Oversight at Dilley Family Detention Facility in Texas, Raises Alarm Over ICE Secrecy
