I can breathe easier now knowing that I will finally be getting the VA benefits I am entitled to. Thank you to Congressman Ryan for caring about seniors like me and having a team who can help us navigate the agencies that we depend on to be able to survive.”

I was granted 100% P&T disability compensation. My wife and I couldn't be happier. Thank you!”

WASHINGTON — Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez (D-NY) and Rep. Hank Johnson (D-GA), co-chairs of the Congressional Hepatitis Caucus, reintroduced a resolution recognizing July 28, 2026 as World Hepatitis Day, raising awareness about the issues surrounding hepatitis B and C and reaffirming Congress's commitment to ending these preventable diseases.

Each year, thousands of Americans die of viral hepatitis, and another 75,000 are infected. Worldwide, an estimated 520 million people are chronically infected with hepatitis B and C, and an estimated 1.3 million die annually. Hepatitis B and hepatitis C, and the liver disease they cause, remain urgent global health threats, disproportionately impacting communities of color, LGBTQ individuals, and people who inject drugs.

“Far too many Americans have died because of hepatitis, a viral disease that disproportionately affects communities of color and the LGBTQ community,” said Congresswoman Velázquez. “I'm proud to reintroduce this resolution recognizing hepatitis as a public health priority. With increased public education, improved testing, and access to treatment, we can turn the tide on this epidemic. But this Administration has chosen to walk away from decades of proven vaccine policy, putting newborns at risk of a preventable disease. We cannot let that stand.”

“How we respond to preventable diseases says a great deal about our values,” said Rep. Johnson. “Every family deserves access to accurate information, lifesaving treatments, and quality healthcare. As we recognize World Hepatitis Day, we must continue investing in the public health tools that save lives and protect future generations.”

The reintroduction comes amid an unprecedented rollback of federal hepatitis prevention policy. After firing all 17 members of the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP), Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s reconstituted committee voted in December to end the longstanding recommendation that all newborns receive a hepatitis B vaccine dose at birth, a policy in place since 1991 that drove a dramatic reduction in pediatric hepatitis B infections. The CDC adopted the change over the objections of the American Academy of Pediatrics, the American Medical Association, and public health experts nationwide.

The Administration has also suspended U.S. support for global health institutions including USAID, the World Health Organization, and Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, jeopardizing hepatitis prevention programs abroad.

The resolution is endorsed by: African Health Coalition Incorporation, American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases, Association of Asian Pacific Community Health Organizations (AAPCHO), Coalition Against Hepatitis for People of African Origin (CHIPO), Community HealthCare Network, Community Liver Alliance, Congolese United Foundation, ekiM For Change, Empire Liver Foundation, End Hep C SF, Hawaiʻi Health & Harm Reduction Center, Health Betterment Initiative, Hep Free Hawaiʻi, Hep B United, Hepatitis B Foundation, Hepatitis C Allies of Philadelphia (HepCAP), HIV+Hepatitis Policy Institute, Housing Works - Positive Health Project, Illinois Public Health Association, Indiana Recovery Alliance, Liver Coalition of San Diego, Montefiore Starfish Program, NASTAD, National Harm Reduction Coalition, National Survivors Union, National Viral Hepatitis Roundtable (NVHR), North East Medical Services, SF HepB Free, The AIDS Institute, The Hepatitis C Mentor and Support Group, Inc. (HCMSG), Thomas Boyer Liver Research Institute, and VOCAL-NY.

“Amid federal public health funding declines and falling rates of the lifesaving hepatitis B vaccine, it is critical that we reaffirm our commitment to eliminating viral hepatitis,” said Chari Cohen, DrPH, MPH, President of the Hepatitis B Foundation. “We cannot allow the millions of people living with hepatitis B and hepatitis C in the U.S. and around the world to be left behind. Viral hepatitis elimination is possible, but requires sustained federal investment and strong congressional support to ensure that essential prevention, testing, care, and treatment services are accessible to all who need them.”

“We have taken a step back in our efforts to eliminate hepatitis over the past year and yet we have the tools to save lives. We must re-commit to the science-back strategies that we know prevents hepatitis B and C while increasing access to treatment,” said Heather Lusk, Co-Director of Hep Free Hawaiʻi and Executive Director of the Hawaiʻi Health & Harm Reduction Center.

“The Illinois Public Health Association (IPHA) is committed to recognizing World Hepatitis Day and the urgent need to expand testing, vaccination, accessible treatments, and global elimination of this deadly disease by 2030. Viral hepatitis claims more than 1.3 million lives annually and disproportionately impacts vulnerable populations across the globe and here in the United States. IPHA strongly supports World Hepatitis Day and our public health champions worldwide who work to increase vaccination, screening, and treatment for our impacted communities day in and day out!” said Jeffery Erdman, Deputy Executive Director of the Illinois Public Health Association.

A PDF of the resolution can be found here.

title: Velázquez and Johnson Reintroduce Resolution Recognizing World Hepatitis Day as Administration Rolls Back Vaccine Protections

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Following disturbing reports that the Department of Defense removed the names of four American troops from the official Iran War death toll, Rep. Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06) joined 14 fellow Democratic veterans in urging the Administration to accurately and transparently account for U.S. servicemembers killed and wounded in the Iran war.

“As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers,” wrote the lawmakers.

“The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports,” they continued. “We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.”

Following public outcry, the Department of Defense quietly restored the names of the four U.S. servicemembers removed from the Iran War death toll over the weekend. The Administration has not provided an adequate explanation as to why the servicemembers were removed in the first place.

The letter, led by Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04), was also signed by Representatives Pat Ryan (NY-18), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Derek Tran (CA-45), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), Jason Crow (CO-06), Bobby Scott (VA-03), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), and Jared Golden (ME-02).

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear President Trump,

As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers.

The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports. Inaccurate and delayed reports from the Department of War about U.S. casualties is bad for morale and undermines our U.S. servicemembers.

We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.

Sincerely,
title: Democratic Veterans Demand Transparency on Iran War Casualties

WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement today recognizing the 36th anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA):

“Today, I join in celebrating the thirty-sixth anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) – pivotal legislation that reshaped the lives of millions of Americans living with disabilities, guaranteeing them equal access and equal opportunity.

“Championing the ADA in the House was one of the proudest moments in my career. Over the past thirty-six years, we have continued to strengthen this progress through the ADA Amendments Act of 2008 and seen it advanced through the 1999 Supreme Court decision in Olmstead v. L.C., which reaffirmed our original intent to secure full inclusion and equality for all.

“As we reflect on these accomplishments, we are reminded that the fight is not over. We must acknowledge the dangers of this moment as the Trump Administration undermines the progress we have achieved, seeking to erode opportunities for Americans with disabilities and overturn Congress’s clear intent as recognized by Olmstead. So, our work continues, and we will keep fighting diligently so that every American may enjoy the promises upon which our nation was founded – liberty and justice for all.”
title: Hoyer Statement on the 36th Anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act

Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on CNN’s State of the Union, where he outlined how with 100 days until the midterm elections, Democrats are going to continue to push back on Republican extremism and fight to lower costs for hardworking American taxpayers.

DANA BASH: Here with me now is the House Democratic Leader, Congressman Hakeem Jeffries. Mr. Leader, thank you so much for being here. I know that you are launching what Democrats are calling 100 Days Out Weekend of Action with more than 400 grassroots events in competitive states, including Pennsylvania, where you’re going to be speaking later today. At the same time, your party is fighting over whether the path back to the majority runs through the center or the activist left, who want to defund the police, abolish ICE, end aid to Israel, open borders. I know that you call the Democratic Party a mosaic, but are you going to push any of those positions if you win the majority back?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well what unites the party, and certainly what will take place over the next 100 days, beginning today, is a focus on us fighting for an affordable America, based on the reality that life in this country is far too expensive and everybody agrees that that’s the dynamic that the country confronts. Too many people are working hard, they’re playing by the rules, but they can’t thrive and they can barely survive. Not enough food on the table, not enough gas in the tank, unable to actually regularly and consistently afford to pay the rent or pay the mortgage. We want to drive down the cost of groceries, drive down and lower the cost of gasoline, drive down the cost of housing and also make sure that healthcare is affordable for every single American.

DANA BASH: Right, but to do those things, which is the messaging that I’ve heard you say, especially recently, you need to come up with policy proposals. So will those policy proposals be in line with what some of the more progressive members who keep getting elected are pushing? Or will you sort of move more towards the moderate area, where if you do win the majority, it will be likely because they pick up swing districts?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we want to make sure that we are solving problems on behalf of the American people, and that’s in every possible area. It is clear that what unites Democrats, for instance, we forcefully have been pushing back against the One Big Ugly Bill and the effort to enact the largest cut to Medicaid in American history. That’s a disgrace, and clearly that needs to be reversed. We need to make sure that we do things like extending the Affordable Care Act tax credits so that more than 20 million people actually can have healthcare that they can afford restored to them as opposed to the situation that they confront right now because of MAGA extremist policies, which is that they’ve experienced dramatic increases in their health insurance premiums in some cases more than $1000 per month. It certainly is the case, as we’ve already demonstrated unanimously on the House Floor, that we need to stop this reckless and costly war of choice that has skyrocketed gas prices on everyday Americans, and we need to stop the Trump tariffs, which have increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year.

DANA BASH: You, according to my colleague Manu Raju, clash with Senator Bernie Sanders over the fact that he is campaigning for progressive candidates, some of whom are challenging incumbents you back, including Members of the Congressional Black Caucus. Are Senator Sanders and other progressives in the party making it harder for you to win in November? Is that what you said to Senator Sanders?

LEADER JEFFRIES: No, I wouldn’t describe it as a clash. It was a candid conversation along with Congressman Greg Meeks, the Chair of the Congressional Black Caucus PAC, with respect to one particular race in North Carolina at the beginning of the primary cycle and trying to get a sense of his approach to that race. I do think that Senator Sanders and Democrats in both the House and the Senate understand the stakes that are in front of us, particularly as we are one hundred days out. And that’s making sure that we actually take back control of the Congress so we can end this MAGA extremism that has been unleashed on the American people that is actively hurting hardworking American taxpayers and actually commit to making life more affordable for the American people. That’s clearly what the American people want to see done, and that’s not what Republicans have been able to accomplish during their time in office since Trump was sworn in back in January of last year.

DANA BASH: I think one of the things that some of those who are winning their primaries and will likely be in office want to know is if you are going to agree to hold votes on abolishing ICE, opening borders, things of that nature. Will you?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I’ve spoken to several of the incoming Members of Congress across the ideological spectrum. Not a single person has raised those issues, other than obviously what they’ve seen from Democrats in pushing back against an out-of-control ICE because we believe that immigration enforcement in this country clearly should be fair, just and humane, and that’s not what’s taking place. That’s the reason why House Democrats have taken a strong position as it relates to not giving a dime to Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine until, of course, there is dramatic reform in this country and that ICE agents actually start to conduct themselves like every other cop, police officer and law enforcement agent in the country.

DANA BASH: Your next-door neighbor, New Jersey, just disclosed that 6,600 non-citizens were mistakenly registered to vote there from 2023 to 2024. 400 of them actually voted in elections since then. It is a small number compared to the 7 million voters in New Jersey and there’s no evidence that that swayed any election. But this is one of the most significant disclosures of non-citizen registration. Democrats have repeatedly said that non-citizen voting doesn’t happen. It happened. Is this a problem?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I think that I continue to have confidence in state and local authorities in making sure that there’s going to be a free and fair election in November. And if modest or minor challenges emerge, such as the one that was disclosed voluntarily by the authorities in New Jersey, that it is immediately corrected. And that’s what I expect will continue to happen. Unfortunately, what we’ve seen from Donald Trump is that, in this particular case, Republicans have adopted voter suppression as an electoral strategy because they have failed to actually deliver on making life more affordable for the American people. It was Donald Trump who promised to lower costs on day one, but we know that costs haven’t gone down in this country, costs have gone up. It was Donald Trump, I believe, who said that he was elected not to start wars—endless wars in the Middle East—but to stop them, and then turned around and has gotten us involved in this reckless war of choice in Iran that has skyrocketed gas prices on the American people. By the way, it was Donald Trump who said they were going to love and cherish Medicaid, and then Republicans enacted the largest cut to Medicaid in American history, ripping healthcare away from more than 14 million Americans. They have nothing to run on. We’re going to run on fighting for an affordable America.

DANA BASH: Mr. Leader, before I let you go, President Trump ordered signs placed outside the Museum of American History, warning that it promotes inaccurate history. It comes, of course, as the White House is attacking the Smithsonian, accusing the institution of promoting left-wing ideology. Is there anything you can do to stop those signs from going up?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’re going to explore every legislative avenue and every litigation avenue, as we’ve repeatedly done up until this point. Here’s the thing. Black history is American history, and we are not going to let the extremists whitewash it. Not now. Not ever.

DANA BASH: Hakeem Jeffries, Democratic Leader of the House of Representatives. Thanks so much for being here. I appreciate it.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Thank you.

Full interview can be watched here.

Report outlines rising cost of groceries, housing, utilities, gas, and healthcare under President Trump and Congressional Republicans

Birmingham, AL – Today, U.S. Rep. Terri Sewell (AL-07) released a new report examining the growing affordability crisis facing families across Alabama's 7th Congressional District. The report details how President Trump's economic policies and congressional Republicans' legislative agenda have driven up the cost of everyday essentials while threatening access to healthcare and food assistance for thousands of Alabamians.

The report comes as House Democrats unveil their "Fighting For An Affordable America Agenda," with exactly 100 days until Election Day. The agenda involves three pillars: lowering the cost of groceries, gas and housing, providing affordable healthcare for every American, and cleaning corruption by holding the crooks accountable.

Watch Rep. Sewell's video message here.

Among its findings, the report notes that Alabama families are paying an average of $2,700 more for basic living expenses, families in Alabama's 7th District now spend an average of $1,110 per month on groceries, and approximately 70,000 people in AL-07 are expected to see their health insurance costs rise because Republicans allowed enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits to expire. The average Alabama household has paid $686 more for gasoline since President Trump launched his unauthorized war in Iran, and more than 81,800 Alabamians have already lost SNAP benefits under Republicans' budget law.

"One hundred days before Election Day, Alabama families deserve to know the truth about who is driving up their costs," said Rep. Sewell."President Trump promised to lower prices on Day One. Instead, families across Alabama's 7th District are paying more for groceries, housing, electricity, gas, and healthcare while Republicans in Congress have chosen to cut Medicaid and food assistance to help pay for tax breaks for billionaires."

"It doesn't have to be this way," continued Sewell. "House Democrats are fighting for an Affordable America by lowering the cost of groceries, gas, and housing, making healthcare more affordable, and holding corporations accountable when they exploit consumers and drive up prices. Alabama families deserve an economy that works for them—not just the wealthy and well-connected."

The report highlights several economic challenges facing Alabama families, including:

Alabama families are paying an average of $2,700 more for basic living expenses under President Trump and congressional Republicans.

Families in Alabama's 7th District paid an average of $233 more for electricity in 2025.

The average monthly grocery bill in AL-07 has reached $1,110.

The average Alabama household has paid $686 more for gasoline since the start of President Trump's war in Iran.

The average annual cost of child care for two children in Alabama has climbed to $16,640.

Approximately 24,353 people in Alabama's 7th District are projected to lose health coverage because of Republican cuts to Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act.

More than 81,800 Alabamians have already lost SNAP benefits.

More than 20,000 Alabama individuals and families filed for bankruptcy in 2025, a 6.7 percent increase over the previous year.

The full report, "The Affordability Crisis in Alabama's 7th Congressional District: How President Trump and Congressional Republicans Are Driving Up Costs for Alabama Families," is available here.
title: Rep. Sewell Releases New Report Detailing the Affordability Crisis Facing Alabama's 7th Congressional District

text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on MS NOW’s PoliticsNation, where he reiterated that nearly 100 days until the midterm elections, Democrats are united in our commitment to lowering the high cost of living, fixing our broken healthcare system and holding crooks accountable.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Joining me now, the Congressman from Brooklyn, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries. Thanks very much for being with us this weekend. I want to start with the news unfolding today in Maine, where Democrats have chosen Troy Jackson to run against Senator Susan Collins in November. My first question is, are you satisfied that Democrats are now in a better position to win the seat in Maine and possibly retake the Senate in the fall?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, good afternoon, Rev. Great to be with you. First of all, I’m very confident that we have extraordinary candidates on the House side and we’re on our way to taking back control of the House of Representatives. And what we see on the Senate side, and I think Maine today will complete that picture, is a strong set of candidates to make the Senate competitive, which no one thought was the case just about a year ago. The Maine Democrats seem to have rallied behind Troy Jackson, and I expect that they’ll be unified moving forward and put up a very good fight against Susan Collins, who clearly—it’s time for her to go.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, Democrats chose to hold Graham Platner accountable, and they have switched their candidates in Maine in the middle of a must-win race for the party. But take a listen to your House colleague, Speaker Mike Johnson, when asked about how he intends to handle allegations against two Members of his party on Tuesday.

RECORDING OF SPEAKER JOHNSON: The key word there is allegation. We have a process here—the House Ethics Committee works on those things. If allegations are made, they work through a process. So I’m not in the business of commenting on investigations as they are in process. And we’ll see how it shakes out. That’s how this always works. And, by the way, it’s done for Rs and Ds on both sides of the aisle.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, we should note both Representatives Miller and Mills deny the accusations against them, but isn’t it the case that the two parties hold their Members to a very different ethical standard?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I think, as Democrats, we’re going to continue to try to uphold an American standard of decency and fairness and ensuring, of course, that people get their due process in an administrative or legal or congressional process, while at the same time trying to uplift American values. And what Republicans are trying to do, of course, is just take a partisan approach to everything, and that’s just the reality. We’ve seen it over the last 18 months. And at the end of the day, Republicans are just all consumed with power, and not power to actually make life more affordable for the American people in the midst of a crisis where life is too expensive, they’re continuing to just lean into lifting up the wealthy, the well-off, and the well-connected.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Let’s switch gears to the House. As we mentioned, we’re closing in on 100 days until the election, and Democrats are honing their message and laying out their priorities. You’ve said the first bill of a new Democratic session would be focused on affordability. This week, Democrats in the House passed another resolution to halt U.S. military action in Iran, gaining four Republican votes in the process. You’ve called the Trump administration’s strategy with Iran, quote, ‘Operation Epic Failure,’ end of quote. Are voters responding to what you’re doing and saying, and are you confident your party can regain power in Congress this fall?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We’re definitely confident that we’re on the right side of the American people in terms of our commitment to drive down the high cost of living, to make sure that we actually deliver affordable healthcare for every single American and that we hold the crooks accountable in the midst of a level of corruption, the likes of which have never been seen in America’s 250-year history. Our agenda, of course, begins aggressively with addressing the affordability crisis. And we’re committed to lowering the cost of groceries, the cost of gas, the cost of housing, the cost of everyday goods, the things that are making life untenable for far too many Americans. We believe when you work hard and play by the rules in this country, you should be able to live a middle-class life, an affordable life, live the good life. That’s not the case right now. Far too many Americans are drowning in this failed Trump economy, and it’s time to move the country in a different direction.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Fox News polling out this week shows nearly 40% of voters want dramatic change right now, and Democrats are favored over Republicans on nearly every issue, including the economy and foreign policy. Republicans hold only slight edges on national security and crime, yet with their poll numbers plunging, Trump and Republicans have been focused on rigging the electorate in their favor. Tomorrow we’re going to be talking to your colleague Congressman Cleo Fields, who announced he will not be seeking re-election this week, after his majority-Black Louisiana district was eliminated in the wake of the Supreme Court Callais decision. You’ve been very clear that you view what happened to Representative Fields a form of voter suppression. A gut check question now: how deeply will this country be impacted in November by what Republicans and the courts have done to Black representation, and how are Democrats working to overcome it?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Congressman Cleo Fields will be deeply missed. We’re going to work closely over the next six or so months so he can finish out his term strong. He’s a tremendous champion for the people of Louisiana, and it’s a shame that his seat has been carved up as a result of the unprecedented attack on the Voting Rights Act by the Supreme Court, and then the Jim Crow-like tactics that have been unleashed in states like Louisiana as well as Tennessee and Alabama, signed off on by the United States Supreme Court, which is why we believe dramatic change is necessary in a whole host of areas—that’s dramatic campaign finance reform, dramatic electoral reform, including, of course, passage of the John Robert Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act so we can end the era of voter suppression in the United States of America once and for all. And certainly we need dramatic Supreme Court reform because this right-wing Supreme Court extremist majority is totally out of control and they need to be reigned in.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, President Trump and his allies continue to push for the so-called SAVE Act that includes many of the President’s vote supressing—suppression priorities and, like, voter ID. This week, House Republicans tucked elements of the SAVE Act into a budget reconciliation bill that passed along party lines, that Senate Majority Leader John Thune has said will not pass the Senate in its current form. Are you concerned Republicans could still find a way to push through parts of the SAVE Act before the midterms, and what are the Democrats doing to counter this?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We’re going to continue to stand strong against the voter suppression efforts of the Republican Party led by Donald Trump. Clearly, they have no agenda that they feel comfortable in selling to the American people because they’ve broken all their promises, including promising not to start forever wars in the Middle East, but to stop them. And then Donald Trump and Republicans turned around—they’ve gotten us involved in this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran. That, of course, has skyrocketed gas prices through the roof and are hurting everyday Americans day after day after day. And so, from our standpoint, we know that Republicans are going to try to rig the midterm elections. They’re doing it in real time. We’ve got to stop them from jamming this voter suppression bill down the throats of the American people. Democrats have been strong in the House and in the Senate in holding the line. We have to continue to do that. At the same period of time, we’re putting together the largest voter protection effort in the history of the country, working, of course, with Senate Democrats, House Democrats, the Democratic Governors Association, the Attorneys General Association on the Democratic side, the Democratic Secretaries of State, as well as civil society, which includes the faith community, civil rights groups, democracy protection groups, civil liberties groups, good government groups as well as organized labor. And together I’m confident we’re going to ensure that there’s a free and fair election in November.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Last question. I’m out of time, but I must ask you. Your Caucus is heading into an August recess with momentum toward the election but plenty of uncertainty. We don’t know what Trump and Republicans will do, how far they will go to try and undermine our democracy as they cling to power. We don’t know how tensions will play out between progressives and centrists inside the Democratic Party. So what’s your message to Members and to the candidates out there as we enter this critical stretch, the final 100 days?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Important for all of us to continue to keep the main thing the main thing. And that’s our commitment to fighting for an affordable America. Wherever one falls on the Democratic spectrum, we know that everyone is unified behind that fight. We want to lower the high cost of living for the American people. We want to make sure that there’s affordable healthcare for every single American. And we’re all committed to holding the crooks accountable and dealing with the rampant corruption that is undermining the Congress’ ability and our government’s ability to actually deliver for hardworking American taxpayers. Let’s keep the main thing the main thing. Let’s run through the finish line over the next 100 days or so. And then together, we can end this national nightmare, take back control of the Congress and continue our country’s march toward a more perfect union.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Well, thank you for being with us as we start the 100-day countdown to the election, Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries.

Full interview can be watched here.

HOUSTON, TX — Yesterday, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) joined Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Congressman Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Congressman Bennie G. Thompson (MS-02), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Homeland Security and 7 additional Members of Congress from across the country for a congressional hearing in Houston examining the fatal shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Held at the Harris County Commissioners Court, right in Congressman Menefee’s district, the hearing brought Lorenzo's family, local officials, faith leaders, legal experts, and community advocates together to examine ICE's use of deadly force, the agency's lack of transparency, and the urgent need for accountability following Lorenzo's death.

Congressman Menefee questioned Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare about ICE agents' failure to wear body cameras during the fatal encounter, highlighting what both agreed is a striking departure from modern law enforcement practices.

Rep. Menefee: "Throughout your career, you've worked on thousands of cases involving local law enforcement, correct?"

District Attorney Sean Teare: "Yes."

Rep. Menefee: "It's standard practice in 2026 for law enforcement officers on the street to wear body cameras, correct?"

District Attorney Sean Teare: "Congressman, you and I have been in this very room talking about things like this. We have 86 law enforcement agencies that operate in Harris County alone. The only one that doesn't have body cameras is ICE."

Following the hearing, Congressman Menefee condemned the agency's lack of accountability.

"This is an agency that needs to be torn down to the studs and rebuilt into one that enforces immigration law while recognizing the dignity of every person it encounters," said Congressman Menefee. "We all know that won't happen under this Administration, and it won't happen under this Republican-controlled Congress."

Congressman Menefee also emphasized that meaningful oversight will require a change in congressional leadership, stating that if Democrats regain control of the U.S. House of Representatives after the November midterm elections, one of their first priorities will be conducting a full congressional investigation into the death of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and other deaths involving ICE agents since President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025.

Since Lorenzo's death, Congressman Menefee has repeatedly called for the immediate release of all unedited evidence, including body camera and dash camera footage, demanded an independent investigation into the shooting, and pushed for transparency and accountability for Lorenzo's family and the Houston community.
title: Rep. Menefee Joins Congressional Leaders in Houston to Demand Answers in the Killing of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo

Hernández propone reforma al financiamiento de campañas para combatir "la corrupción de la claque”
CAYEY, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, marcó hoy el 74.º aniversario del Estado Libre Asociado con un mensaje contundente contra lo que denominó "la corrupción de la claque": una red de funcionarios de distintos partidos que, según Hernández, antepone intereses propios al servicio público y pone en riesgo miles de millones en fondos federales de reconstrucción. "La claque son los que se compran y se venden, los que confunden servir con servirse", afirmó, citando casos recientes de nombramientos y contratos gubernamentales cuestionados.
Entre ellos, el escándalo en el Departamento de Desarrollo Económico y Comercio que llevó al senador federal Mike Lee a cuestionar directamente a la gobernadora sobre el manejo de fondos de reconstrucción. El riesgo, dijo Hernández, no es hipotético: la semana pasada el Departamento de Vivienda federal congeló más de $1,000 millones destinados a las Islas Vírgenes tras hallazgos de corrupción. "No queremos que eso le pase a Puerto Rico", advirtió.
Para atajar ese riesgo, Hernández identificó el financiamiento de campañas como una de las causas principales de la corrupción pública en Puerto Rico y presentó cuatro reformas para controlar el inversionismo político:
- Limitar más o prohibir los donativos en efectivo, para dificultar el lavado de dinero.
- Limitar más o prohibir los donativos anónimos, luego de que candidatos a la gobernación y partidos recibieran más de $1 millón de fuentes anónimas en las pasadas elecciones.
- Limitar más o prohibir las donaciones de contratistas del Gobierno, para reducir el inversionismo político.
- Requerir que las campañas divulguen dónde trabaja cada donante de cierta cantidad, y que el Contralor Electoral publique esa información.
La urgencia, explicó, está en lo laxo de las reglas actuales frente a las federales: un contratista federal no puede donar a candidatos federales, pero uno estatal en Puerto Rico puede donar hasta $3,300 a un candidato estatal. Además, puede donar hasta $3,300 en efectivo, contrario al límite de $100 en efectivo a nivel federal. A eso se suma el abuso de la regla que permite $50 en donativos anónimos, que fueron más de $1 millón de dólares entre todos los candidatos y partidos en 2024.
Hernández ilustró el riesgo de ese vacío: "Un contratista saca $100,000 en efectivo. Ese dinero se disfraza como donativos anónimos de $50 en un radiomaratón, o se reparte entre decenas de empleados públicos para que compren, a su nombre, boletos de $2,500 a un evento político. Violaron la ley, pero no hay manera efectiva de detectarlo: nadie tiene cómo saber de dónde salió el dinero, ni cuestionar cómo un empleado público que vive cheque a cheque tiene $2,500 en efectivo para donar a un político. El candidato gana — y el contratista recupera su inversión con un contrato de gobierno muy superior a los $100,000 originales.”
Hernández reconoció que no le sorprendería que personas de otros partidos ya hayan propuesto implantar restricciones similares en Puerto Rico. “Si es así, me uno a ellos. Las ideas no son de un líder, partido, o alianza … las ideas simplemente son buenas o malas. Y debemos estar con las ideas buenas, siempre.”
El mensaje llega una semana después de que Hernández señalara públicamente, en Barranquitas, a funcionarios de varios partidos vinculados a nombramientos y contratos cuestionados — señalamientos que, según dijo, ya provocaron la salida de algunos de sus puestos.
Hernández cerró invocando la constitución de 1952 y las palabras de Luis Muñoz Marín sobre la responsabilidad de sembrar bien para las generaciones futuras, y concluyó con un llamado que repitió tres veces: "El pueblo contra la claque”.
Puede ver una conferencia de prensa después del evento AQUÍ.

title: Hernández propone reforma al financiamiento de campañas para combatir "la corrupción de la claque”

Washington, D.C. – This week, Congressman Shri Thanedar (D-MI-13) and Congressman Bennie G. Thompson (D-MS-02), Ranking Member of the House Homeland Security Committee, introduced H.R.9882, the DHS Acquisition Documentation Integrity Act, legislation that creates objective procedures for how the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) should use public funds to carry out its responsibilities to protect our homeland.

“The Department of Homeland Security’s duties to protect the American people are some of our country’s most serious,” said Congressman Shri Thanedar. “In order to strengthen the American people’s confidence in this work, our federal agencies must follow transparent processes when they spend taxpayer dollars. It’s why I introduced the DHS Acquisition Documentation Integrity Act, legislation that requires DHS to institute and follow processes that prioritize solutions that best address our national security needs, and to introduce accountability measures when the agency fails to do so. I am grateful to Homeland Security Committee Ranking Member Bennie G. Thompson for joining this legislation as an original cosponsor, and I look forward to continuing our work together on the Committee.”

“DHS invests billions of taxpayer dollars each year in acquisition programs that are vital to our national security. But for too long, some of the Department’s largest programs have been plagued by missed deadlines and high costs.” said Ranking Member Thompson “This legislation will help keep these programs on track, and protect taxpayer dollars. I thank Congressman Thanedar for his leadership on this important bill.”

The full text of the legislation can be viewed here.

Congressman Shri Thanedar proudly represents Michigan's 13th Congressional District, which includes Detroit, Downriver, and the Grosse Pointes. As a champion for working families, Shri is committed to advancing economic opportunities, education, healthcare access, and entrepreneurship for underserved communities. Drawing from his journey from poverty to success, he works tirelessly to uplift Metro Detroit, ensuring every resident has the resources and support they need to thrive.

title: Congressmen Shri Thanedar, Bennie G. Thompson Introduce DHS Acquisition Documentation Integrity Act

Washington D.C. — Today, Congressman Herb Conaway Jr., MD and Congressman Gregory Murphy, MD introduced the Protecting Patients from Automated Denials Act. This bipartisan bill would establish safeguards on the use of artificial intelligence in Medicare Advantage prior authorization decisions.

Under the bill, any AI-assisted denial must be reviewed and approved by a qualified physician under the supervision of the plan’s medical director. It also requires physicians to attest that they exercised independent medical judgement and that the denial was not generated or dictated by AI. Additionally, the bill grants the Department of Health and Human Services the authority to audit and inspect AI use in prior authorization decisions, including reviewing denial data, internal policies, algorithms, employee practices, and overturn rates.

“Artificial intelligence is dramatically changing the technology and healthcare industries, but we need to ensure that patients aren’t being left behind,” said Congressman Conaway, MD. “This legislation establishes necessary physician oversight and will increase transparency with the federal audit requirements to make sure patient claims aren’t being wrongfully denied.”

“Artificial intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing healthcare at the speed of light, but we must protect the physician-in-the-loop," said Congressman Greg Murphy, MD. "While advancements in diagnostics, research, and administrative work will advance medicine in incredible ways, the value of a trained physician and sentient influence cannot be eroded. This is especially important for prior authorization decisions - patients are not merely numbers on a spreadsheet. We cannot allow greedy health insurers to utilize AI to deny healthcare to those in need. I am proud to lead on this issue by establishing sensible guardrails that ensure the proliferation of AI in the field of medicine does no harm.”

“Artificial intelligence is no substitute for a highly trained physician. Medicare Advantage plans should not be permitted to empower AI to make prior authorization decisions, especially denials of medically necessary treatment. We strongly support the provision requiring that physicians oversee any initial prior authorization denial that stems from the use of artificial intelligence. Our patients are being denied care by AI that doesn’t know them, their circumstances, or the nuances of their treatment – and doesn’t care! We applaud Reps. Herb Conaway, MD (D-NJ) and Greg Murphy, MD (R-NC) for introducing the Protecting Patients From Automated Denials Act, and our patients will be grateful and healthier when it becomes law.” AMA President Willie Underwood III, MD, MSc, MPH
title: Conaway and Murphy Introduce Bill to Protect Patients from AI-Assisted Insurance Denials

text:
Washington, D.C. -- Today, Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), who serves on the House Oversight and Government Reform and Homeland Security Committees, secured House passage of his amendment to more efficiently deploy modern cybersecurity solutions within the Department of Defense (Dod), strengthen military cyber readiness, and encourage the concept of interagency reciprocity with regard to cloud security assessments and certifications.

The amendment establishes a pilot program to help the DoD deploy modern cybersecurity tools more efficiently by accelerating review of cloud-based products that have already received FedRAMP High certification, the federal government's highest cloud security standard for handling sensitive unclassified information.

By encouraging reciprocity between FedRAMP and DoD's cloud security assessment processes, the amendment saves taxpayer resources and helps ensure America's servicemembers have faster access to proven commercial cybersecurity capabilities.

"At a time when cyber threats from our adversaries are becoming more sophisticated, the DoD must continue to improve efficiency around how it securely deploys proven cybersecurity tools," said Congressman Walkinshaw. "My amendment will help the Department speed up the process of assessing solutions that have already been vetted for federal agency use, while upholding rigorous security standards and helping ensure our servicemembers have access to the innovative capabilities they need to defend our nation."

Currently, cloud service providers seeking to serve both civilian federal agencies and the DoD must complete separate security assessment processes, even though both rely on the same underlying National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) cybersecurity standards.

Walkinshaw's amendment makes that process more efficient by helping DoD deploy trusted cybersecurity solutions faster while upholding the rigorous security standards our military and national security depend on.

The amendment was included in the House-passed FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act.

###
title: Walkinshaw Amendment to Speed up Pentagon’s Adoption of Cybersecurity Tools Passes House

Hollywood, FL – Today, U.S. Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz joined Overtown Youth Centers (OYC) Co-Founder Alonzo Mourning, Broward School District representatives, and local elected officials to announce OYC’s expansion into Broward County.

Click here to watch the full press conference.

In partnership with Broward County Public Schools (BCPS), OYC is further expanding its proven youth development model to communities in South Broward County. Through an official agreement with Broward County Public Schools, OYC expanded its programming to McNicol Middle School in Summer 2026 and will continue through the new school year.

The expansion will also offer OYC services at McNicol Middle School to students from four nearby elementary schools. This represents a strategic investment in increasing access to high-quality, outcome-driven programming for more students and families.

“I'm ecstatic that the Overtown Youth Center will bring its proven, holistic model for family and child success to Broward County,” said Wasserman Schultz. “If we truly want all our children to travel on a path of success, they must have access to sound nutrition and tutoring, STEM and arts education, and the family support systems that make it all possible. This proven enrichment blueprint is just the type of empowering infrastructure that our Broward communities deserve, and I'll support these efforts any way that I can. I'm also very proud that our Broward County School District leaders and Hollywood Mayor Josh Levy are teaming with community leader and OYC architect Alonzo Mourning, to embrace this amazing expansion opportunity to support our children and families.”

“For 25 years, I have been committed to ensuring that children and families have access to the high-quality programs they need to thrive. I know firsthand that there are a lot of champions in our communities; and my goal is to galvanize resources for our families and to nurture the gifts and talents of our young people. Through OYC and Honey Shine, our goal is to provide empowering, enriching and exposure opportunities that positions all those we serve to compete and win in this world, and I am proud to strengthen that mission through our partnership with Broward County Public Schools,” said Mourning.

“This partnership reflects our shared commitment to ensuring every child has access to meaningful opportunities that support academic growth, personal development, and long-term success. We are proud to welcome OYC’s proven programming into our schools and to expand the resources available to students and families in South Broward,” said Broward School Board Member Maura McCarthy Bulman.

OYC is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization whose mission is to inspire, empower, and enrich the lives of youth, adults, and families by providing a comprehensive and long-term approach to strengthening communities.
title: Wasserman Schultz Joins Mourning, Overtown Youth Center to Announce Broward Expansion

Harder led calls for NIH to join national initiative connecting scientists, artificial intelligence, supercomputers, and federal research data

New mission aims to use artificial intelligence to cure cancer, Alzheimer's two times faster

WASHINGTON – Today, following his calls for new biomedical research infrastructure, Rep. Josh Harder (CA-09) celebrated the launch of a new partnership between the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and the Genesis Mission, a new federal research initiative designed to speed up breakthrough science. Harder pushed language to expand the Genesis Mission and support AI-driven drug discovery at the NIH, which was included in the FY27 LHHS Appropriations bill leading up to this partnership. The NIH’s new Bio Genesis Mission will connect scientists, federal datasets, artificial intelligence and advanced computing to accelerate biomedical research and get new treatments to patients faster.

"The scientists on the front lines fighting cancer, Alzheimer's, and the diseases that touch every American family deserve the best tools this country can offer," said Rep. Harder. "I pushed for NIH to join the Genesis Mission because breakthroughs happen faster when our researchers have AI and advanced computing at their fingertips. This launch is a major step toward finding new cures, lowering the cost of treatments, and getting lifesaving medicine to patients faster."

The Mission will initially focus on six major biomedical challenges:

Unlocking Pediatric Cancer Cures – The mission will apply AI to research across hundreds of rare childhood cancer subtypes to help identify new treatments and accelerate the search for cures.

Faster Drug Discovery – Researchers will use AI and advanced computing to identify promising new medicines and find new uses for treatments that already exist.

Chronic Disease Research – The initiative will combine health, environmental, and biological data to better understand the root causes of chronic diseases.

More Predictive Biomedical Models – Scientists will work to improve their ability to predict how living systems behave, helping researchers develop and test treatments more effectively.

Stronger Biosecurity – The mission will use AI to identify biological threats earlier and strengthen the country’s ability to respond.

American Biomanufacturing – The initiative will help turn scientific discoveries into medicines and technologies that can be produced here in the United States.

Read Harder’s letter to NIH Director Jay Bhattacharya and White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios here.

Harder is also leading bipartisan, landmark legislation to invest in higher-risk, higher-reward research at the NIH by creating a new, four-part funding series at the agency dedicated to foundational discovery, toolbuilding, biomedical regranting, and new institution seeding. Harder also serves as Chair of the bipartisan Build America Caucus, which was founded to pass pro-growth policies across infrastructure, energy, housing, health care, and technology.

###
title: GENESIS MISSION: Harder Celebrates New Partnership Between NIH and Genesis Mission to Accelerate New Cures

WASHINGTON – Today, Representative Brittany Pettersen (D-CO) led 45 members in calling on the Trump Administration to reverse course on their policy effort to politicize the federal grantmaking process, allowing political appointees to have the final say on whether or not communities receive taxpayer funding. In her letter to Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Director Russel Vought and Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Pettersen specifically highlights the importance of non-partisan grant making for programs under the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), which would also be at risk under the administration's proposal.

“My mom, like far too many Americans, struggled with substance abuse disorder for decades until she was finally able to get the help she needed and enter recovery. In the fight to save her life, I realized just how broken our health care system is, especially for mental health and substance use. I’ve spent 15 years in elected office building up our behavioral health system, and it has worked. Colorado recently saw a 35% reduction in fentanyl-related deaths,” said Rep. Pettersen. “But Trump wants to backtrack on all the progress we have made. SAMHSA performs critical work, and its grants make sure communities in Colorado, especially our rural areas, have access to high-quality care when they need it. I am so lucky that my mom was able to get help, but that opportunity should be open to everyone who needs it. Federal grants are existential for many of these treatment programs, and we must ensure they continue to be awarded based on evidence, not by Trump's political goals and vendettas.”

In the letter, the members wrote, “The proposed rule would fundamentally alter how federal grants are awarded by shifting decision-making away from an established, neutral criteria. Instead of relying on statutory requirements, expert agency review, and merit‑based evaluation, the rule would allow appointed officials to decide which communities, institutions, and programs receive federal support. It’s a sharp break from long‑standing Uniform Guidance.”

The members continued, “The proposed rule would undermine the longevity of vital programs, including those that support care for mental health and substance use disorder in the United States. By destabilizing the very framework that enables sustained federal investment in these services, the rule threatens the backbone of our national response and the programs that rely on predictable, reliable grant administration to reach the communities most in need.”

SAMHSA operates grant programs that help states and local communities prevent and treat substance use disorder, expand mental health services, strengthen the behavioral health workforce, and support crisis response and suicide prevention efforts. These efforts have shown incredible success, with preliminary data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) showing a 14% drop in overdose deaths in 2025. But earlier this year, SAMHSA terminated over 2,000 grants — totaling more than $2 billion — deepening widespread insecurity across our federal grantmaking system. After pressure from Congresswoman Pettersen, the Trump Administration reversed this decision.

Trump’s Office of Management and Budget’s (OMB) so-called “Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance” would fundamentally alter how federal grants are awarded by shifting away from an established, neutral criteria, instead allowing political appointees to determine which communities, institutions, and programs receive federal support. This is an unprecedented move, which would further their efforts to use the federal government as a tool to settle political scores against certain states and communities rather than a non-partisan support for the American people.

Colorado has been a consistent target of the Trump Administration’s politically motivated funding attacks. The Administration has moved to freeze more than $300 million for child care and other essential services, $94 million from Jefferson County Public Schools, and canceled $109 million in transportation grants for rail safety improvements, public transit, and electric vehicle infrastructure. These were resources already approved to help Colorado families and communities, but the Administration withheld them because Colorado would not fall in line with its political agenda. This proposed rule would give the Administration broad authority to deny federal funding from specific communities and localities, further jeopardizing the services and development projects that Coloradans rely on.

This rule also comes in the aftermath of over two years of grant instability caused by widespread impoundment, cancellations, and delays of federal funding under the Trump Administration. Millions of organizations, local governments, and providers in every state depend on federal funding through the grantmaking process to perform essential services and critical scientific and medical research. One-third of nonprofits reported experiencing a disruption in government funding in the first months of 2025, including 21 percent that lost funding and 27 percent that experienced a delay, pause, or freeze. These disruptions have forced child care providers, schools, local governments, health care organizations, and research institutions to operate under constant uncertainty, threatening the services families rely on and the research that drives American innovation and strengthens our global standing.

Rather than correcting the instability of recent years, this rule risks deepening it — creating new barriers, injecting additional uncertainty into the grantmaking process, and undermining the ability of communities to plan and deliver the programs Americans depend on.

Rep. Pettersen has consistently spoken out against the Trump Administration’s politicization of federal funding and its targeting of Colorado and the resources families rely on. Rep. Pettersen led 83 members of the Democratic delegation alongside Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi in demanding that the Trump Administration immediately reverse course on its freeze of over $10 billion in child care funding for five Democratic-led states. After this pressure, the Trump Administration recently announced that it would lift its freeze.

The full version of Pettersen’s latest letter can be found here and below:

Dear Director Vought:

We write to express our deep concerns with the Office of Management and Budget’s (OMB) proposed rule, “Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance,” released on May 29, 2026. This rule would revise Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards, otherwise known as “Uniform Guidance,” and it carries significant implications for our mental health and substance use disorder services and systems. Uniform Guidance has existed for over a decade. It serves as the framework for managing financial assistance while also consolidating OMB requirements for federal awards. This guidance has historically supported the financial and physical security of federal grant operations, providing a durable oversight structure that safeguards federal dollars, preserves interagency integrity, and anchors the stability that the proposed rule now places at risk.

The proposed rule would fundamentally alter how federal grants are awarded by shifting decision-making away from an established, neutral criteria and toward processes that could allow for political influence over funding determinations. Instead of relying on statutory requirements, expert agency review, and merit‑based evaluation, the rule would invite political actors to decide which communities, institutions, and programs receive federal support. It’s a sharp break from long‑standing Uniform Guidance.

The proposed rule would undermine the longevity of vital programs, including those that support care for mental health and substance use disorder in the United States. By destabilizing the very framework that enables sustained federal investment in these services, the rule threatens the backbone of our national response and the programs that rely on predictable, reliable grant administration to reach the communities most in need. Our concerns arise from recent instances that have demonstrated the importance of safeguarding the foundation, stability, and predictability of Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) grants.

In January 2026, SAMHSA announced the abrupt termination of over 2,000 grants, totaling more than $2 billion. Upon notification, awardees received minimal justification regarding the cancellation. Only twenty-four hours later, administration officials rescinded this decision confirming that all impacted grant funding would be restored. Despite this reinstatement, the unanticipated announcement sent awardees across the country into widespread alarm. The whiplash of termination, reinstatement, and subsequent recovery time demonstrated how fragile program stability becomes when foundational guardrails are weakened, underscoring the critical need to safeguard predictability for SAMHSA grantees and the communities they serve.

Funding for substance use disorder treatment and mental health services is not a partisan priority; it is a responsibility of the government and must not be left to the priorities of political actors. All fifty states and the District of Columbia offer programs and strategically invest in resources and services to support individuals with substance use disorder and those living with mental health conditions. Combatting this epidemic and reducing overdose deaths remains a collaborative effort. Preliminary data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) demonstrates a 13% decline in U.S. overdose deaths this year. This decline is the result of long-term investment in substance use disorder funding and resources, and further progress must not be delayed or threatened. Individuals, communities, and families across the nation are depending on reliable resources that are anchored to dependable funding sources, including the federal investments that sustain critical mental health and substance use disorder programs.

Given the overwhelming support to preserve and protect grant funding that expands access to treatment and resources for mental health and substance use disorder, we request that OMB immediately repeal any proposed changes to Uniform Guidance. At a moment when progress against overdose deaths is finally emerging and demand for mental health services continues to rise, it is essential that we maintain, not weaken, the foundation that allows these lifesaving programs to operate. Fracturing that foundation would jeopardize the future of critical services that individuals, families, and communities depend on every day.

We appreciate your attention to this matter.

Sincerely,
title: As Trump Moves to Politicize Federal Grants, Rep. Pettersen Leads Push to Protect Mental Health and Substance Use Treatment Funding

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), alongside Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) and Congresswoman Terri Sewell (AL-07), led 52 of their House Democratic colleagues in urging Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz to rescind a final rule that allows health insurance companies to offer loans to Affordable Care Act enrollees to cover their deductibles and other medical costs. This rule will place health insurers in a new role as loan officers, potentially allowing these companies to subject patients to predatory interest rates or condition care on patients’ ability to pay back their loans.

In June, the New York Times reported on the rule and the strain many Americans are already dealing with as insurance premiums and healthcare costs rise, highlighting that 36% of U.S. households have medical debt.

“100 million Americans are currently living under the weight of medical debt and now the Trump administration is proposing making the load even heavier,” said Congresswoman Ocasio-Cortez. “This will only further entrench working families in a never-ending cycle of medical debt, and could lead health insurers to require repayment before people can renew their insurance plans or receive the care they need.”

“Every American should have quality, affordable healthcare with providers they know and trust when and where they need it,” said Congressman Schneider. “Sadly, thanks to President Trump and Congressional Republicans’ refusal to extend the ACA tax credits, millions of families have lost access to healthcare, and millions more have seen their healthcare costs skyrocket this year. We should be working together on solutions that lower costs and expand access to care. Instead, the Trump Administration is inviting insurers to profit off of our nation’s growing medical debt crisis. The Administration must rescind this predatory rule and better focus on advancing policies that make healthcare more accessible, more affordable, and more sustainable for American families.”

“The Trump Administration and Congressional Republicans have spent the past year making health care more expensive for American families—allowing ACA premium tax credits to expire, driving up premiums, and stealing coverage from more than a million Americans,” said Congresswoman Sewell. “Now, instead of fixing the problem they created, they're encouraging insurance companies to offer loans to patients who can't afford sky-high deductibles. This policy will push more Americans deeper into medical debt, forcing them to borrow money just to access the care they need. Every American deserves affordable, quality health care they can count on, not a system that profits from families' financial hardship. As Co-Convener of House Democrats' Cost of Living Healthcare Working Group, I'll keep fighting to lower costs and put patients first.”

“Since this Administration allowed the Affordable Care Act (ACA) enhanced tax credits to expire at the end of last year, there has been a 58% average increase in out-of-pocket premiums in 2026 per person,” the lawmakers wrote. “This trend is expected to continue as rates are set for 2027, with a recent analysis indicating a median proposed premium increase of an additional 14%. This cost increase, adding to an already intense affordability crisis, has resulted in 1.2 million Americans losing health coverage all together.”

“Ultimately, this Administration has deliberately constructed plans with deductibles that most enrollees cannot afford to pay and is allowing the same insurer who sold the unaffordable plan to offer the enrollee a loan to cover the gap, presumably with interest, and under terms established entirely by the issuer,” the lawmakers continued. “Health insurance was designed to help families during their darkest moments, not profit off denying Americans care and perpetuating prolonged illness. This policy incentivizes health plans to profit off their own enrollees’ medical debt, not provide Americans adequate health coverage.”

View the full letter text here.

###
title: Ocasio-Cortez, Schneider, Sewell, Lead 52 Democrats Urging Secretary Kennedy and Administrator Oz to Rescind Trump Policy to Allow Health Insurance Companies to Offer Predatory Loans

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Reps. George Whitesides (D-CA) and Jay Obernolte (R-CA) introduced the bipartisan PILOT (Providing Increased Local Opportunities for Test-pilots) Act to study expanding job opportunities for civilian pilots and engineers trained at local flight schools. Under current law, flight test professionals trained at civilian flight schools, like the National Test Pilot School in Mojave, have to go through an additional waiver process when applying for military flight testing positions, which makes it more difficult for candidates from civilian flight schools to be considered. By ordering a review of the current military test pilot capacity and the possibility of changing the waiver policy, the PILOT Act takes steps to reduce barriers for local pilots and engineers.

“Our district is home to so many dedicated flight test professionals looking to assist our military with flight testing, who often face barriers to certain opportunities based on existing requirements and bureaucracy,” said Rep. Whitesides. “The PILOT Act studies the prospect of expanding access to high-quality jobs for qualified candidates in our area who have graduated from accredited flight schools and want to pursue public service. By removing bureaucratic obstacles that block local pilots from job opportunities, we can draw from the immense local talent we have here at home.”

“Test pilots and flight test engineers are essential to ensuring the safety and effectiveness of the advanced aircraft and systems our military depends on,” said Rep. Obernolte. “The PILOT Act will help the Department of Defense evaluate whether graduates of accredited U.S. civilian test pilot schools can play a greater role in supporting military test activities while maintaining the rigorous training standards this work requires. This is a responsible step toward strengthening our test pilot workforce and supporting the next generation of American aerospace innovation.”

“For more than four decades, the National Test Pilot School has provided high quality, professional flight test training to military and commercial aerospace organizations from around the world,” said Jeff Trang, National Test Pilot School CEO. “The PILOT Act provides critical legislation that will enable NTPS to better complement the U.S. military Test Pilot Schools, by increasing training capacity and creating training opportunities not otherwise available for civil servants and civilian flight test professionals. Congressman Whitesides understands that this legislation will play a key role in accelerating DoD’s flight test activities, essential to its efforts in fast-tracking state-of-the-art capabilities to the operational warfighter. I look forward to continued collaboration with the Congressman in supporting the local flight test community at Edwards AFB, USAF Plant 42, and Defense partners across the Antelope Valley.”

The legislationdirects the Department of Defense to review whether the number of civilian test pilots meets their current test flight needs and look into ways to expand opportunities for graduates of accredited civilian flight schools. By assessing opportunities to make the application process more efficient and easier to navigate, the PILOT Act will help lower the barrier to entry for qualified local pilots.

###
title: Reps. Whitesides and Obernolte Introduce Bipartisan PILOT Act to Expand Job Opportunities for Local Civilian Pilots and Engineers

Federal Award, Paired With $1,301,438 in Matching Funds, Brings Total Investment in Buffalo Service Corps, ABLE Early Childhood, and YouthBuild Buffalo to More Than $4.1 Million

AmeriCorps- and U.S. Department of Labor-Funded Programs Set to Launch This Fall, Serving Hundreds of Children, Youth, and Young Adults Across Western New York

BUFFALO, N.Y. — Standing outside of a new home constructed with the aid of the previous cohort of YouthBuild Buffalo participants, Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) joined leadership from The Service Collaborative of WNY (TSC) to announce $2,895,322 in federal funding, leveraged by an additional $1,301,438 in matching funds, to support three of the organization’s flagship workforce development initiatives. Together, the investments total more than $4.1 million dedicated to preparing the next generation of workers and community leaders throughout Western New York. The funding includes grants awarded by AmeriCorps for Buffalo Service Corps and ABLE Early Childhood, and by the U.S. Department of Labor for YouthBuild Buffalo. All three programs are set to launch in Fall 2026.

“Investing in our young people and our workforce is one of the smartest investments Western New York can make,” said Congressman Kennedy. “The Service Collaborative has spent years proving what strong programming, fiscal discipline, and community partnership can accomplish for our region. This funding will help hundreds of children, teenagers, and young adults across Erie and Niagara Counties build the skills, credentials, and confidence they need to succeed, while also helping their fellow community members. Western New Yorkers deserve exactly this kind of investment in their future, and I’m proud to help deliver it.”

“In a year when federal funding nationwide has been anything but certain, we set out to submit the strongest applications in our organization’s history — and we delivered,” said Kate Sarata, Executive Director of The Service Collaborative of WNY. “This recognition speaks to what TSC does best: exceptional programming, fiscal discipline, and operational excellence. We take our role as stewards of federal investment seriously — and we’ve proven we’re worthy of it.”

New York State Senator April N.M. Baskin said, “For more than 30 years, The Service Collaborative has been changing lives by equipping young people and adults with the skills, training, and opportunities they need to build successful careers while strengthening our community. I was proud to secure $70,000 in State funding last year to support this important work, and I'm thrilled to see Congressman Kennedy and our federal partners recognize the tremendous value this organization brings to Western New York's workforce and economy.”

"The Service Collaborative has earned a reputation for changing lives by creating pathways to education, workforce development, and public service,” said Senator Jeremy Zellner. “I thank Congressman Tim Kennedy for securing this critical federal investment, which will strengthen programs that empower young people, build our workforce, and invest in the future of Western New York."

Assemblymember Jon D. Rivera said, “By supporting organizations like The Service Collaborative, Buffalo Service Corps, ABLE Early Childhood, and YouthBuild Buffalo, we're helping young people gain valuable job skills, preparing future educators, and investing in the next generation of community leaders. Just as importantly, these programs are making a tangible difference here in Western New York, from building affordable homes to expanding educational opportunities and connecting residents with meaningful careers. I want to thank Congressman Tim Kennedy for his leadership in securing this critical federal funding and for continuing to champion investments that empower people, strengthen neighborhoods, and build a brighter future for Buffalo.”

The ABLE Early Childhood program mobilizes AmeriCorps members to implement evidence-informed math interventions with small groups of 3- to 6-year-olds in Erie and Niagara counties. Forty AmeriCorps members will serve 290 students during the school year and in summer programming. Since its inception in 2019, ABLE Early Childhood has positively impacted more than 500 children from low-income households, addressing critical gaps in math readiness crucial for kindergarten preparedness.

The Buffalo Service Corps grant will engage 91 AmeriCorps members serving throughout Buffalo in environmental stewardship and career and workforce development activities. These members will assist with the landscaping of 705 acres of city parks and rain gardens, and the program’s summer members will support community outreach efforts of local partners, delivering education on conservation and environmental stewardship topics to more than 1,000 individuals of all ages. The previous AmeriCorps cohort completed 46 work orders covering 128,923 square feet of rain gardens and bioswales, and members removed 4,971 pounds of debris from 32 parks covering 632 acres.

The YouthBuild Buffalo grant will serve 74 young adults through an integrated education and workforce development model that combines academic support, leadership development, and hands-on career training in construction, advanced manufacturing, and customer service/hospitality. In the first six months of 2026, YouthBuild Buffalo served 67 youth, with 99% completing an education or workforce credential and more than 63% placed into employment or higher education, including 16 additional completions, 13 industry-recognized credentials earned in customer service and advanced manufacturing, and 2 NYS High School Equivalency Diplomas.

These awards reinforce TSC’s long-standing commitment to building a stronger Western New York by addressing workforce needs while strengthening communities through service. By connecting individuals to education, industry-recognized credentials, employment opportunities, and civic engagement, The Service Collaborative continues to invest in people who will shape the future of the region. Kennedy will continue to champion the federal investments that connect Western New York’s children, youth, and young adults to the skills and opportunities they need to succeed.

###
title: Investing in the Next Generation: Congressman Kennedy Announces $2.9 Million in Federal Funding for The Service Collaborative of WNY’s Workforce Development Programs

ORLANDO, FL — Today, Congressman Darren Soto (FL-09) hosted a press conference at Orlando International Airport (MCO) to announce over $36 million in U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) funds for MCO. He was joined by City of Orlando Commissioner Tom Keen and union representatives.

“We are proud to announce another $36 million in federal funding for MCO, which builds upon the $33 million recently awarded from the Airport Terminals Program to modernize public restrooms and enhance family facilities,” said Rep. Soto. "Since passing the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, we’ve worked to secure over $500 million in funding for MCO—more than any other Florida airport. As Congress works on a new Infrastructure Law, we must ensure that it includes airports, ports, water, and electric grid projects in addition to roads, bridges, and road transportation projects.”

“It is critical for us to maintain the infrastructure that supports our airport in order for it to continue running efficiently,” said Commissioner Tom Keen. “I thank Congressman Soto for his leadership to ensure the over 58 million people who visit our airport have a smooth travel experience.”

“It is important to recognize leaders who understand what a strong airport depends on. Keeping our airport running boosts the local economy and helps thousands of workers maintain their jobs,” said TWU Local 555 Representative Edgar Jimenez. “We thank Congressman Soto for supporting working families and investing in the future of Central Florida.”
