Following a weekend of dangerously poor air quality across the Washington region, Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), joined by Representatives Don Beyer (VA-08), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), and Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC) introduced the bipartisan Federal Facilities Indoor Air Quality Assessment Act to identify and address air quality and ventilation problems across federal buildings.

Recently, wildfire smoke pushed the region into Code Purple conditions, meaning the air was considered very unhealthy for everyone.

“Last week’s dangerous air quality was a stark reminder that clean indoor air is essential to protecting public health,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “Federal employees should never have to risk their health by showing up to work, yet the General Services Administration’s own watchdog has identified persistent ventilation problems in federal buildings. Our bipartisan bill will uncover these deficiencies and require agencies to develop concrete plans to fix them.”

“Too many of our federal buildings have aging ventilation and systems that may no longer meet modern standards. We know that indoor air quality impacts the health and productivity of our workforce and as outside threats like wildfire smoke and other climate-driven impacts become more common and further threaten indoor air quality, we have a responsibility to protect the health and well-being of the public servants who keep our government running,” said Congressman Beyer. “Our bill would provide the comprehensive information needed to identify deficiencies in air quality and ventilation standards, guide necessary improvements, and help ensure our federal workforce can breathe clean, healthy air in the workplace.”

“The federal government should lead by example when it comes to protecting the health and safety of its workforce,” said Congressman Fitzpatrick. “The men and women who serve the American people should never be placed at risk by preventable failures in the buildings where they work. This bipartisan bill will identify those failures, demand corrective action, and ensure our federal facilities meet the standard our public servants deserve.”

“In recent weeks, communities across the Northeast have experienced the public health harms that stem from unsafe air quality,” said Congressman Tonko. “We know that poor air quality can lead to negative health impacts in both the short and long term. But for too many Americans, poor ventilation and filtration in our buildings mean that even spending time indoors does not offer adequate protection. Our government must do more to address indoor air quality, and we can start by improving ventilation and filtration in federal facilities across the nation. That’s why I’m proud to support the Federal Facilities Indoor Air Quality Assessment Act, a bipartisan bill that will help our government lead by example and ensure that our hardworking federal employees have a safe, healthy environment in which to work on behalf of the American people.”

“Federal employees should never have to wonder whether the air in their own workplace is safe to breathe,” Congresswoman Norton said. “I'm proud to join Congressman Walkinshaw and this bipartisan coalition in cosponsoring the Federal Facilities Indoor Air Quality Assessment Act. GAO's review will finally give us the data we need to hold GSA and federal agencies accountable for the ventilation problems their own watchdog has already flagged. This is a commonsense, bipartisan step, and I urge my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to support it.”

“We are proud to endorse the bipartisan Federal Facilities Indoor Air Quality Assessment Act, innovative and long overdue legislation introduced by Rep. James Walkinshaw (D-VA) and three longtime champions for safe and healthy indoor air quality, Reps. Paul Tonko (D-NY), Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA), and Don Beyer (D-VA). While many public officials are speaking out now due to the hazardous smoke covering many states in our nation, these four Members of Congress have advocated for assessing HVAC deficiencies and remediating indoor air quality dangers for many years at the local, state and federal levels, especially in schools, military facilities and all types of public buildings. Our firms are the leaders in the installation of IAQ mechanical systems in existing buildings and facilities and in new public facility construction projects. These highly skilled construction corporations and their skilled workforce know well that countless thousands of public employees and the millions of our citizens who visit public buildings nationwide will benefit from such a valuable federal effort. The Federal Facilities Indoor Air Quality Assessment Act is a vital legislative effort to assess the federal building portfolio and then move quickly to better protect the health and well-being of America’s public employees,” said Stan Kolbe, Executive Director for Government and Political Affairs, Sheet Metal and Air Conditioning Contractors’ National Association (SMACNA).

“Over the last couple weeks, as hazardous air covered huge parts of the country, Americans have been reminded just how critical it is to make sure our buildings have clean, healthy air indoors,” said the International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation Workers (SMART). “That’s why it’s so important for Congress to get behind the Federal Facilities Indoor Air Quality Assessment Act. This bill would implement a comprehensive review of indoor air quality conditions across all federal buildings, protecting the safety of millions of people and putting SMART members to work ensuring indoor air quality in those buildings. This legislation just makes sense — for SMART sheet metal workers, government employees and Americans nationwide. We thank Rep. Walkinshaw for introducing this act, and we urge every pro-worker member of Congress to add their support.”

“Federal employees deserve workplaces that are safe, healthy, and equipped to support their well-being. Too many federal workers spend their days in buildings with aging infrastructure and ventilation systems that may not provide the indoor air quality they need to do their jobs safely and effectively,” said Everett Kelly, National President, American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE). “We commend Representative Walkinshaw for introducing this important legislation directing the Government Accountability Office to evaluate indoor air quality across federal buildings. This commonsense step will help identify where improvements are needed, strengthen workplace health and safety, and ensure the federal government is making informed investments in the facilities where public servants work every day. AFGE is proud to support this effort to protect the health of the federal workforce.”

“Ensuring that federal buildings provide healthy indoor environments is essential to protecting occupant health and supporting productivity," said Sarah E. Maston, P.E., BCxP, LEED AP BD+C, President,American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE). "A comprehensive review of indoor air quality across the federal building portfolio will provide valuable information about how these facilities perform against nationally recognized indoor air quality standards and where improvements may be needed. This legislation demonstrates a commitment to improving the spaces where millions of federal employees and visitors live, work, and conduct business.”

The legislation directs the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to conduct a comprehensive review of indoor air quality, ventilation, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning system performance across federal buildings and facilities. The review would examine:

Whether federal buildings meet applicable air quality, ventilation, and HVAC standards;

How agencies monitor, test, and document indoor air quality;

The frequency and causes of air quality deficiencies;

Whether agencies effectively identify and correct indoor air hazards; and

The qualifications and certifications of workers performing HVAC installation, maintenance, and remediation.

GAO would report its findings and recommendations to Congress within 12 months. Agencies found to have material indoor air quality deficiencies would then have six months to submit corrective action plans.

The bill is endorsed by the International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation Workers (SMART), the Sheet Metal and Air Conditioning Contractors’ National Association (SMACNA), the American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and the American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE).
title: After Dangerous Air Quality Blankets D.C. Region, Walkinshaw, Beyer, Fitzpatrick, Tonko, & Norton Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve Air in Federal Buildings

(Washington, DC) – Yesterday, Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren (CA-18) of the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology and Ranking Member Marcy Kaptur (OH-09) of the Committee on Appropriations’ Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development sent a letter to Department of Energy (DOE) Secretary Chris Wright demanding answers regarding a political appointee remaining on paid administrative leave nine months after they were removed from their position. The appointee in question, Ms. Cathy Tripodi, served as the Director of DOE’s Office of Clean Energy Demonstration (OCED). She was removed from her position in October 2025.

“The American people expect the leaders who hold political appointment at the Department to do the work for which they are being paid at significant public expense,” the Ranking Members wrote in their letter. “Unfortunately, it appears this foundational expectation and the public trust was violated by recent personnel-related decisions.”

The lawmakers call into question whether Secretary Wright’s handling of Ms. Tripodi’s departure represents a misuse of taxpayer dollars, writing: “It appears that the Department allowed Ms. Tripodi to continue to earn her taxpayer-funded $190,000 per annum salary, potentially with benefits, for close to a full year after her removal from the OCED Director position. If she performed no work for the Department during the time she remained on the payroll, that would constitute a serious misuse of public funds. If she was working or detailed elsewhere while the Department paid her salary, such an arrangement raises serious questions of its own. In either case, the Department owes Congress and the American people a full and timely explanation.”

The letter is available here and below:

Dear Secretary Wright,

We write to exercise appropriate Congressional oversight over, and request information and documents about, a troubling personnel matter that has unfolded under your leadership at the Department of Energy (“the Department”). We send this letter and exercise this oversight based on the long-held understanding and core principle that political appointees privileged to serve at the Department assume public trust, hold public office, and earn taxpayer-funded salaries. The American people expect the leaders who hold political appointment at the Department to do the work for which they are being paid at significant public expense. Unfortunately, it appears this foundational expectation and the public trust was violated by recent personnel-related decisions.

Specifically, we recently learned that Ms. Cathy Tripodi, a political appointee of the Administration who served as Director of the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations (OCED) at the Department, remained on paid administrative leave for nearly nine months after she was removed from her at-will position. It appears that the Department allowed Ms. Tripodi to continue to earn her taxpayer-funded $190,000 per annum salary, potentially with benefits, for close to a full year after her removal from the OCED Director position. If she performed no work for the Department during the time she remained on the payroll, that would constitute a serious misuse of public funds. If she was working or detailed elsewhere while the Department paid her salary, such an arrangement raises serious questions of its own. In either case, the Department owes Congress and the American people a full and timely explanation.

This situation represents the latest in a series of developments since you were sworn in as Secretary in February 2025 that have caused ongoing concern and that collectively call into question the decisions being made at the Department. Among these developments are forced indiscriminate firings and resignations of employees; the cancellation of billions of dollars for projects as political retaliation against “blue” States, which you sought to deny was the basis of such cancellations despite the admission in court by the U.S. Department of Justice that such retaliation was indeed the deciding rationale; the pursuit of ideologically-driven market interventions that distort energy markets and raise energy costs for consumers; and the illegal transfer of appropriated funds in ways that violate Congressional spending laws. The consequences of these troubling developments have fallen on the American people in the form of relentless energy price increases that are compounding our Nation’s current affordability crisis.

Your tenure as Secretary to date is also marked by significant turnover at the Department among political appointees, which includes the departures of Mr. Steven Winberg as Deputy Under Secretary for Infrastructure and Mr. Wells Griffith as Under Secretary for Energy, both of whom departed within months of assuming their respective positions. Most notably for the purposes of this letter, Ms. Tripodi – who previously served at the Department during the President’s first term and who was among the current Administration’s earliest political appointments at the Department – was reportedly removed in October 2025 from her position as OCED Director.

As the respective Ranking Members of the Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies of the Committee on Appropriations and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology in the House of Representatives, we have a duty to conduct oversight of the Department, including over personnel decisions affecting the execution of its mission and the upholding of public trust for the American people. Last October, we had no reason to believe that Ms. Tripodi’s removal represented anything beyond a discretionary Presidential personnel matter. However, it now appears that the Department’s handling of her departure under your leadership and other personnel matters may have implicated and may represent the misuse of taxpayer dollars.

Late last month, we learned that Ms. Tripodi remained on paid administrative leave at the Department long after her reported removal from the OCED Director position. Ms. Tripodi had been relieved of her duties nearly nine months earlier in October 2025, and by all accounts her work at the Department had ended at that time. As a political appointee, she lacked civil service protections. There was no legal or administrative barrier to terminating her employment with the Department on the day she was removed. Even so, she apparently remained on the Department’s payroll for nearly nine months, presumably without performing any work. Her government annual salary of $190,000, according to the most recent publicly available information from the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM), was significant by any standard, and certainly by the standards of most American families. Our understanding upon learning about this situation was that Ms. Tripodi’s paid administrative leave was scheduled to end on or around the end of the month of June 2026. However, it is unclear whether any additional financial benefits or severance pay accompanied the end of her leave.

Since January 2025, the Administration has moved quickly to remove a significant number of highly respected, expert career employees. The Department’s leadership has eagerly participated and embraced these career employee removals. Yet the same urgency through which these Federal workforce reductions have been carried out under the current Administration does not appear to have been applied in the case of Ms. Tripodi. If Ms. Tripodi did not perform any work for the Department during the period she remained on the payroll, that is a troubling double standard – particularly for an Administration that repeatedly invokes “waste, fraud, and abuse” as justification for its broad, unprecedented reductions in force, terminations of career civil servants, and curtailment of programs that serve the public interest. If, on the other hand, Ms. Tripodi was employed or detailed outside the Department – for example, at a National Laboratory or a Department contractor – while continuing to draw her Department of Energy salary, such arrangement raises serious conflict-of-interest and dual-compensation concerns, and it is difficult to understand why the Department would pay a former appointee to work outside its domain. We do not know which of these scenarios may apply in this case, and the Department should tell us.

Keeping a political appointee who has been relieved of her duties on the payroll for nearly nine months is difficult to justify as being in the public interest, whether she performed no work during that time or was paid by the Department while working elsewhere. As skyrocketing energy costs increasingly burden American families, the Department should be able to explain what public purpose this arrangement served. We expect you to account for how it occurred and to identify who was responsible.

We intend to obtain the answers that we seek through this letter. Please respond to the following questions and document production requests no later than two weeks from today, 5:00 PM on Wednesday, August 5, 2026:

1. How long was Ms. Tripodi on paid administrative leave at the Department? Please disclose the initial date that she was placed on paid administrative leave and the final date of her paid administrative leave.

2. How much salary did Ms. Tripodi earn during her time on paid administrative leave? To what government benefits was Ms. Tripodi entitled during her time on administrative leave, what benefits did she receive, and what was the total value of those benefits?

3. Did Ms. Tripodi receive any severance pay, or any other financial benefit, at the end of her paid administrative leave?

4. Which Department official(s) authorized Ms. Tripodi’s placement on paid administrative leave?

5. Why did the Department place Ms. Tripodi on paid administrative leave after she was removed from her position as OCED Director? What was the legal justification for her placement on paid administrative leave and what specific statutory and regulatory basis served to authorize such leave?

6. Have any other political appointees at the Department been placed on paid administrative leave since January 20, 2025? Please identify each political appointee who has been placed on paid administrative leave since that date, the initial date of their administrative leave and the final date of their administrative leave, and the specific reason(s) and legal basis for placing them on administrative leave.

7. During the period she remained on the Department’s payroll following her removal as OCED Director, was Ms. Tripodi detailed or otherwise assigned at any time to any other entity, including but not limited to a Department of Energy National Laboratory, a contractor, another Federal agency, or any other organization? If so, please identify each such entity, the date(s) of the detail or assignment, the nature of the work performed, which DOE official(s) authorized it, and the source(s) of funding for her salary during that time.

8. During the period she remained on the Department’s payroll following her removal, did Ms. Tripodi hold any other employment or receive any other compensation from any source? If so, please identify each source of employment or compensation and the dates involved.

9. Did the Department’s ethics official(s), or ethics official(s) placed anywhere else in the Federal Government, review any detail, assignment, outside employment, or other activity of Ms. Tripodi during this period in question for compliance with applicable conflict-of-interest and ethics requirements? If so, please describe each such review and its outcome. If not, please explain why no such review was conducted.

In addition, please provide the following information to our Committees:

1. All documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, Signal messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) within the Department regarding the decision to place Ms. Tripodi on paid administrative leave.

2. All documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, Signal messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) within the Department regarding the end of Ms. Tripodi’s paid administrative leave.

3. All documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, Signal messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) between the Department and the White House Liaison and Deputy White House Liaison, assigned to the Office of the Secretary inside the Department, regarding Ms. Tripodi’s paid administrative leave.

4. All emails sent from Ms. Tripodi’s official government email account at the Department, and all emails received by Ms. Tripodi’s official government email account at the Department, between October 1, 2025, and the final date of her paid administrative leave.

5. All text messages, instant messages, and Signal messages sent from Ms. Tripodi’s official government-issued equipment, and all text messages, instant messages, and Signal messages received by Ms. Tripodi’s official government-issued equipment, between October 1, 2025, and the final date of her paid administrative leave.

6. A copy of the written administrative leave policies, and any associated guidance or memoranda, adopted for the Department that applied during the period Ms. Tripodi was placed on paid administrative leave, and the current version of such policies and related documentation as of the date of this letter, if different.

If you have any questions regarding this letter, please contact Scott McKee with the Minority Staff of the House Committee on Appropriations at (202) 225-3481 or Adam Rosenberg with the Minority Staff of the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology at (202) 225-6375. Thank you for your attention to this important matter.
title: Lofgren, Kaptur Demand Answers from DOE After Political Appointee Remained on Payroll Nearly Nine Months after Agency Removal

Washington, D.C. – House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-CA) and Congressman Don Beyer (D-VA) led 70 House Democrats in demanding that the National Park Service (NPS) immediately address its reported backlog of 1,400 grant approvals, which has delayed more than $360 million in funding for critical projects that keep national parks safe and accessible to the American public.

In a letter addressed to NPS Acting Director Jessica Bowron, the lawmakers warned that the grant approval bottleneck is delaying routine but essential work, including trail maintenance, wildfire mitigation, and other projects during peak visitation and wildfire risk season.

The Members pointed to a new grant process that requires two political appointees to manually review every grant and agreement over $50,000. Members stressed this review process has resulted in more than $360 million in delayed NPS funding. The Members also noted this process bears similarities to review processes that were rolled back at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) after findings they violated federal court orders.

“These delays are unacceptable. Nonprofit programs to clear trails have been delayed at the critical start of peak visitation season, while prescribed burns and other wildfire control programs are at risk of the same fate during peak wildfire risk season,” wrote the Members. “Choosing to make such grants contingent on review by unqualified political appointees puts the safety of the American people at risk, whether they choose to visit our national parks or simply live near them.”

The letter is signed by Representatives Becca Balint (D-VT), Nanette Barragán (D-CA), Wesley Bell (D-MO), Julia Brownley (D-CA), Salud Carbajal (D-CA), Andre Carson (D-IN), Ed Case (D-HI), Joaquin Castro (D-TX), Judy Chu (D-CA), Steve Cohen (D-TN), Herb Conaway (D-NJ), Jim Costa (D-CA), Angie Craig (D-MN), Jasmine Crockett (D-TX), Madeleine Dean (D-PA), Diana DeGette (D-CO), Mark DeSaulnier (D-CA), Sarah Elfreth (D-MD), Laura Friedman (D-CA), John Garamendi (D-CA), Robert Garcia (D-CA), Jesus “Chuy” Garcia (D-IL), Sylvia Garcia (D-TX), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ), Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ), Pablo Hernández (D-PR), Steven Horsford (D-NV), Sara Jacobs (D-CA), Hank Johnson (D-GA), Julie Johnson (D-TX), Robin Kelly (D-IL), Ro Khanna (D-CA), Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), Ted Lieu (D-CA), Zoe Lofgren (D-CA), Stephen Lynch (D-MA), Seth Magaziner (D-RI), April McClain Delaney (D-MD), Jennifer McClellan (D-VA), Betty McCollum (D-MN), Dave Min (D-CA), Kelly Morrison (D-MN), Jared Moskowitz (D-FL), Seth Moulton (D-MA), Joe Neguse (D-CO), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC), Frank Pallone (D-NJ), Nancy Pelosi (D-CA), Scott Peters (D-CA), Mike Quigley (D-IL), Raul Ruiz (D-CA), Mary Gay Scanlon (D-PA), Jan Schakowsky (D-IL), Kim Schrier (D-WA), Bobby Scott (D-VA), Lateefah Simon (D-CA), Melanie Stansbury (D-NM), Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA), Mark Takano (D-CA), Mike Thompson (D-CA), Dina Titus (D-NV), Rashida Tlaib (D-MI), Jill Tokuda (D-HI), Paul Tonko (D-NY), Juan Vargas (D-CA), Gabe Vasquez (D-NM), Nydia Velázquez (D-NY), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL), Bonnie Watson Coleman (D-NJ), George Whitesides (D-CA).

Full text of the letter follows below, and a signed copy is available here.

***

Dear Acting Director Bowron:

We write to request that National Park Service (NPS) immediately adjust its grant review process to address a reported 1,400 active grant approval backlog. According to public reports, NPS currently requires all grants and cooperative agreements valued at $50,000 or above to be manually reviewed by two political appointees. Those appointees serve at the department level and are not solely tasked with ensuring timely review of NPS grants and agreements, creating a severe bottleneck that has left more than $360 million in NPS funding behind schedule.

These delays are unacceptable. Nonprofit programs to clear trails have been delayed at the critical start of peak visitation season, while prescribed burns and other wildfire control programs are at risk of the same fate during peak wildfire risk season. Ensuring that those and similarly routine programs are funded during critical times of the year should be part of the regular operation of the National Park System. Choosing to make such grants contingent on review by unqualified political appointees puts the safety of the American people at risk, whether they choose to visit our national parks or simply live near them.

During the first Trump administration, the Government Accountability Office investigated DOI’s grants review process that was also run through an unqualified political appointee. They found that the appointee, an old football friend of then-Secretary of the Interior, Ryan Zinke, centralized grants review for all bureaus at DOI. He “closely scrutinized applications focused on certain topics, such as endangered species and climate change, rather than considering the merit of individual grant applications or program policy factors, such as leveraging resources between similar programs.” When he rejected grants, he kept his decisions off the books, hiding the truth from the American people and suggesting willful malfeasance.

The NPS decision bears striking similarities to other manual review processes that have been rolled back at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). Last year, DHS instituted a manual grant review process that – similar to the reported NPS process – required additional review above a value threshold. That process delayed more than 1,000 FEMA contracts, grants, and disaster assistance awards. The delays came amid historic flooding in Texas and in the heart of the Atlantic hurricane season. After repeated findings that the process violated federal court orders, the DHS approval system was rolled back earlier this year.

We urge you to do the same at NPS, while also providing a full accounting of the current NPS grant and cooperative agreement backlog. It is a core responsibility of NPS to ensure that routine, lifesaving programs are funded on time and in full, while offering full transparency on the status of any delayed approvals. We request an update on NPS’ plans for its grant review process, as well as a full list of all grants and cooperative agreements in the approval backlog, no later than July 28, 2026.

###
title: 70+ House Democrats Demand NPS Address Multimillion-Dollar Grant Backlog Delaying Trail Maintenance, Wildfire Prevention, and Critical Projects

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, U.S. Representative and Ranking Member of the House Agriculture Committee Angie Craig (D-MN-02) introduced legislation alongside Rep. Andy Barr (R-KY-06) to create a comprehensive regulatory framework for hemp and hemp-derived THC products, ensuring hemp remains safe and available for Minnesota’s farmers, processors, brewers, retailers and consumers.

Rep. Craig’s Lawful Hemp Protection Act comes after House Republicans effectively repealed a 2018 law that allowed Minnesota and other states to legally produce hemp and sell hemp-derived products, such as hemp beverages and textiles. Since 2018, the hemp industry has grown into a roughly $300 million a year industry and provided a new income stream for local farmers, brewers and small businesses. As of 2023, the Minnesota hemp industry supported over 3,400 jobs. The state is home to 132 licensed grow operations, 96 processors and over 2,000 retailers. If Congress does not act by November 12, 2026, Minnesota’s legal hemp industry will effectively be shut down.

“Minnesota became the model for responsible hemp regulation when it established a regulatory framework that complied with federal law and enabled local farmers and businesses to thrive,” said Rep. Craig. “My commonsense legislation will give regulatory clarity to Minnesota farmers, brewers and small business owners and provide an alternative to short-sighted federal policies that threaten Minnesota jobs and consumer choice. I am proud to have worked with Rep. Barr on a solution that protects our farmers and small businesses while also keeping our kids and communities safe.”

“Kentucky farmers helped build America’s hemp industry and they deserve certainty,” said Rep. Andy Barr. “The Lawful Hemp Protection Act protects Kentucky agriculture, safeguards consumers, and establishes a commonsense regulatory framework that allows this important industry to continue to grow while ensuring products are safe and kept out of the hands of children. Kentucky has demonstrated that hemp can be successfully regulated while supporting farmers and protecting consumers. This legislation builds on that success by creating a national framework that rewards responsible producers, eliminates bad actors and ensures consumers have confidence in the products they purchase.”

“We are dangerously close to one of Minnesota’s most promising small business industries being shut down,” said Bob Galligan, director of government and industry relations for the Minnesota Craft Brewers Guild. “Minnesotans proved that responsible regulation can lift businesses, strengthen economies and protect consumers. We now need Congress to do its job. We’re grateful for Rep. Craig for her continuous support and for now forging a path that reflects what our state has already shown: prohibition doesn’t work, but thoughtful, practical regulation does.”

“The entire Minnesota hemp industry thanks both Reps. Angie Craig and Andy Barr for their leadership in bringing sensible regulation to this industry that is so important to so many,” said Kyle Markinovich, the founder and CEO of Northern Diversified Solutions in Burnsville, MN. “The farmers, brands, distributors, retailers, patients, and consumers are so grateful this amazing success story will continue to grow and thrive. As Minnesotans, we are particularly grateful to Rep. Craig who continues to serve hemp farmers and businesses so well in the Congress.”

“Reps. Andy Barr and Angie Craig deserve tremendous credit for stepping forward with a serious, science-based and bipartisan solution at exactly the moment the hemp industry needs it most,” said Jonathan Miller, general counsel of the U.S. Hemp Roundtable. “Their leadership on the Lawful Hemp Protection Act reflects a clear-eyed recognition that prohibition is the wrong path, and that American farmers, small businesses, manufacturers, retailers and consumers deserve a workable federal framework built on responsible regulation. We are grateful for their willingness to engage stakeholders across the industry throughout the drafting process, and we look forward to continuing to work with them and their colleagues in Congress to advance a long-term federal solution.”

###
title: Rep. Angie Craig Introduces Comprehensive Regulatory Framework for Hemp

Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) introduced the Military Spouse Employment and Child Care Readiness Act, legislation that would direct the Department of Defense to identify ways to strengthen the military child care workforce while creating meaningful employment opportunities for military spouses.

“Supporting our servicemembers means supporting their families,” said Congresswoman Escobar. “Military spouses often sacrifice their own careers, stability, and opportunities every time they answer the call and have to start over in a new community. The Military Spouse Employment and Child Care Readiness Act provides a crucial first step toward removing unnecessary barriers to employment for military spouses, strengthening military child care, and ensuring military families have the support they need to thrive."

Military families frequently relocate wherever the mission requires, often requiring spouses to rebuild their careers and navigate new licensing, certifications, or other requirements. At the same time, staffing shortages at military child development centers can limit the number of children who receive care. Together, these challenges prevent military spouses from entering the workforce, strain family finances, and make it more difficult for active-duty servicemembers to balance the demands of their service with the basic needs of their families.

By examining barriers and opportunities, the Military Spouse Employment and Child Care Readiness Act would pave the way for Department of Defense-supported career pathways that can follow military spouses between installations and expand the network of qualified child care providers serving military communities. It endorsed by the Military Family Advisory Network.

Specifically, the legislation would direct the Department of Defense to:

Determine the percentage of military child development center employees who are military spouses or spouses of retired or separated servicemembers

Assess the feasibility of making child care licenses and certifications more portable for military spouses

Examine vacancy rates at military child development centers and identify the primary causes of staffing shortages

Determine how many additional children could receive care if military child development centers were fully staffed

Assess whether military spouses living in on-post housing could provide home-based child care

Recommend incentives to attract and retain military spouses in the military child care workforce.

To view the full bill text, click here.

WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Shomari C. Figures (AL-02) introduced the Tuskegee Airmen Memorial Act, a bill to create a memorial in Washington, DC, to commemorate the service, sacrifice, and enduring legacy of the Tuskegee Airmen.

“The Tuskegee Airmen are among the most heroic and consequential soldiers that our nation has ever had,” said Congressman Figures. “While facing horrific discrimination at home, these men risked their lives to defend rights and freedoms abroad. Their courage, skill, and unwavering dedication not only contributed to the Allied victory but also helped pave the way for the desegregation of the U.S. military. Their contributions to our country deserve to be memorialized in our nation’s capital, and I'm proud to introduce this bipartisan bill to make that a reality.”

"The introduction of this authorizing legislation in Congress is a vital milestone in our ongoing mission to preserve and honor the legacy of our nation’s pioneering heroes,” said Ms. Angela Holmes, 1st Vice President for Tuskegee Airmen, Inc. "We extend our deepest gratitude to Representative Shomari Figures and our congressional partners for championing this effort. As we see the final generation of our original members passing, establishing a permanent landmark in Washington, D.C., ensures that their monumental contributions to military integration, excellence, and civil rights will never be forgotten by future generations.”

Congressman Figures’ bill would authorize Tuskegee Airmen, Incorporated to establish a memorial on federal land in the District of Columbia. This is a key, necessary first step towards making this well-deserved memorial a reality. Tuskegee Airmen, Incorporated is a national nonprofit founded to preserve the history and achievements of the original Tuskegee Airmen and engage with youth to inspire future careers in aviation, aerospace and STEM.

The memorial will serve as an educational resource, designed to teach future generations about one of the greatest, most well-decorated fighting forces in our nation’s history, and to highlight the important roles that Black military pilots and support personnel played in World War II.

This bill is cosponsored by the entire Alabama House Congressional Delegation, Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Sanford Bishop (GA-02), and Emilia Sykes (OH-13).
title: Figures Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Establish Tuskegee Airmen Memorial in Washington, DC

WASHINGTON DC - El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, anunció hoy la aprobación en la Cámara de Representantes de la Ley de Autorización de Defensa Nacional para el año fiscal 2027, que incluye varias disposiciones relacionadas con instalaciones militares y personal de las Fuerzas Armadas en Puerto Rico. El proyecto busca permitir que la instalación pueda tratar y mantener un suministro de agua durante interrupciones del servicio, desastres naturales u otras emergencias, fortaleciendo la continuidad de sus operaciones.

También la medida extiende la autorización de un proyecto previamente aprobado de microred eléctrica y generación de energía de respaldo en Fort Buchanan. Esta extensión evita que la autorización expire mientras se completan los procesos necesarios para desarrollar la obra. La medida también incluye disposiciones nacionales que aplican a Puerto Rico, entre ellas protecciones relacionadas con planes suplementarios de salud para militares y esfuerzos para facilitar que médicos de combate y otro personal de salud militar puedan utilizar su experiencia y credenciales al ingresar a la fuerza laboral civil.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) voted against H.R. 7008, the Stop Insider Trading Act that was combined with H.R. 9368, the Voter ID Act.

Rep. Sykes has consistently supported strong congressional ethics reforms, including signing a discharge petition to force a vote on the Restore Trust in Government Act, establishing a comprehensive stock trading ban for top federal officials. She opposed the Stop Insider Trading Act because it leaves significant conflicts of interest unaddressed, and she opposed House Republicans' decision to tie the bill to voting restrictions instead of allowing each proposal to stand on its own.

Rep. Sykes believes Congress should pass meaningful ethics reforms that restore public trust while considering voting legislation on its own merits, not forcing Members to choose between the two.

“The American people are tired of Washington playing games with issues that matter. If we're going to restore trust in government, then let's pass a real stock trading ban, not one riddled with loopholes,” said Rep. Sykes. “And don't ask me to sacrifice Americans' right to vote just to pretend we've solved a different problem. My constituents deserve better than political stunts.”

While the Stop Insider Trading Act creates new restrictions on stock transactions by Members of Congress, it falls short of a comprehensive stock trading ban and leaves significant loopholes that allow conflicts of interest to continue. Among other shortcomings, the legislation:

Exempts the President and Vice President from its restrictions.

Does not require covered officials to divest all covered investments.

Does not ban trading of commodities or futures.

Does not ban trading of stock in privately held companies.

Allows Members of Congress to keep stocks they already own and continue selling those holdings.

Does not require the House Ethics Committee to publicly disclose fines imposed on Members for violations.

The Voter ID Act creates new federal photo identification requirements for voting, including not allowing state or local election officials to provide a ballot to a voter who does not present a valid physical photo ID. That voter may not vote, in-person or otherwise, without the correct documentation. The ban would not apply to military voters serving overseas and certain disabled or elderly voters.

The bill passed the House and now moves to the Senate for consideration.
title: Rep. Sykes Opposes Restrictive Voting Legislation That Allows Congressional Stock Trading

WASHINGTON, DC — Today, following President Trump’s announcement of a new 50% tariff on Canadian imports, U.S. Representative Kelly Morrison (MN-03), a member of the House Small Business Committee, questioned Small Business Administration Associate Administrator Paul Fitzpatrick about how the tariffs will affect American small businesses.
Canada is one of the United States’ closest allies and Minnesota’s largest trading partner. Minnesota imports more than $14 billion in goods from Canada and exports more than $5 billion in goods to Canada each year. The new tariffs threaten imports on which many Minnesota small businesses depend and increase the possibility that Canada will impose retaliatory tariffs.
The Small Business Administration has proposed eliminating 15 of its 16 federal entrepreneurial-development programs, including a program that helps small businesses enter and expand in international markets. Combined with the new tariffs, these proposed cuts pose a serious threat to Minnesota small businesses that depend on trade with Canada and have already experienced the effects of tariffs during the past year.
Representative Morrison asked Associate Administrator Fitzpatrick how small businesses would be expected to navigate trade with Canada under these conditions. Fitzpatrick did not provide a clear plan for protecting affected businesses.
As a member of the House Small Business Committee, Representative Morrison has advocated for small businesses throughout her first term in Congress. Her work has included:
- Meeting with Minnesota small-business owners to learn how tariffs are affecting them;
- Seeking immediate tariff exemptions for small businesses;
- Pressing Small Business Administrator Kelly Loeffler to exempt small businesses from tariffs;
- Demanding that the Trump Administration rescind tariffs on Canada;
- Urging Speaker Mike Johnson to bring the House back for a vote to end the President’s tariff war;
- Introducing and passing the Rural Small Business Resilience Act, which helps rural small businesses recover from natural disasters; and
- Working to strengthen research and development opportunities for small businesses.
Transcript of Representative Morrison’s Remarks
REP. MORRISON: Thank you, Chairman Williams and Ranking Member Velázquez, for holding this hearing. Thank you, Associate Administrator Fitzpatrick, for being here today.
The leading concern I hear from small-business owners in my district is the difficulty of operating amid the uncertainty created by the President’s tariffs.
Many businesses are experiencing reduced profit margins, disrupted supply chains, and an inability to plan reliably because of these tariffs, putting the futures of their businesses at risk.
The President’s fiscal year 2027 budget proposes eliminating 15 of the 16 entrepreneurial-development programs, including the State Trade Expansion Program, or STEP. This program helps small businesses enter or expand in international markets.
One consequence of the President’s tariffs has been retaliatory tariffs imposed on the United States by other countries. These measures create even more uncertainty for small businesses interested in participating in international trade.
During the past year, as the President imposed tariffs on Canadian automobiles, aluminum, steel, and lumber, Canada responded with retaliatory tariffs against the United States. Those measures restricted exports to our northern neighbor for Minnesota small businesses.
Now, we must wait to see how Canada responds to the President’s new 50% tariff on Canadian goods.
Given the administration’s stated interest in increasing U.S. exports and balancing trade deficits, I question the decision to eliminate STEP at a time when small businesses need more assistance navigating trade uncertainty—not less.
How is the Office of Entrepreneurial Development helping small businesses in international markets navigate retaliatory tariffs?
ASSOCIATE ADMINISTRATOR FITZPATRICK: Congresswoman, thank you for the question. We support the administration’s policies promoting fair trade, which we believe support small businesses. As we travel around the country, we have encountered businesses adding shifts and receiving contracts they did not previously have. I recently met with a business in Wisconsin that—
REP. MORRISON: I’m sorry to interrupt, but how does your office plan to continue helping small businesses increase their exports? How will you help small businesses expand their exports amid retaliatory tariffs if the STEP program is eliminated?
ASSOCIATE ADMINISTRATOR FITZPATRICK: Congresswoman, thank you for the question. We have limited resources, and we will follow the law. We will distribute funding as Congress appropriates it. If Congress directs funding to STEP, we will administer that program.
###
title: U.S. Rep. Kelly Morrison Grills SBA on How Trump’s New 50% Tariffs on Canada Will Affect Small Businesses

WASHINGTON – Today, ahead of Senate floor action to extend Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haiti, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Co-Chair of the House Haiti Caucus, alongside Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04), urged Senators to support legislation to extend Haiti TPS and protect the lives and livelihoods of Haitians and Americans alike. Senators Ed Markey and Lisa Blunt Rochester lead the companion bill, introduced after the successful House passage of Congresswoman Pressley’s discharge petition to preserve and extend TPS for Haitians.

In their letter to Senators, the Congresswomen made clear the harm of terminating TPS both for the safety and well-being of Haitian families and for the health of the American economy, workforce, and communities that are beneficiaries of Haitians’ essential contributions.

“Protecting the safety, dignity, and humanity of our Haitian neighbors is the right thing to do, and our country is strengthened by their contributions to our communities, the economy, our healthcare workforce, and more,” said Rep. Pressley. “Since my discharge petition to extend TPS for Haitians successfully passed the House, we’ve been pressing hard to advance this essential legislation and protect our Haitian neighbors. The Senate must pass the extension of Haiti TPS without delay.”

“The Senate must respond to the Supreme Court’s harmful decision to terminate TPS for hardworking, taxpaying, law-abiding Haitian members of our community and pass our bipartisan bill immediately,” said Rep. Gillen. “Haitian TPS recipients have been thoroughly vetted, passed rigorous background checks and are essential to our nation’s workforce. Forcing them to face the violence and chaos in Haiti would be tantamount to a death sentence and bad for our economy. I’m proud to join my colleagues to urge every senator to support our legislation preserving the legal status of our Haitian friends and neighbors.”

The legislation preserves TPS protections for more than 300,000 Haitian nationals, offering a critical lifeline as Haiti continues to confront political instability, widespread violence, and a serious humanitarian emergency.

Bill text can be accessed here.

Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11) and Congresswoman Laurel Lee (FL-15) introduced the Swatting Registry Best Practices Act, bipartisan legislation to help State, Tribal, territorial, and local governments reduce the risk of deadly swatting incidents through voluntary, privacy-protective tools and stronger emergency response protocols.

Swatting is a serious public safety threat. Former FBI Special Agent Kevin Kolbye estimated that swatting incidents increased from approximately 400 cases in 2011 to more than 1,000 in 2019. However, inconsistent reporting and classification across law enforcement agencies make it difficult to determine the full scope of the problem.

Swatting is the deliberate act of making a false report of a violent emergency—such as an active shooter, hostage situation, bomb threat, or murder—to trigger an armed law enforcement response to an unsuspecting person’s home or workplace. These hoaxes put innocent families and first responders at risk, divert emergency resources from real crises, and can quickly turn deadly. According to NBC News, law enforcement agencies have estimated that a swatting incident can cost several thousand dollars and potentially $10,000 or more, even before follow-up expenses such as investigations, property repairs, and counseling.

"Swatting weaponizes our emergency response system against innocent people," said Congressman Walkinshaw. "A single false call can send heavily armed officers to a family's front door, putting lives at risk in a matter of minutes. My bill gives communities practical tools to help prevent these dangerous hoaxes while protecting privacy and civil liberties."

“Swatting is a dangerous crime that puts innocent families, law enforcement officers, and entire communities at unnecessary risk,” said Congresswoman Lee. “When emergency responders are dispatched to a fabricated crisis, critical resources are diverted from people facing real emergencies, and a split-second decision can have tragic consequences. The Swatting Registry Best Practices Act provides law enforcement with voluntary, commonsense guidance to help identify potential swatting incidents while protecting privacy and civil liberties. I am proud to join Congressman Walkinshaw in advancing this bipartisan legislation to better protect both the public and the first responders who put their lives on the line every day.”

The Swatting Registry Best Practices Act directs the Department of Justice, in consultation with the Department of Homeland Security, to develop national best practices for jurisdictions that choose to establish voluntary swatting registries or integrate swatting verification into existing 911 and dispatch operations. The bill also authorizes technical assistance for agencies seeking to implement these practices.

Read the full bill text here.

title: Walkinshaw, Lee Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect Families & First Responders from Swatting Attacks

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congress Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee, issued the following statement after the House passed the FY27 National Defense Authorization Act. After Republican leaders allowed partisan poison pill amendments to be added to the NDAA, Courtney voted “no” on initial House-passage of the FY27 NDAA. To watch Courtney’s floor speech urging against partisan poison amendments, click here. In June, following months of bipartisan work with his colleagues on the Armed Services Committee and the Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee, Courtney voted to pass the bipartisan committee-passed (44-12) version of the FY27 NDAA. To read his statement on committee passage, click here.

“It is deeply unfortunate that, for the fourth year in a row, House Republican leadership has taken the bipartisan NDAA passed by the House Armed Services Committee and allowed extreme Members of their caucus to add partisan poison pills. Chief among these poison pills are the merger of the voter suppression bill, the SAVE Act, which has nothing to do with national defense, and an amendment to the bill which would cut health care services for military families. This amendment would degrade the coverage provided to families who sacrifice so much for our nation to a lower level than the coverage available to civilians in the private health insurance market. During last night’s House of Representatives debate on the annual national defense policy bill, also known as the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24) spoke out against the Hunt amendment, which would grant the federal government unprecedented access to California-owned public lands associated with the Santa Ynez Unit and Las Flores Pipeline System.

Download a video clip of Carbajal’s full debate here.

Background on the Hunt amendment

Specifically, the Hunt amendment would authorize the Secretary of Defense to use federal eminent domain to acquire permanent easements across California-owned lands and submerged lands under the Santa Ynez Pipeline system, the pipeline that caused the 2015 Refugio oil spill off the coast of California.

This amendment broadly preempts California law by eliminating state permitting requirements and blocking state injunctions. It also requires the Secretary to grant the operator an irrevocable license that cannot be revoked by California courts, state agencies, or future administrations, except under extremely limited circumstances

A rough transcript of Carbajal’ opening remarks is available below:

Thank you, Mr. Chair. Thank you, Mr. Garamendi.

I oppose this amendment.

We know that the military does not need this provision to ensure a stable supply.

We already are the largest oil producer in the world, producing nearly 14 million barrels of oil a day.

So let’s be clear: this is not about energy independence or national security.

It is about giving Big Oil special treatment at the expense of California.

Under this amendment, a single certification from the Secretary of Defense unlocks sweeping legal protections for fossil fuel projects.

States and local governments cannot interfere.

Courts are told to presume that delaying this project harms national security on the Secretary's word alone. And we know what that means.

Challengers cannot dispute the Secretary's determination.

And developers receive procedural advantages that no other litigant enjoys – including the ability to essentially choose which federal court will hear a challenge.

It is interesting to me that this amendment is sponsored by Congressman Hunt, from Houston, where Sable Offshore Oil’s headquarters is located.

Sable Offshore, of course, is the operator of the Santa Ynez Pipeline System, which the Trump administration forced back online over the objections of California.

This is the pipeline that caused the devastating Refugio oil spill in 2015 in my district.

My constituents, who must live with the risk this operation poses, are overwhelmingly opposed.

But the Trump administration used the Defense Production Act to preempt state law.

The state of California is challenging that authority in court.

I guess Sable is worried about losing in court—as they should be—because this amendment would allow the company to avoid accountability by moving to a more favorable court, blocking the California lawsuit, and preventing any court from issuing an injunction against this project.

So let me be clear again: this isn’t about national security.

It is a bailout for polluters.

I oppose this amendment and I urge my colleagues to also vote no.

Republicans’ attempt to increase military funding by more than $250 billion compared to the previous fiscal year also comes amidst a war of choice in Iran that seemingly has no clear goal or exit strategy. As the American people pay the price at the gas pump and beyond and our servicemembers are asked to make the ultimate sacrifice, a vote to funnel more money into a war that has cost at least 17 U.S. servicemembers’ lives and billions of dollars would only rubberstamp the President’s agenda to keep us in a forever war with no end in sight.

They pushed for Section 219 to expand and merge American and Israeli defense capabilities, a provision that undermines our sovereignty and lacks any form of oversight. WASHINGTON, DC — Today, U.S. Representative Sarah McBride and U.S. Senators Chris Coons and Lisa Blunt Rochester (all D-Del.) celebrated a $940,000 U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Rural Development grant for Milford Housing Development Corporation. The funding, awarded through the USDA Rural Development’s 523 Mutual Self-Help Housing Technical Assistance Grant program, will support the construction of two dozen new, energy-efficient homes for low-income families in rural communities throughout Sussex and Kent Counties. Over a two-year period, the grant will help Milford Housing Development Corporation continue its self-help housing program and expand access to affordable homeownership in rural Delaware.

“Every Delaware family deserves access to a safe, stable, and affordable place to call home,” said U.S. Representative Sarah McBride. “This grant will help Milford Housing Development Corporation build 24 energy-efficient homes, continuing their work to make homeownership more attainable for working families in Kent and Sussex counties. I am proud to join Senators Coons and Blunt Rochester in celebrating this investment to expand affordable housing opportunities in rural Delaware, and I look forward to continuing to work together to bring down housing costs across our state.”

“Affordable housing is about more than building homes, it’s about creating opportunity. Thanks to this $940,000 investment, the Milford Housing Development Corporation will help more Delaware families realize the dream of homeownership in our rural communities,” said U.S. Senator Chris Coons. “I’m grateful for USDA’s continued partnership in creating safe, decent, affordable housing that strengthens neighborhoods, lowers energy costs, and builds a brighter future for the next generation.”

“Good homes are the foundation of strong communities — because without a roof over your head, the promise of good-paying jobs and high-quality education are out of reach,” said U.S. Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester. “That is why I’m so excited for communities in Kent and Sussex Counties, who will be receiving two dozen new energy-efficient homes through this grant. Alongside Senator Coons and Representative McBride, I am committed to making housing more attainable and expanding opportunity for all Delawareans.”

“We are incredibly grateful to continue our long-standing partnership with USDA Rural Development in expanding access to affordable homeownership opportunities” said David Moore President/CEO Milford Housing Development Corporation. “Through the Self-Help Housing Program, individuals and families who might otherwise be unable to achieve homeownership invest their own "sweat equity" by working together to build not only their own homes, but also those of their neighbors. This unique approach fosters a strong sense of community while making homeownership attainable and affordable. Along the way, participants gain valuable construction experience, financial education, and the confidence needed to become successful, informed homeowners, creating lasting benefits for themselves, their families, and their communities”.

This $940,000 investment represents an ongoing effort by Coons, Blunt Rochester, and McBride to secure more federal investment to address the cost-of-living crisis and to expand access to affordable housing opportunities, especially in rural and low-income areas across Delaware. Recently, the congressional delegation voted to pass the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act in their respective chambers – the first comprehensive housing affordability bill to pass Congress in three decades. The congressional delegation will continue working to secure resources that increase housing supply, strengthen rural communities, and help more families achieve the stability of homeownership.

Bill Addresses Technicality That Denies Grieving Families of Benefits Their Loved Ones Earned

WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representatives Lou Correa (D-CA) and Jefferson Van Drew (R-NJ) introduced the bipartisan Public Safety Officers’ Benefits Enhancement Act, which would improve the Public Safety Officers’ Benefits (PSOB) Program by making it easier for families of public safety officers who suffer from fatal heart attacks or strokes in the line of duty to receive benefits from the program.

"Firefighters and officers put their bodies on the line every single shift, and sometimes that toll shows up hours or days later, not the same afternoon. A 24-hour cutoff doesn't match how a heart attack or stroke actually works. This bill just brings the rule in line with reality, so families aren't punished for paperwork technicalities while they're grieving," said Congressman Lou Correa.

The need for the legislation was brought forth by the family of Stephen Wilson, a California Fire Apparatus Engineer. When Mr. Wilson died, his wife, Annette Wilson, filed for death benefits through the PSOB Program with all the required paperwork. The claim was denied anyway. The government stated the record didn't show his death was "a direct and proximate result of a line of duty injury" under the PSOB Act's rules because he did not see a doctor within 24 hours of leaving work.

"My husband spent his career running toward danger to keep our community safe. He died because of that work, and yet his own claim was denied because of a technicality," said Annette Wilson, wife of Stephen Wilson. "No family should have to fight this hard for benefits their loved one earned. This bill means people do not have to go through what I did."

“When our first responders answer the call, they are willing to put everything on the line for complete strangers,” said Congressman Van Drew. “If the stress of that job costs them their life, their loved ones should not have to battle the government for the support they deserve. This is a common-sense fix, and I am proud to work with Congressman Correa to get it done.”

"The Public Safety Officers' Benefits Enhancement Act represents a critical step toward ensuring that the families of fallen firefighters and other first responders receive the support they deserve. Too often, survivors face unnecessary barriers when seeking benefits after a line-of-duty heart attack or stroke. By extending the eligibility window and creating a fairer presumption that recognizes the realities of emergency service, this legislation strengthens the Public Safety Officers' Benefits Program and honors the sacrifices made by our nation's first responders. The National Fallen Firefighters Foundation is proud to support this important legislation," said Victor Stagnaro, Chief Executive Officer of the National Fallen Firefighters Foundation.

"Our nation's public safety officers deserve the assurance that if they make the ultimate sacrifice, their families will be treated fairly and receive the benefits they deserve," said Mathew Silverman, Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association (FLEOA) National President. "The Public Safety Officers' Benefits Enhancement Act is a commonsense, bipartisan measure that better reflects the realities of line-of-duty service and removes unnecessary barriers for surviving families to receive much needed benefits and FLEOA strongly supports its passage."

“Unless there is evidence to the contrary, it should be presumed that a police officer’s line-of-duty fatal heart attack or stroke was job related. Requiring police families to offer definitive proof, especially when it’s known that cardiovascular disease and strokes are leading causes of illness and mortality, places undue hardship on grieving survivors. It also dishonors the memories of our heroes who sacrifice greatly to protect and serve. The National Police Association is grateful to Reps. J. Luis Correa and Jefferson Van Drew for introducing the Public Safety Officers’ Benefits Enhancement Act, a bill that will help ensure law enforcement families are spared from having to navigate these unnecessary bureaucratic hurdles,” said Paula Fitzsimmons, Legislative Director, National Police Association

"When a peace officer makes the ultimate sacrifice, their family shouldn't have to fight a second battle just to receive the support they were promised. This legislation honors that sacrifice by removing unnecessary obstacles from the claims process, ensuring survivors can access the benefits they deserve when they need them most.” said Brian R. Marvel, President, Peace Officers Research Association of California.

This bill is cosponsored by U.S. Representatives Mike Thompson (D-CA), Stephen Lynch (D-MA), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL), Don Bacon (R-NE), Mark Alford (R-MO), Thomas Kean (R-NJ), Adam Gray (D-CA), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ), Jared Golden (D-ME), and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D-WA).

This bill is endorsed by the Blue Dog Coalition, National Association of Police Organizations, Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association, National Police Association, National Fallen Firefighters Foundation, International Association of Fire Fighters, Major County Sheriffs of America, Peace Officers Research Association of California, and National Narcotic Officers' Associations' Coalition.

View bill text here.

Background

The PSOB Program provides death and education benefits to survivors of fallen law enforcement officers, firefighters, and other first responders, and disability benefits to officers catastrophically injured in the line of duty.

The program provides benefits to survivors when first responders suffer from fatal heart attacks or strokes in the line of duty, but current law requires that the heart attack or stroke begin within 24 hours of nonroutine physical activity and requires the survivors to prove that the line of duty action directly resulted in the heart attack or stroke—which leads to claims being excluded where additional risk factors may have been at play.

This bill modifies the PSOB program by:

Extending the time period for heart attacks and strokes to be covered from 24 to 72 hours.

Changing the presumption so that qualifying events are covered unless medical evidence says it was unrelated to service—instead of placing the burden of proof on the survivors to show it was directly caused by the activity.
title: CORREA, VAN DREW INTRODUCE BILL TO PROTECT BENEFITS FOR FAMILIES OF PUBLIC SAFETY OFFICERS

New legislation would ensure voters have access to a polling location in their area for federal elections.

Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) introduced the Polling Place Standards Act that would provide a minimum number of polling places for voters to cast a ballot in an election for Federal office and to ensure that such polling places are not concentrated in a specific area, and for other purposes.

Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) said:

“Voting is a constitutional right, and no one should have to wait for hours or travel miles just to cast a ballot. Yet for decades, polling place closures have been used to make voting harder and silence communities.

As Trump and his allies continue trying to undermine our democracy ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, Congress must ensure every eligible voter has a fair opportunity to cast a ballot and have their voice heard. That’s why I’m introducing the Polling Place Standards Act to establish a national standard to polling place access ensuring where you live never determines whether you can exercise your constitutional right to vote.”

The bill is endorsed by Democracy Defenders Action.

What the Bill Does

The Protecting American Homes from Hedge Funds Act would require states and local governments to provide 1 polling place or vote center (a polling place that accepts a ballot cast for a Federal Election from any voter regardless of the precinct of such voter), for every 2000 registered voters.

This formula allows for a clear standard across the country, in rural and urban areas alike. And these new polling places would be required to be located in geographically diverse areas and not be concentrated in a certain part of a locality.

Click here to read the text of the Polling Place Standards Act.
title: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Introduces Bill to Make the Ballot Box More Accessible

Congresswoman Dina Titus led eleven other members of Congress representing Upper Basin and Lower Basin states in sending a bipartisan letter to House leadership today urging them to include measures in a supplemental appropriations package that would mitigate the effects of extreme drought on the Colorado River.

“Bureau of Reclamation projections recently released show Lake Mead will drop below its record low of 2022 by the end of next month,” Congresswoman Titus said. “The lake is expected to drop even further to 31 feet below that level by mid-2028. We can wait no longer to address this crisis and the impacts it will have on the millions of people who rely on the Colorado River.”

Other Members of Congress signing the letter were Representatives Biggs, Stansbury, Crane, Vasquez, Stanton, Correa, Ansari, Costa, Grijalva, Hamadeh, and Gosar.

The letter to Speaker Mike Johnson, Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, and Reps. Tom Cole and Rosa DeLauro, chair and ranking member of the House Appropriations Committee, stated: “Any emergency funding package that aims to bolster our national security must recognize the immediate threat that prolonged drought and rapidly declining water levels in the Colorado River and its reservoirs pose to the millions of people whose lives and livelihoods depend on this resource. Federal investments are needed to build water supply resilience and reduce consumptive water use throughout the Colorado River Basin.”

The letter notes that in 2022 Congress provided $4 billion for drought mitigation measures. “Now is not the time to let federal support dry up. We recommend that the supplemental appropriations package include emergency funding for water infrastructure investments and upgrades in the Colorado River Basin and that significant funding is directed towards long-term planning for water reductions, conservation, and smart augmentation measures to protect the health and future of the Colorado River,” the Members said.

They also expressed support for a long-term agreement among the seven Colorado River Basin states that recognizes the natural limitations of the Colorado River. “Funding is urgently needed to limit the pain that could be felt by communities across the Basin in the near term and may smooth the path forward for post-2026 operating agreements.”

This letter was endorsed by Trout Unlimited; Hispanics Enjoying Camping, Hunting and the Outdoors (HECHO); Family Farm Alliance; National Audubon Society; Theodore Roosevelt Conservation Partnership (TRCP); Great Basin Water Network; The Nature Conservancy; American Rivers.

###
title: Rep. Titus Leads Members Urging House Leadership to Address Colorado River Drought
